giant_rat.name: giant rat
giant_rat.lore: The incisors of the rat never cease from growing, and their enamel is harder than iron, so that it must gnaw or die. When rats have grown as great as terriers, therefore, no door or barrel or boot is safe from them. They follow the smell of rations in packs down the upper corridors, and the bite of one, if it be left unwashed, turns to fever within days.

goblin.name: goblin
goblin.lore: In Normandy long ago the town of Evreux was haunted by a spirit whom the chroniclers of that age called Gobelinus, and his name has clung ever since to all the small and spiteful folk of the dark. The goblins of the dungeon are cowards alone and bold in company. They set snares and cut purses from the fallen, and they hoard the stolen coins in old boots.

alarm.line_unseen: Somewhere near, a thin voice yells.

grid_bug.name: grid bug
grid_bug.lore: The grid bug goes north or south, east or west, along paths that it alone can perceive, as though the floor were a chessboard and it a very little rook, and no one has ever seen it walk upon a diagonal. Its bite bears a spark of static that will sting and do no more. Scholars suppose that some spell went awry long ago, and that these creatures are the crumbs of it.

floating_eye.name: floating eye
floating_eye.lore: Through the corridors of the deep the floating eyes drift without a sound, and whoever meets the vast unblinking gaze of one may be held fast and helpless with terror. They have neither limbs nor mouth and live only to watch, so that the sages believe them to be the cast-off eyes of some greater being whom none has seen.

bat.name: bat
bat.lore: The giant bats that dwell in the deep caverns are far fiercer than their kindred under the sky. The cry by which they find their way in darkness has grown into a pulse of sound that troubles the inner ear and sets a traveller reeling, and whole colonies roost in the roofs of the caves to drop upon their prey.

cobra.name: cobra
cobra.lore: Upon the crowns of the pharaohs the cobra was set rearing, as a threat to all their enemies. When the living serpent rears it lifts a third of its body from the ground and swings out a row of long ribs to spread its hood, which is more than skin alone. Its venom works upon the nerves, and those that are bred in the caves give no hiss for warning.

zombie.name: zombie
zombie.lore: It was in Haiti that the zombie had its name, for there a sorcerer, who is called a bokor, would raise a corpse as a zonbi and set it to labour without any will of its own, and the horror of it lay in the stolen rest far more than in the rot. The dead of these halls walk in the same fashion, slow and patient, and the wounds of their filthy nails soon sicken.

gelatinous_cube.name: gelatinous cube
gelatinous_cube.lore: The gelatinous cube is ten feet upon a side because the corridors are so, and it fills them as a cork fills a bottle. As it slides along, it scours floor and wall and roof of all that ever lived. Bone, coin and steel hang undigested within it, so that often the first sign a traveller has of it is a skeleton floating upright in what seems to be clear air.

wraith.name: wraith
wraith.lore: Of old the Scots gave the name of wraith to the ghostly double of a man or woman, seen a little while before death. The wraith of these halls is such an omen, but there is none left for it to warn, and it has neither flesh to wound nor memory to which one might appeal. Its touch draws the warmth out of a limb and its cry draws the courage out of the heart.

mimic.name: mimic
mimic.lore: So cunning is the mimic that it can take the shape of a chest, a door or a table, even to the grain of the wood and the rust upon the hinges, and it is betrayed only because nothing in a dungeon is ever placed so conveniently. Its skin sweats a glue stronger than pitch, and the first hand that is laid upon the lid will stick fast to it.

greater_mimic.name: Greater Mimic
greater_mimic.lore: After decades of feeding this mimic grew too great for the likeness of a chest, and now it will stand as a wardrobe or a staircase, or at times as the whole end wall of a treasure vault, with the treasure painted upon it. Hammers rebound from its rubbery bulk or stick fast in it. Its tongue is barbed and envenomed, and the venom brings so pleasant a drowsiness that this is the last thing against which its prey will strive.

abyssal_mimic.name: Abyssal Mimic
abyssal_mimic.lore: A thing out of the pit crept long ago into an old mimic and made its dwelling there. Since that day it has copied furniture no more, but reaches into the mind of a traveler and becomes whatever he most longs for, be it an open door home, a lost friend or a heap of gold, and its embrace empties the will before it empties the body. Fire and prayer compel it to show its true shape.

leprechaun.name: leprechaun
leprechaun.lore: The leprechaun of the Irish tales is a solitary cobbler, who is heard tapping at a single shoe beneath a hedge, and whoever catches him may demand his crock of gold, if only he keeps both eyes upon him, for at one glance aside the little man is gone. Those who dwell below have learned that craft backward, and with a touch and a wink your purse grows lighter and he is standing elsewhere upon the floor. He has not left that floor, and if you find him the gold will come back to you.

bargain.line: {The}, cornered, holds up a fat purse: 'Let me go and it's yours!'
bargain.accept_line: {The} tosses the purse at your feet and is gone in a flash of green.
bargain.refuse_line: 'Then you'll get nothing!' {The} squares up to you.

kobold.name: kobold
kobold.lore: In the deep shafts of Germany the miners dreaded a spiteful spirit named the kobold, and they blamed him for an ore that had the look of silver, yet smelted away to nothing and poisoned those who worked it. They named that ore after him, and its metal is called cobalt still. His kindred of the dungeon delve as well as he, and line every tunnel with pits, tripwires and darts.

cave_spider.name: cave spider
cave_spider.lore: The cave spider spins a silk that is stronger than steel wire of the same thickness, and stretches it across a passage at the height of a man's face. There it will wait for days, if need be, with one leg resting upon the thread. Its venom first numbs and then slowly kills, for it likes best to eat its prey alive.

skeleton.name: skeleton
skeleton.lore: A skeleton is bare bones, held together by nothing but the will of the necromancer who raised it. It remembers how to swing a weapon and has forgotten all else. Spear point and arrow pass between its ribs and find nothing to hurt. Yet what cannot bleed may still be broken, as with a hammer or a mace, and a blessing will loose at once the knot that binds it.

fire_beetle.name: fire beetle
fire_beetle.lore: Fire beetles carry a luminous oil in glands behind their eyes and in their bellies, and beneath the open sky they kindle that light to draw their mates. In the dungeon they have learned to cast it forth in defence as a burst of flame that reaches but a little way, and the glands keep their power for days after the beetle is dead.

death_throes.line: {The}'s glands burst in a spray of fire!

orc_scout.name: orc scout
orc_scout.lore: The Beowulf poet numbered the orcneas with giants and elves among the monstrous kin of Cain, and never since has the name of orc meant anything gentle. The scout runs before the warband clad in light leather, counting the doors and marking the easy prey. For every kill he earns a tattoo, so that one who is thickly inked should be held in respect.

alarm.line_unseen: A bellow of warning, not far off.

gnoll.name: gnoll
gnoll.lore: The gnolls have the heads of spotted hyenas upon the shoulders of men, and they go armed with spears. Such jaws can crack the thigh bone of a buffalo, and such a belly digests the splinters. They build nothing and plant nothing, but follow a wounded quarry for miles until it falls and leave no scrap of it behind, and the cackle that sounds so like laughter is the pack calling the others in to the kill.

alarm.line_unseen: A whooping laugh echoes from somewhere near.

hobgoblin.name: hobgoblin
hobgoblin.lore: Among the goblin races the hobgoblins are the lords of war, as orderly and well governed as their lesser kindred are unruly. They are drilled to fight in ranks and hold strictly to the degrees of captain and soldier, so that a warband of them is an army in very truth and can hold its lands in the dungeon against monsters far greater than themselves.

alarm.line_unseen: Somewhere near, a harsh order is shouted.

ghoul.name: ghoul
ghoul.lore: Travellers among the Arabs told of the ghul, a demon of the desert that haunts graveyards and robs the dead and lures men from the road, and it prowls through the tales of the Thousand and One Nights. Those of the dungeon were men once, until they ate what no man should. Their claws bear a slime that numbs, and with any who cannot move they take their time.

dire_rat.name: dire rat
dire_rat.lore: Dire rats grow as large as great hounds and are far fiercer than the common rat. They hunt in packs and fall together upon prey larger than themselves until it is overwhelmed. Their teeth can shear away a finger, and because their habits are foul their bites will often fester.

acid_blob.name: acid blob
acid_blob.lore: An acid blob has some glimmering of wit, and it sweats a liquor so biting that metal and bone are dissolved by it alike, so that its road may be known by the trail of etched stone behind it. What is found in the body of one that has been slain is commonly much marred, though it may yet be saved.

troll.name: troll
troll.lore: The hills of Norway are full of rocks in the shape of trolls, for the old tales say that a troll who is caught by the sunrise turns to stone. Under the earth no sun rises, but a strong light is the next best thing, and he hates it bitterly. His wounds close as fast as a blade can open them and a severed arm will creep back to its owner, and there is no argument that he remembers save fire and acid.
troll.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} lair and watches you go.

orc_warrior.name: orc warrior
orc_warrior.lore: An orc warrior goes clad in whatever armor his last enemy died in, and bears an axe of whose notched edge he is very proud. It is his belief that the god of war takes account only of those who fall with their faces to the foe, and therefore he does not retreat, and fights the harder when he is cornered. Most warbands are no more than as many of his kind as one chief can feed.

dark_elf.name: dark elf
dark_elf.lore: Two peoples of the elves are named by Snorri Sturluson: the Light Elves, who are fairer than the sun, and the Dark Elves, who are blacker than pitch and live down in the earth. It is this second people that has built cold cities in the lowest tunnels, whence they send scouts and assassins upward, armed with little darts that have been dipped in a venom to stop the breath.

wight.name: wight
wight.lore: Wight meant no more than a living creature in the Old English tongue, until the burial mounds lent the word a darker meaning. The wight is a dead lord who would not be parted from his barrow or his gold and who still looks to be obeyed, and the lesser dead gather to him. His hand is colder than the grave in which he sleeps, and those whom he slays do not stay buried.

rust_monster.name: rust monster
rust_monster.lore: The rust monster has the shape of an armadillo, with a tail like a propeller and two long feelers like feathers, and all that it desires of a knight is his armor. At one brush of those feelers good steel flakes away to red dust, which the creature licks up with great contentment, and wherever such beasts have lived every hinge and nail and torch bracket is long since gone.

cave_bear.name: cave bear
cave_bear.lore: In the Ice Age the cave bears stood taller than any grizzly now living, and they wintered under the earth in such numbers that the bones of thousands lie in some of the caves, where villagers of the Middle Ages found the great skulls and took them for dragons'. In the lightless middle levels that breed has never died out, and the bear is jealous of its ground and swift for all its bulk, and makes no idle threat.

ogre.name: ogre
ogre.lore: It was Charles Perrault who gave the ogre his place among the fairy tales in 1697, and in his Puss in Boots a cat flatters one of that race into changing himself into a mouse, and devours him. So it is with all the kind, who are huge and hungry and vain but have little cleverness. An ogre keeps his larder and his loot in one heap, and may be known afar by the smell of both.

shadow.name: shadow
shadow.lore: When a wicked soul departs, the darkness that it cast will sometimes remain behind as a shadow. It lies flat along a wall or beneath a table, like any other patch of gloom, until it rises up to stand. Blades pass through it, and its touch steals the strength from an arm, and with every theft it grows the darker, but it may be hurt by torchlight and by prayer.

mummy.name: mummy
mummy.lore: For seventy days the embalmers of Egypt laboured over a king, drawing the brain out through the nose with a hook and packing the body in natron salt, and they left the heart alone in its place, because it must be weighed. All this care was meant to keep the lord of the tomb whole forever, yet linen so dry and resin so old will burn very readily.
mummy.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} tomb and watches you go.

giant_spider.name: giant spider
giant_spider.lore: As large as horses are the spiders of the deep halls, and they spin their round webs from wall to wall with every strand as thick as a bowstring. Their bite will stiffen a grown man within a few heartbeats. Whatever the spider does not eat at once it wraps and hangs up against a later day, so that in the old cocoons of a web there is often still a sword, a purse or a helmet.

ettin.name: ettin
ettin.lore: Eoten was the word for a giant among the English of old, the same that the Norse spoke as jotunn, and from it the ettin has his name. His two heads have never agreed in anything, and they quarrel over supper, over the road and over whose turn it is to sleep. Yet each commands one arm and one club, and one or the other of them is always awake.

manticore.name: manticore
manticore.lore: From the court of Persia the Greek physician Ctesias brought home the tale of the manticore, whose name in the Persian tongue means man-eater. It has a lion's body, red of hue, with the face of a man and three rows of teeth, and from its scorpion's tail it shoots spines as if they were arrows. It is said to leave nothing of those it slays, not so much as a bone, and so it is that the missing are never found.

specter.name: specter
specter.lore: All that a specter was in life has burned away long since, and nothing is left of it but hunger. It has neither face nor name nor any grudge to remember, and it drifts through the halls of stone as silent as a fog. A great cold goes before it, so that the breath of the living turns to mist, and that chill is all the warning they are given before its touch drains the life from whatever it passes through.

basilisk.name: basilisk
basilisk.lore: Pliny of old named the basilisk the king of serpents, though it was no longer than a man's forearm and had but a white mark for its crown. So venomous was it that its glance killed and its breath split the rocks. Yet a weasel could slay it, he said, and later writers swore by the crowing of a rooster. Its den may be known by the statues that stand about it, which no sculptor ever carved.

chimera.name: chimera
chimera.lore: Homer sang of the Chimera, who was a lion before, a serpent behind and a goat in the midst, and who breathed out fire. She burned the fields of Lycia until Bellerophon rode the winged horse Pegasus against her and thrust a spear tipped with lead into her throat, where her own flame melted it and choked her. Whoever meets with one of her kind must keep watch upon three heads at once.

minotaur.name: minotaur
minotaur.lore: Queen Pasiphae of Crete bore a son with the head of a bull, and King Minos, to hide the shame of it, bade Daedalus build the Labyrinth at Knossos. Seven youths and seven maidens of Athens were sent there for his meat, until Theseus went in with a sword and with Ariadne's ball of thread. The bull-men of the dungeon are made in his likeness, and in no maze do they ever lose their way.

frost_crawler.name: frost crawler
frost_crawler.lore: From the frozen levels far below, where water never thaws, the frost crawler comes climbing, a centipede as long as a wagon with armour plates that are white with rime. The slime upon its jaws is colder than ice itself and freezes flesh at a touch. Old delvers know by the draught when they draw near its lair, for a corridor will of a sudden breathe upon them like winter.

medusa.name: medusa
medusa.lore: Of the three Gorgon sisters Medusa alone was mortal. Living serpents grew upon her head in place of hair, and her face turned all who beheld it to stone, until Perseus came walking backward, watching her image in the polished shield that Athena had lent him, and took her head at a single stroke. She has daughters yet in the darkness, who set out their statues with great care and wait behind them for whoever may come.

vampire_spawn.name: vampire spawn
vampire_spawn.lore: As a lord takes servants into his house, so a vampire makes his spawn, in haste and with no thought for what shall become of them. The spawn is strong and hungry and bound to obey the one who drained him, though he has not yet the art of turning to mist or of calling the wolves. He can but hunt where he is sent, and hope that his master will be destroyed before he is.

fire_elemental.name: fire elemental
fire_elemental.lore: Each of the four elements has a people of its own, as the physician Paracelsus taught, and salamanders was his name for the people of fire. Of that race is this pillar of living flame, and there is no body within it. Blades stir it and do it little harm, and whatever it leans upon is set alight, but a hard frost will dim it until it is no more than embers.

earth_elemental.name: earth elemental
earth_elemental.lore: The spirits of earth, as Paracelsus wrote, are as much at home in rock as fishes are in water. When an earth elemental rises to its feet, it is as though the stone of a whole hill had resolved to stand upright and walk, and any edge will chip upon it, yet acid will eat it away as the rain eats limestone.

storm_elemental.name: storm elemental
storm_elemental.lore: A storm elemental is a thundercloud as great as a room, which its own winds have driven into a rough shape. The lightning within it walks to and fro seeking a way out, and will find no better road all day than a knight in full plate, while his sword and spear can wound it no more than they can wound the weather.

lich_apprentice.name: lich apprentice
lich_apprentice.lore: He who sets out upon the road to lichdom may not turn back. This mage has given up sleep and warmth and most of the beating of his heart, though he has not yet hidden his soul away, and he serves an older lich to earn the last secret of the rite. That secret will never be given him, for his master has no intention of raising up a rival.

mind_flayer.name: mind flayer
mind_flayer.lore: Robed like a scholar, with a nest of tentacles where a mouth should be, the mind flayer goes seeking after thinking creatures, for it will eat nothing but their brains. Before it feeds it sends forth a blast of thought that makes no sound, and the strongest man is left unsure of his own name. Among delvers there is talk of a whole city of these creatures, lying somewhere far below.

vampire.name: vampire
vampire.lore: In the 1720s and 1730s the surgeons of the Austrian army who were posted among the villages of Serbia sent home sober reports of peasants who dug up their dead and staked them, and soon the word vampire passed into English. The creature itself is far older, and has learned patience. He drinks the life of men and bends weak minds with a look, but he fears the stake, the flame and the sign of the Cross.

death_knight.name: death knight
death_knight.lore: Every oath of a paladin the death knight swore in his lifetime, and every one he broke, so that when he died the grave would not receive him. He has kept all his skill at arms and none of his mercy, and for his sentence he must bear a sword that he can never lay down. There are few men who can meet that empty helm face to face and not turn and run.

bone_golem.name: bone golem
bone_golem.lore: A necromancer gathered the bones of many creatures, the ribs of an ox, the skull of a bear and the arms of a dozen men, and built of them this servant. No ghost dwells in it, and it knows nothing but its last command. Swords and spears slide through the gaps and the bones knit together behind them, but a heavy mace will scatter them faster than they can gather.

greater_demon.name: greater demon
greater_demon.lore: John beheld in his Revelation how the tail of the dragon swept a third of the stars from heaven, and the Church has long read those stars as the angels who fell with him. A greater demon is of that company, and with a clear mind, such as no beast or madman has, it chose to fall. It burns and is never consumed, it hates all that is made, and it cannot endure a holy thing.

young_dragon.name: young dragon
young_dragon.lore: At Silene in Libya, as the Golden Legend tells, a dragon poisoned all the country round until the townsfolk fed it their sheep and afterward their children, and then Saint George rode against it and brought it down with his lance. A young dragon stands at the beginning of such a tale, for its hoard is small and its appetite is great, and it has only lately learned to aim its fire.
young_dragon.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} hoard and watches you go.

beholder.name: beholder
beholder.lore: Delvers give the name of beholder to a floating globe of flesh with one great eye in its midst, a mouth full of fangs and a crown of lesser eyes on stalks. Each of these casts a curse of its own, one to numb, one to blind and one to unmake. It trusts no living thing, and another beholder least of all, and it keeps all who have ever visited it as ornaments for its lair.

vampire_lord.name: vampire lord
vampire_lord.lore: When Bram Stoker told of his Count he gave him the name of a true prince, Vlad Dracula of Wallachia, and a castle full of servants who went in fear of him. Such a ruler is the vampire lord. A thousand years of feeding have made him rich and courteous and very hard to slay, and he holds a whole level of the dungeon for his estate, where all who come are treated as guests until the hour of supper, when he feeds upon them.

lich.name: lich
lich.lore: Lich was the Old English word for a corpse, and many a churchyard has still its lychgate, where the coffin rests before burial. But this is a corpse that chose its own burial, for a wizard who feared death cut out his soul and locked it in a vessel. While that vessel lasts his body cannot be ended, and all that remains within it is intellect, from which the last of pity has departed.

spells.name: Grave-Hold
spells.cast: {The} speaks one cold word, and your limbs lock.

adult_dragon.name: adult dragon
adult_dragon.lore: Three hundred years the dragon of Beowulf slept upon its gold, until a runaway slave crept into the barrow and stole a single cup. It woke and counted and knew that it had been robbed, and that same night it burned the hall of the king. So is it with every dragon come to full growth, for it knows each coin of its hoard, and exactly how each one was taken.
adult_dragon.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} hoard and watches you go.

iron_golem.name: iron golem
iron_golem.lore: Hephaestus forged Talos, a man of bronze, to be warden of Crete, and three times a day he ran about the island, hurling boulders at strange ships, until the sorceress Medea drew the single nail that sealed his one vein. Upon the same pattern, but in a cheaper metal, the iron golem was made. It neither tires nor takes hurt from fire, and it is faithful yet to a master long since dead.

greater_lich.name: greater lich
greater_lich.lore: The tale-tellers of Russia say that Koschei the Deathless hid his death in a needle, the needle in an egg, the egg in a duck, the duck in a hare, and the hare in an iron chest beneath an oak on a distant island. A greater lich has had centuries to hide his own more cunningly, and so well has he done it that he no longer troubles to guard his body at all.

spells.name: Grave-Hold
spells.cast: {The} speaks one cold word, and your limbs lock.

arch_demon.name: arch demon
arch_demon.lore: In the year 1589 the bishop Peter Binsfeld assigned a prince of Hell to each of the seven deadly sins, with Lucifer for pride, Mammon for greed, Asmodeus for lust, and the others after them. An arch demon holds such rank as theirs. Legions march at its bidding and its designs are laid by centuries, and it burns still with the fire into which it was thrown, and it can abide neither holiness nor bitter cold.

ancient_dragon.name: ancient dragon
ancient_dragon.lore: There is a proverb in Old English that the dragon belongs in the barrow, old and wise, proud of its treasures. An ancient dragon has outlived the very kingdoms whose crowns it sleeps on. Ages ago its fire went out and something colder took the place of it, so that those who feel the breath of such a wyrm feel the frost of a grave that has never been opened.

aura.line: The dread of {the} falls on you like a shadow. You turn to run!

ancient_lich.name: ancient lich
ancient_lich.lore: No one now living remembers the name of this wizard, and he has himself forgotten it. Through thousands of years of study he has won the answers to questions that no one else would know how to ask, and long ago he solved the riddles of frost and of edge and point. Fire and the hammer may hurt him yet, but what is holy troubles him most, since holiness was never a thing to be mastered by knowledge.

death_lord.name: death lord
death_lord.lore: John saw in his vision a pale horse, and the name of its rider was Death, and Hell followed after him. In that following rides the death lord, who was once a conqueror and now bears some part of the authority of the grave itself. For miles about him every lesser corpse turns its face toward him as he goes by, and his glance alone will take the strength from the living.

chaos_spawn.name: chaos spawn
chaos_spawn.lore: First of all things, as Hesiod sang, came Chaos, the yawning gap that was before earth or sky. A chaos spawn is a shred of that gap which has strayed into a world of laws and resents every one of them. It has claws at one moment and wings at the next, so that whoever looks on it too long grows troubled in his wits, and whoever is touched by it fares worse.

soul_eater.name: soul eater
soul_eater.lore: Out of the borderland beside death comes the soul eater, a hunger with a shape drawn loosely about it, to feed upon the spark that makes of a body a person. It can scent a strong soul through a mile of rock, and the brave men who venture deepest smell sweetest to it of all. When it has finished with them, nothing remains of them for which their friends might pray.

orc_shaman.name: orc shaman
orc_shaman.lore: In all the warband the shaman alone carries no axe, and he is the only orc with whom the chief is careful. He paints his skin with ash and old blood and cries to the war-god of the tribe to lay a curse upon its enemies, and when he takes up the chant the marks on his arms begin to glow like coals in a draught.

spells.name: Blood Dread
spells.cast: {The} howls the name of {his} god at you.

giant_centipede.name: giant centipede
giant_centipede.lore: A centipede bites with the foremost pair of its legs, which have become hollow fangs that fold beneath the head and pump venom. In the jungles of the New World the largest of the race hangs from the roofs of caves and plucks bats out of the air. The breed of the dungeon has grown as long as a man, and it hunts in the very same manner.

skeletal_archer.name: skeletal archer
skeletal_archer.lore: Bowmen of great skill they were while they lived, and the necromancy that raised their bones has preserved the memory of that craft, so that skeletal archers draw and loose as evenly as engines. They have no love of close fighting, but stand far off and riddle their quarry with arrows, and then withdraw behind those of their company who fight hand to hand.

cave_toad.name: cave toad
cave_toad.lore: Behind the eyes of every toad lie two swollen glands that sweat a milky poison when they are squeezed, and a dog that mouths one will foam and stagger. By the black pools under the earth lives a cave toad that is itself as big as a hound, and it has learned to spit. Delvers have been hungry enough to cook one, and they report that for a week afterward they saw strange colours.

brigand.name: brigand
brigand.lore: Old soldiers, felons who have escaped their prisons and folk who are merely desperate have taken to robbery in the dungeon, and men call them brigands. They have what the monsters lack, for they were trained to arms and are equipped for battle. Some bands hold whole reaches of the dungeon as their own land, and of all who pass through it they exact a toll, or else they slay them.

shadow_hound.name: shadow hound
shadow_hound.lore: On the fourth of August 1577, while a great storm raged, a black dog burst into the church at Bungay in Suffolk and left two of the congregation dead at their prayers, and in East Anglia he is remembered as Black Shuck. The shadow hounds of the dungeon are of his kindred, cold and but half present, and they make no sound until the howl that causes a man to feel utterly alone.

flesh_golem.name: flesh golem
flesh_golem.lore: Mary Shelley told in 1818 how Victor Frankenstein stitched a man together from the dead and gave him life, and afterward fled in horror from what he had made. The artificers of the dungeon repeat both the work and the mistake. A flesh golem is obedient until some buried scrap of memory wakens in it, and then it falls to grieving, and out of its grief it passes into rage.

harpy.name: harpy
harpy.lore: Harpy signifies snatcher, and the harpies earned that name well, for whenever a table was laid before the blind king Phineus they swooped down to seize the food and foul what they left, until the winged sons of the North Wind, who sailed with Jason, chased them away. A harpy has the face of a woman and the body of a vulture, and with her voice she draws the unwary close.

necromancer_apprentice.name: necromancer apprentice
necromancer_apprentice.lore: When King Saul was forsaken and afraid he went in disguise to the witch of Endor, and she called up for him the dead prophet Samuel, who told him that he would die the next day. Such is necromancy, which asks of the dead what God has withheld. The apprentice has learned enough of it to raise a corpse, but he has not yet learned enough to be afraid of it.

spells.name: Grave Ward
spells.cast: {The}'s chant ends: grave-dust rises about {him} and hangs in the air.

stymphalian_bird.name: Stymphalian Bird
stymphalian_bird.lore: Sacred to Ares were the birds of Lake Stymphalia, whose beaks and claws were bronze and whose feathers flew from them like arrows, until Heracles put them to flight with the bronze krotala of Hephaestus. Now they roost in high crevices of these dungeons and dive upon the unwary who pass below.

satyr_warrior.name: Satyr Warrior
satyr_warrior.lore: The satyrs, those unruly followers of Dionysus who are half goat, care more for wine and revel than for war. One who bears arms has been cast out by his band, and exile has made him bitter and violent. He fights with a rude club, and with the butting of his horned head he leaves an enemy dazed and bewildered.

empusa.name: Empusa
empusa.lore: At the crossroads, where Hecate sent them to devour travellers, the Empusai lay in wait in borrowed shapes. One would seem a beautiful woman, or a dog or a cow, until she showed her true form, which has one leg of bronze and one of an ass. By these fair illusions they beguile their victims and drain away the life that is in them.

hecate_hound.name: Hecate's Hound
hecate_hound.lore: Hecate, the goddess of magic and of crossroads, keeps a pack of phantom hounds to walk the marches between the living world and the underworld. Their mournful howling will shatter the thought of any mortal and may drive him to madness, and they are met with most often where the way leads from one depth to another, near the stairwells of the dungeon.

lamia.name: Lamia
lamia.lore: Zeus loved Lamia, who was queen of Libya, and for that cause Hera in her jealousy destroyed the children of the queen. Grief then so changed her that she became a stealer of the children of others, and Zeus, that she might rest from what she saw, gave her the power to take out her own eyes. She is a woman above and a serpent below, and whoever touches her finds that she is cold.
lamia.omen: Somewhere close, a woman is singing a lullaby to no one.

gorgon_warrior.name: Gorgon Warrior
gorgon_warrior.lore: Edward Topsell in his bestiary of 1607 gave the name of Gorgon to a scaled beast of Africa, shaped like a bull, whose breath killed all that it touched. He had it from Pliny's catoblepas, which had so heavy a head that it hung always toward the ground. Smiths of the dungeon have since cast that beast in bronze and set it on guard, and they gave it the deadly breath as well.

cyclops.name: Cyclops
cyclops.lore: Polyphemus the son of Poseidon shut Odysseus and his men within his cave and ate them two at a time, until that crafty captain made him drunk, told him that his name was Nobody, and put out his single eye with a stake sharpened and hardened in the fire. The giant screamed that Nobody was hurting him, and so his neighbours went back to their beds. Since that night every Cyclops has been careful to guard his one eye.
cyclops.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} cave and watches you go.

sphinx.name: Sphinx
sphinx.lore: Before the gates of Thebes the Sphinx lay crouched, and she devoured all who could not answer her riddle: what walks on four legs at dawn, two at noon, three at dusk? Oedipus alone answered rightly, and she threw herself down from her rock. In the dungeon she sits at the crossroads to guard the passage, and she waits no longer for answers, but hurls her riddle to confound the mind and then falls upon whoever comes near.

griffin.name: Griffin
griffin.lore: Herodotus heard tell that in the far north the griffins guard the gold of the mountains, and that a one-eyed people named the Arimaspians steal it from them. The ancients saw in this beast, eagle before and lion behind, the image of a watchman who cannot be bribed. In after days kings drank from cups that were called griffin claws, trusting that they would darken if poison were poured in them.

pegasus.name: Maddened Pegasus
pegasus.lore: From the blood of Medusa, when Perseus had struck her down, sprang Pegasus the divine winged horse, dear to the Muses and a bearer of the thunder. The Pegasi are gentle by nature when a hero draws near, but those that the dungeon has corrupted were driven mad by their confinement under the earth, and they will charge at whatever moves.

hydra.name: Lernaean Hydra
hydra.lore: Nine heads had the Hydra of Lerna, and for each that Heracles struck off two grew back, until his nephew Iolaus took a burning brand and seared every stump before it could sprout. The last head was immortal, and the hero buried it beneath a rock. Afterward he dipped his arrows in the blood of the creature, and of all the wounds those arrows made there was none that ever healed.

cerberus.name: Cerberus
cerberus.lore: At the threshold of the underworld the three-headed hound of Hades kept watch, and he let the dead go in and suffered none to come out. Heracles subdued him by sheer strength for his twelfth labour, and Orpheus charmed all three heads to sleep with the music of his lyre. Now in the deepest dungeon he stands an eternal guardian, and his serpent-barbed tail lashes at all who would go by.

scylla.name: Scylla
scylla.lore: Scylla was a nymph of the sea until the witch Circe, who was jealous over the sea god Glaucus, poisoned the pool in which she bathed. She rose out of it with twelve dangling legs and six long necks, and on each a head with three rows of teeth. From her cave above the strait she reached down as Odysseus sailed beneath, and she took six of his best men at once, one for every mouth.

charybdis_spawn.name: Charybdis Spawn
charybdis_spawn.lore: Charybdis, as some tell, was a daughter of Poseidon whom Zeus smote with his thunderbolt and cast into the sea, and there she became the great whirlpool that three times daily swallows the waters and three times gives them up again. Her spawn are lesser whirlpools with life in them, which cling to the walls of the dungeon and drag all creatures toward the maw at their centre.

titanspawn.name: Titanspawn
titanspawn.lore: Ten years Zeus and his brothers fought against the Titans, and the vanquished they cast into Tartarus, as far below the earth as the earth is below the sky, behind gates of bronze. Yet something of them has seeped upward since that war, and thence come the titanspawn, rough shapes of men in bedrock, moved by an ancient anger that they do not understand.

frost_giant.name: Frost Giant
frost_giant.lore: The hrimthursar, as the Norse named the rime giants, are all descended from Ymir, who took shape where the ice of Niflheim met the heat of the south. Odin and his brothers slew that first giant and built the world from his body, making the sea of his blood and the sky of his skull. His children have never forgiven the deed, and they bide in the cold until Ragnarok shall come.

fire_giant.name: Fire Giant
fire_giant.lore: Upon the border of Muspelheim stands Surtr, with a sword in his hand that outshines the sun. At Ragnarok he will ride north with the sons of Muspell, and the rainbow bridge will break beneath them, and he will cut down the god Freyr and set the world alight. The fire giants of the deep forges are his people, and they keep their blades hot against the coming of that day.

valkyrie_shade.name: Valkyrie Shade
valkyrie_shade.lore: Over the fields of battle rode the valkyries, Odin's choosers of the slain, to carry the bravest of the fallen to Valhalla. One who chose amiss, or fell herself and lost the favour of the god, became a valkyrie shade. She knows no labour but the old one, and so she marks a soul with her spear and strives still to carry it away, though the only road left to her now leads downward.

fenrir_pup.name: Fenrir's Pup
fenrir_pup.lore: Fenrir the wolf was reared among the gods until they dared trust his strength no longer, and would bind him with Gleipnir, a ribbon made of such impossible things as the sound of a cat's footfall. He allowed it only while the god Tyr held a hand between his jaws in pledge, and when the bond held fast Tyr lost that hand. The whelps of Fenrir bite as their father bit, and will not let go their hold.

jormungandr_spawn.name: Jörmungandr Spawn
jormungandr_spawn.lore: Into the sea Odin threw the serpent Jormungandr, and there it grew until it circled the world and took its own tail in its teeth. Thor once hooked it with the head of an ox for bait, but the giant Hymir in his terror cut the line. When Ragnarok comes Thor will kill it, and walk nine steps, and die of its venom, and that same venom is in the fangs of all its young.

draugr.name: Draugr
draugr.lore: When a dead man of the North would not lie still in his mound he became a draugr, swollen to a giant's size, who guarded the goods of his grave and rode by night upon the roofs of the farms. Grettir the Strong, as his saga tells, wrestled the draugr Glam and won, but Glam cursed him as he perished, and for the rest of his life that hero was afraid of the dark.

aura.line: {The}'s eyes catch the light, and you cannot bear to look. You turn to run!

draugr.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} mound and watches you go.

einherjar_ghost.name: Einherjar Ghost
einherjar_ghost.lore: In Valhalla the chosen dead, who are called einherjar, arm themselves each morning and cut one another down in the courtyard, and each evening they rise whole and feast upon the boar Saehrimnir, who is whole again on the morrow. This warrior never came to that hall. He fights with all the skill of a veteran, and with the bitterness of one whose name was left out of the roll.

nidhogg_brood.name: Níðhöggr Brood
nidhogg_brood.lore: At the foot of Yggdrasil lies the great dragon Níðhöggr, who feeds on corpses and gnaws forever at the World Tree from below. The brood of that dragon are lesser wyrms that have their parent's nature in them and are sick with the same rot of worlds. They are found in the deepest passages, where they carry on, slowly and without rest, the work of ruining the foundations of the world.

hugin_raven.name: Huginn Raven
hugin_raven.lore: Odin keeps two ravens, Huginn and Muninn, which is to say Thought and Memory, and at dawn he sends them out to fly over all the world. They return at breakfast with their tidings, but he has confessed that he fears for Thought, and the more for Memory. The ravens of the dungeon are of that lineage, and they watch and remember, and when they strike they go for the eyes.

alarm.line: {The} croaks and wheels away to tell!

lindworm.name: Lindworm
lindworm.lore: A queen in the Danish tale bore a dragon without wings, who was named King Lindworm and who devoured each of his brides. At last a clever girl came to the wedding in ten shifts and bade him shed a skin for every one that she took off, until the last skin fell and a prince stood before her. The lindworms of the flooded tunnels have no such prince within them to be set free.

sheds_skin.line: The Lindworm sheds a skin, and its wounds come away with it!

lindworm.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} lair and watches you go.

berserker_spirit.name: Berserker Spirit
berserker_spirit.lore: The berserkers, the bear-shirts of the North, fought in a howling trance, and some chessmen carved in the twelfth century show them yet, biting the rims of their shields. King Harald Fairhair set such men in the prow of his ship. In this spirit the trance has outlived the man, so that it never tires and never parries, and it is defenceless against cold and against prayer, having no skin any longer to keep either of them out.

light_elf_hostile.name: Corrupted Light Elf
light_elf_hostile.lore: Fairer than the sun to look upon are the Light Elves of Alfheim, as Snorri wrote, but a sourness has entered into these. The brightness that once blessed has become a burning, and they loose it upon whatever casts a shadow, caring nothing whether it be friend or stranger. For all their glory they are fey still, and cold iron hurts them as it hurts all their kind.

sea_serpent_norse.name: Norse Sea Serpent
sea_serpent_norse.lore: Olaus Magnus, a churchman of Sweden, wrote in 1555 of a serpent two hundred feet long that had its home in the sea caves near Bergen and came forth on summer nights to pluck sailors from the decks of their ships. Others of its kind have followed the cold rivers down beneath the earth, and they lie coiled in drowned chambers where the water about them never quite thaws.

anubis_guardian.name: Anubis Guardian
anubis_guardian.lore: Jackal-headed Anubis is the god of embalmers, who leads the dead into the Hall of Two Truths and steadies the scales while the heart is weighed against the feather of Maat. The builders of the tombs set his likeness beside the door in black stone, and some of those images hold their post still. They are swift to judge a trespasser, and beneath their gaze a guilty heart will for a moment cease to beat.
anubis_guardian.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} tomb and watches you go.

ra_serpent.name: Ra's Serpent
ra_serpent.lore: Upon the crown of Pharaoh reared a cobra, the uraeus, which the Egyptians held to be the fiery Eye of Ra, spitting flame at the enemies of the king. Each night, as the boat of the sun made its voyage through the underworld, serpents of that kind defended Ra against Apep, the snake of chaos. These golden guardians have the same fire in their fangs, and it is pain to the eyes to look on them.

scarab_swarm.name: Scarab Swarm
scarab_swarm.lore: The Egyptians watched the dung beetle roll its ball across the sand and saw in it the god Khepri pushing the sun across the sky, so they carved the scarab on their seals and laid it over the hearts of their dead. But the curses of the tombs have made the sacred beetle hungry. One alone is a small matter, yet ten thousand will pour together from a crack in the wall like black water.

sphinx_guardian.name: Egyptian Sphinx
sphinx_guardian.lore: A young prince fell asleep in the shade of the Great Sphinx at Giza, and it promised him the throne if he would clear away the sand that buried it. He did so and reigned as Thutmose IV, as a stone slab between its paws declares. The sphinxes of Egypt have no riddles to ask, for their charge is to guard the rest of a king, and their roar is like the blaze of the sun at noon.
sphinx_guardian.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} road and watches you go.

ammit_spawn.name: Ammit Spawn
ammit_spawn.lore: Beside the scales in the Hall of Two Truths crouches Ammit, in whom the three man-eaters of the Nile are made one, for she has the crocodile's head, the lion's forequarters and the hindquarters of the hippopotamus. When a heart outweighs the feather of Maat she devours it, and that soul dies a second and final death. Her spawn are as hungry, and they will not wait to hear the verdict.

sobek_warrior.name: Sobek Warrior
sobek_warrior.lore: At Crocodilopolis in the Faiyum men worshipped Sobek, the crocodile god of the Nile, and his priests kept a living crocodile named Petsuchos, hung it with gold and fed it by hand. The soldiers of his temple wear the head of that beast and bear the khopesh, curved like a sickle. They learned war from the river, and so they seize a man and drag him down, and roll until his struggling ceases.

ba_spirit.name: Ba Spirit
ba_spirit.lore: The ba was drawn in Egypt as a bird with a human head, and it was that part of a person which might fly from the tomb by day but must return to the body at nightfall. Were the name erased or the burial spoiled, it had nowhere to roost. These are the lost ones, who flutter starving through the dark and drink the life of any who still possess a name.

khepri_beetle.name: Khepri Beetle
khepri_beetle.lore: Each dawn, as Egyptians believed, the beetle-headed Khepri pushes the sun over the horizon, even as the scarab rolls its ball of dung across the sand. In the depths his sacred beetles have grown to the size of hounds, and each carries a little daylight stored beneath the cases of its wings, which it will loose in a blinding flash when it is cornered.

thoth_construct.name: Thoth Construct
thoth_construct.lore: Thoth of the ibis head invented writing and had the keeping of the calendar, and he stood beside the scales in the Hall of Two Truths to record each verdict. His guardians are carven stone, covered with hieroglyphs that crawl and change their order, and every sign is a working spell. They punish any thief of sacred writings. Spells slide away from that script, but the hammer of a mason will do them far more harm.

duat_shade.name: Duat Shade
duat_shade.lore: For twelve hours each night the barque of Ra sailed the Duat, the underworld of Egypt, and there every dead soul stood before the scales while Anubis weighed the heart against the feather of Ma'at, and Ammit devoured the hearts that failed. These shades are a thinner remnant still, souls that came apart in the dark water, and they drift like smoke and cling to the living to borrow substance from them.

desert_wraith.name: Desert Wraith
desert_wraith.lore: The Egyptians named the fertile bank of the Nile the Black Land, and the waste beyond it the Red Land, which was the realm of Set, the lord of storms and disorder. Many a traveller died there without tomb or rite, and the sun and wind dried him to a husk. The spirits of such men never found the road to the Duat, and now they ride upon the hot wind and steal the water from living flesh.

banshee.name: Banshee
banshee.lore: She is the bean sidhe, 'woman of the fairy mound', who keens outside the house when death draws near to one of the old Irish families. Some who saw her spoke of a crone cloaked in grey, others of a pale girl drawing a silver comb through her long hair. Above ground her cry does no more than foretell a death, but in these halls the cry itself has power to slay.

fomorian.name: Fomorian
fomorian.lore: Out of the sea came the Fomorians to oppress Ireland, until the Tuatha De Danann broke their power at the Second Battle of Mag Tuired. Their champion was Balor, who had one eye whose lid four men must lift, and all that it looked upon died, until his own grandson Lugh drove a sling stone through that eye and out at the back of his skull. The lesser Fomorians have that evil glare still, though in a weaker measure.

changeling.name: Changeling
changeling.lore: It was the belief of country folk throughout Britain and Ireland that fairies would steal a healthy babe and leave one of their own in the cradle, a thin and wailing thing with old eyes and an appetite that had no bottom, and the common defence was to lay iron tongs across the cradle. The changelings of these depths have grown up. Each goes in a borrowed face until it is struck, and then the glamour slips away and something half-finished looks out.

each_uisce.name: Each Uisce
each_uisce.lore: Deadlier than its cousin the kelpie is the each uisge of the Highland sea lochs. It waits by the shore as a fine horse or a handsome stranger, and the moment a rider has mounted, its hide turns sticky and it gallops with him into deep water. There it eats all of him except the liver, which floats ashore the next morning. In the flooded passages it stands waiting still, sleek and patient, for someone to come near.

cath_palug.name: Cath Palug
cath_palug.lore: Henwen the sow, as the Welsh Triads say, bore a kitten on the coast of Arfon, and the swineherd flung it into the Menai Strait. But it swam to Anglesey, and the sons of Palug raised it there to their own ruin. An old poem counts nine score warriors as its food before Cai came against it with his polished shield. It is very swift, and has far more cunning than should ever be found in a cat.

fionn_hound.name: Fionn's Hound
fionn_hound.lore: Bran and Sceolang, best loved of all the hounds of Fionn mac Cumhaill, were his own cousins, for a jealous fairy woman had changed his aunt Tuiren into a hound and she bore them while she wore that shape. They kept human wits behind the eyes of dogs. The hounds of their blood stand as tall as a man's shoulder, and when one has found a scent it will follow without rest.

puca.name: Púca
puca.lore: Farmers in Ireland left the last of the harvest standing as the Púca's share. It comes as a sleek black horse with eyes like coals, or as a goat, a hare or a small dark man, and it offers a weary traveller a ride, only to tear with him across bog and bramble all night and tip him into a ditch at dawn. Should it flee from anyone, it flees only because it wishes to be chased.

dullahan_spawn.name: Dullahan Spawn
dullahan_spawn.lore: Along the back roads of Ireland by night rides the Dullahan on a black horse, holding his own head high in one hand, and in the other a whip made from a human spine. Where he draws rein he speaks a name, and the one so named dies. He lashes at the eyes of all who watch him, and he cannot bear the sight of gold. His lesser riders carry each a name, and they are seeking still for the one to whom it belongs.

aura.line: To look on {the} is to see your own death coming. You turn to run!

sluagh.name: Sluagh
sluagh.lore: The unforgiven dead, turned away by Heaven and earth alike, make up the host that Highland and Irish folk call the Sluagh. It flies in from the west like a flock of dark birds, and families would shut the west windows of a sickroom lest it snatch the soul of the dying. But below ground there are no windows to keep such a host out, and it descends in a cloud to rend whatever walks there.

pazuzu_spawn.name: Pazuzu Spawn
pazuzu_spawn.lore: Pazuzu was king of the wind demons, and he brought upon Assyria the hot wind of the southwest with its fever and its locusts. He had the snarling face of a dog, four wings, an eagle's talons and a scorpion's tail. Yet mothers hung his bronze head above the cradle, for he hated the demoness Lamashtu who stole children, and he would drive her off. His spawn have inherited the wings and the fever, but none of the service for which he was welcomed.

death_throes.line: {The} bursts in a hot wind of plague!

lahamu.name: Lahamu
lahamu.lore: With the mingling of Apsu the sweet water and Tiamat the salt sea begins Enuma Elish, the Babylonian tale of creation. Lahmu and Lahamu were their firstborn, and some scholars read those names as 'the muddy ones', the silt where river and ocean meet. The creature that wears her name in these depths is a shifting bulk of wet clay and coils, never the same shape twice, with the bearing of something older than all that walks on legs.

anzu_bird.name: Anzu Bird
anzu_bird.lore: Lion-headed Anzu, the eagle of Sumer, guarded the doorway of Enlil until the day when he watched the god at his bath and stole the Tablet of Destinies, which gives to its holder the command of fate. With it he bade arrows in their flight turn back into reed and feather. But Ninurta sheared away his wings in a storm and shot him down among the mountains, and that storm is now the inheritance of all his brood.

ugallu_demon.name: Ugallu Demon
ugallu_demon.lore: Ugallu means 'Big Weather Beast', and the name is borne by a demon with a lion's head upon a man's body, which stands on a bird's talons with a dagger raised in one fist. The first of them was one of the eleven monsters that Tiamat made to fight the younger gods, and when Marduk had won, Assyrian kings carved the Ugallu beside palace doorways to frighten sickness away. These have nothing left to guard, though they love a storm as well as ever they did.

kusarikku.name: Kusarikku
kusarikku.lore: The Bull-Man of Mesopotamia, who is called Kusarikku, has the face, arms and chest of a man above and the horns and hindquarters of a bull below. Tiamat counted him among her eleven monsters, and after her defeat he entered the service of Shamash the sun god, so that sculptors set his image at doorways with the gateposts in his grasp. Those of his race who are penned here have no gate left to guard, and they gore whatever comes through.

beholder_spawn.name: Beholder Spawn
beholder_spawn.lore: Afloat at the height of a man's head drifts the young of the beholder, a ball of flesh the size of a shield, with a toothy mouth and a few stunted eyestalks for a crown. Each small eye sends out its own ill, and one will lock the limbs while another scatters thought. It never blinks, and it deems all other life a blemish, but a spear in the great eye at its centre will make an end of it.

mind_flayer_thrall.name: Mind Flayer Thrall
mind_flayer_thrall.lore: Some were scholars once and some were soldiers, before a tentacled master reached into their heads and left nothing there but obedience. A thrall of the mind flayers walks with the care of one asleep, and he never speaks. When he turns his blank eyes upon an intruder the will of his master pours through him like a shout within the skull, and whatever lies behind that stare begins to feed upon the victim's strength.

aboleth_lesser.name: Lesser Aboleth
aboleth_lesser.lore: The aboleths claim to remember all that their forebears saw, back to a sea older than any shore. Each is a fish as long as a longship, with three red eyes set one above another down its brow and four tentacles that trail slime. This one is young as they reckon years. Its slime softens the skin of a victim until he can breathe only water, and those whom it has so changed it keeps for its servants.

gibbering_mouther.name: Gibbering Mouther
gibbering_mouther.lore: Covered over with eyes, and with mouths that open and close wherever they please, the gibbering mouther pours its heap of soft flesh across the floor. All the mouths talk at once, each in a different voice and none with any meaning, until the noise crowds out thought and brave men have been found standing still and muttering along. So they stand until the mouths have reached their boots and every one begins to bite.

intellect_devourer.name: Intellect Devourer
intellect_devourer.lore: Mind flayers breed for their hunting a creature that is no more than a naked brain, as big as a hound, which trots upon four clawed legs. It feeds on the mind of a sleeper, then climbs into the empty skull and walks the body back among his friends. For this reason old delvers, when a companion has fallen silent, will put to him a question that he alone could answer.

nothic.name: Nothic
nothic.lore: There was a wizard whose greed for secrets led him to read one book too many, and the curse that answers such greed bent his back, lengthened his claws and melted his face into a single huge eye. He remembers nothing of himself, and desires every secret that belongs to another. So the nothic crouches giggling in corners and watches, and flesh withers where that stare has rested too long.

grell.name: Grell
grell.lore: Eyeless and silent the grell hangs near the ceiling, a bare grey brain as wide as a wagon wheel, with a parrot's beak and ten long tentacles beneath it. It knows its prey by the trembling of the air and by the faint spark within all living things, which may be the reason that lightning does not trouble it. When someone passes below it drops and stings him limp, and bears its meal upward into the dark.

cloaker.name: Cloaker
cloaker.lore: Until the moment that it strikes, there is no telling the cloaker from a black cloak. In truth it is a creature like the manta, which wraps itself about its prey to smother and blind him, and its haunting moan brings unease upon all who hear it. More than one adventurer has stretched out a hand to take up a cloak, and has found teeth hidden in the folds of it.

star_spawn.name: Star Spawn
star_spawn.lore: Whether it fell or was sent, the star spawn came down from between the stars, a hill of grey flesh that folds and unfolds in no pattern, and minds near it fill with thoughts that are not their own. The sages who studied one judged it to be no more than a footprint, and after that they would not ask what had made the print. Cold does it small harm, but fire will hurt it sorely.

balor_lesser.name: Lesser Balor
balor_lesser.lore: The generals in the armies of the Abyss are balors, horned giants of twice a man's height, winged like bats and wrapped in their own fire. One hand holds a burning sword and the other a whip of flame with many tails, and the stone grows black where such a demon stands. This is a lesser one of the kind, and it is reckoned lesser only because there have been armies that contrived to kill it.

marilith_spawn.name: Marilith Spawn
marilith_spawn.lore: Captains of the demon hosts are the mariliths, who order the battle while lesser fiends have no more than the pleasure of it. Each is a woman to the waist and a great serpent below, with six arms and a blade in every hand. Even this younger one fights as six duelists would who had trained together since their birth, and whoever wins past all her swords will find the tail waiting for him.

vrock.name: Vrock
vrock.lore: A vrock is a demon in the likeness of a gaunt man, with a vulture's head, ragged wings and long hooked talons. Its kind fight in shrieking flocks and dance in a ring before they kill, and when one shakes out its feathers a cloud of spores drifts from them, to take root in the skin and sprout. At the scream alone veteran soldiers have lost all heart and run.

hezrou.name: Hezrou
hezrou.lore: When a wall must be broken the Abyss sends out the hezrou, its foot soldiers, each like a toad as large as an ox that walks upright, with a wrestler's arms and a spine ridged with spikes. Long before such a demon is in sight its smell has arrived, a rot so thick that the eyes stream and the stomach turns, and whatever it wishes dead it crushes by falling bodily upon it.

glabrezu.name: Glabrezu
glabrezu.lore: Fifteen feet tall the glabrezu stands, with the head of a jackal and four arms, two that end in pincers like a crab's, big enough to close around a man, and two in clever hands like any mortal's. It prefers to use the hands. To one in despair it will offer the very thing he asks, so worded that the gift shall be his ruin, and it keeps the pincers for those who refuse to bargain.

nalfeshnee_lesser.name: Lesser Nalfeshnee
nalfeshnee_lesser.lore: There are judges even in the Abyss, and these are the nalfeshnee, who sentence every soul newly damned to the torment that befits it. Each is a mountain of fat upon the legs of a boar, with an ape's arms, a tusked snout and feathered wings far too small to lift it. When it is angry a halo of sickly rainbow light flares about it, and any mind that is caught in that glow grows slack.

quasit.name: Quasit
quasit.lore: Careless conjurers keep quasits as familiars and believe themselves the masters. The quasit is a demon two feet high, green and warty, with horns and a barbed tail and claws that leave an itch like nettles. It has the power to take the shape of a bat or a centipede, but it uses that power for nothing except escape, since its courage fails wherever a fair fight begins.

dretch.name: Dretch
dretch.lore: Lowest of all in the Abyss that may still be called demons are the dretches, squat, pale and sagging, with slack mouths and brains that have room for one spite at a time. Stronger fiends herd them into battle by the hundred and spend them as an archer spends arrows. When one is frightened it gives out a foul green fume, and hardened soldiers have emptied their stomachs at the smell of it.

shadow_demon.name: Shadow Demon
shadow_demon.lore: This fiend had a body once, and when that was lost the hatred remained. Now it is a winged shape cut out of darkness, with claws that chill and eyes like two dim coals, and as it slides along the walls the lamps gutter at its passing. It hates bright fire and holy light, for by either one may be seen how little of it is left.

incubus.name: Incubus
incubus.lore: By night, as the churchmen of the Middle Ages wrote, the incubus came to sleepers and left them pale and wasted by morning. He wears a handsome face that is a little too perfect to be trusted, and in his voice bad counsel sounds like good sense. Those whom he has charmed will defend him against their own friends, though with his kiss he is feeding upon them and drinking away the years of their lives.

succubus_shade.name: Succubus Shade
succubus_shade.lore: Old books of demons tell of the succubus, who preys on sleepers and feeds upon their strength. This one has worn so thin that lamplight passes through her, and the eye slides away when it would hold fast her outline. She comes without a sound to stand beside the bed, and those whom she has visited awaken weak and muddled, and are sure of one thing only, that something is missing.

rutterkin.name: Rutterkin
rutterkin.lore: A single rung above the dretch stands the rutterkin, and it is furious to be no higher. It is a lopsided demon, with one arm too long, a jaw hung crooked and a skin patched over with sores, and it bullies the weaker and grovels to the stronger, sometimes in the same breath. Rutterkins prowl in small packs, and a pack will halt in the midst of a hunt to fight over which of them shall walk in front.

mane_demon.name: Mane Demon
mane_demon.lore: Manes was the Roman word for the spirits of the dead, and the lore of demons borrowed it for the lowest of the damned. A mane is a soul so petty in its wickedness that the Abyss could make nothing better of it than a bloated, white-eyed body with claws. It has neither memory nor purpose, and greater demons drive it forward among a crowd of its fellows to weary the sword arm of an enemy.

chain_devil_spawn.name: Chain Devil Spawn
chain_devil_spawn.lore: Hell has for its jailers the chain devils, who go wrapped from head to foot in iron chains, hooked and barbed, that move like the arms of an octopus. The chains serve such a devil for hands and for armour and for all the speech it has. This lesser one has no patience for anything subtle, but snares a prisoner by the ankle and drags him close, and then winds the rest about him link by link.

bearded_devil.name: Bearded Devil
bearded_devil.lore: Rank upon rank the bearded devils march, for they are the infantry of Hell. Each carries a saw-toothed glaive whose cuts will not close, and wears a beard of wiry strands as thick as snakes, which lash out of their own accord and leave a burning rash. They hold a line and obey their orders, and are therefore worse to meet than demons twice their size, for not one of them will ever run unless it is commanded.

barbed_devil.name: Barbed Devil
barbed_devil.lore: Over the vaults of Hell and the most precious of its prisoners the barbed devils stand sentry, for they never grow weary of watching. Spines as long as daggers cover such a devil from scalp to tail tip, so that none can grapple it or shove it, or even stand beside it in comfort. When it is roused, flame gathers in its palms and the air around it turns hot enough to curl parchment.

bone_devil.name: Bone Devil
bone_devil.lore: Nine feet tall and thin as a dried corpse, with skin stretched tight over its bones and a scorpion's tail arched above its skull, the bone devil serves as an inspector of Hell. Such devils watch the lesser ones for slackness and report it with great relish. One of them will toy for an hour with a trapped enemy, and save the venom of its sting until the game begins to grow dull.

erinyes_lesser.name: Lesser Erinys
erinyes_lesser.lore: Alecto, Megaera and Tisiphone were the Erinyes, the Furies whom the Greeks feared, and they rose from the earth to hound oath-breakers and all who shed the blood of kindred, as they chased Orestes across Greece for the killing of his mother. The devils of Hell that bear their name are winged and fair of face and as tireless in pursuit, and they carry a poisoned sword and a rope that binds whatever it touches.

imp.name: Imp
imp.lore: When a mortal is ambitious Hell will lend him an imp for his familiar, a red devil no bigger than a cat, with the wings of a bat and a scorpion's sting at the end of its tail. It flatters him and fetches for him and gives him excellent advice, and by every word of that advice he is led one step nearer to damnation, for the imp is paid for each soul that it delivers.

lemure.name: Lemure
lemure.lore: Every May at midnight the Romans tossed black beans over the shoulder to buy off the lemures, those restless ghosts of whom they stood in dread. In Hell the name is given to the rawest stuff of all, a damned soul melted into a mound of grey flesh that has a sagging face and no mind. If it is cut asunder it flows together again, but a blessed weapon will make an end of it for good.

pit_fiend_spawn.name: Pit Fiend Spawn
pit_fiend_spawn.lore: The legions of the Nine Hells are ruled by pit fiends, twelve feet of red scale, with wings like the sails of a ship, mouths of green venom, and minds that plan in centuries. This one is newly raised to that rank and so is the least among the mightiest. It commands, bargains and lies with equal skill, and it kills with no more anger than a clerk feels as he closes a ledger.

stone_golem_lesser.name: Lesser Stone Golem
stone_golem_lesser.lore: Out of one block its makers carved this walking statue, and they spent a season cutting their commands into the stone and left it with a single instruction, which it has obeyed from that day. Time seems to thicken about it, so that those who come close find their own limbs grown heavy. Swords skate away from its sides, but it will break beneath the maul of a mason.

clay_golem.name: Clay Golem
clay_golem.lore: Rabbi Judah Loew of Prague, as the old tale relates, shaped a man from the clay of the Vltava's bank and woke it with the word 'emet', truth, written upon its brow. It guarded the ghetto until it ran wild, and then he rubbed out one letter, so that 'met', dead, remained. Clay servants made by lesser hands go berserk likewise, and their makers are seldom there to stop them.

wood_golem.name: Wood Golem
wood_golem.lore: For a hundred years, it may be, a wood golem will stand beside the door or the chest that it was bidden to guard, as still as furniture, until someone lays a hand on what it watches. It was pegged together in the shape of a man from seasoned oak, with a rune burned into its chest. Arrows lodge in it and trouble it not at all, but it has good cause to fear an axe or a torch.

animated_armor.name: Animated Armor
animated_armor.lore: There are suits of full plate that walk with no man inside them, held up by the standing order of a wizard or by a ghost too stubborn to leave its post. Such armour treads its old rounds, turns an empty visor toward any sound, and fights with all the drill of him who wore it last. The edge of a sword finds nothing to cut in it, but a heavy hammer will beat it out of shape.

shield_guardian.name: Shield Guardian
shield_guardian.lore: A wizard builds a shield guardian for one purpose only, that it may stand between its master and all harm. The link between them is an amulet, and the great bulk of wood, bronze and stone will soak up wounds, and even spells, that were meant for the wearer. But the master of this one died long ago, and having no one left to protect it guards the room, and deals with every visitor as though he were the assassin.

homunculus.name: Homunculus
homunculus.lore: To the alchemist Paracelsus is credited a recipe for the homunculus, a tiny man made by art and grown in a sealed flask. Wizards improved upon it, and with a pint of the maker's own blood they fashion a servant a foot tall with the wings of a bat, which sees for its master and bears his messages, though it cannot speak. Its bite brings on sleep, which well suits any master who would have his subjects delivered alive.

clockwork_horror.name: Clockwork Horror
clockwork_horror.lore: The artificers who built the clockwork horrors as assassins are long dead, and none remains who knows the word that stops them. Each is a brass spider of a mastiff's size, forever ticking, with spinning saws at the ends of its legs and a spark that leaps between copper prongs where a head should be. They mend one another from the scrap of their own fallen, and therefore no nest of them ever grows smaller.

displacer_beast.name: Displacer Beast
displacer_beast.lore: Six legs bear the displacer beast, which is like a panther but has two tentacles besides. It casts its likeness a little to one side of the place where it truly stands, so that a hunter may strike many times in vain, while the tentacles find their mark with deadly sureness. Between these beasts and the blink dogs there is an ancient hatred that nothing will ever appease.

owlbear.name: Owlbear
owlbear.lore: By some wretched accident or experiment of alchemy the savagery of a bear was joined to the sureness and ferocity of a great owl, and thus the first owlbear came to be. It is forever hungry and forever furious, and there is little use in reasoning with it. Disordered as its beginning was it breeds true, and so it seems to have won a lasting place among the creatures of the dungeon.

black_pudding.name: Black Pudding
black_pudding.lore: Like a heap of living tar the black pudding creeps on floor and wall and ceiling alike, eating wood, leather and steel, and a sword thrust into it comes out a pitted stump. Worse yet, the blade does not wound it, for each piece that is cut away crawls off as a smaller pudding, and lightning divides it in the same way. Old hands burn it, and they take care to stand well back while they do.

gray_ooze.name: Gray Ooze
gray_ooze.lore: One would take the gray ooze for a patch of wet stone, so still does it lie, until a boot comes down in it and it rears up to strike like a snake. Its slime eats metal with fearful speed, and mail will rust through in the time it takes to say a prayer. Let no one trust to fire and frost, though these are the usual remedies against slimes, for they will do it but half their harm.

ochre_jelly.name: Ochre Jelly
ochre_jelly.lore: Under a door, or through a crack no wider than a finger, the ochre jelly will squeeze its mustard-yellow body, and then it pours down the corridor faster than a man can trot. It has no power to eat metal or stone, but flesh and leather it devours to the last scrap. Delvers once told how a sword or lightning would divide it in two, but either does it only half harm, and its bane is fire and frost.

piercer.name: Piercer
piercer.lore: The piercer is a snail of the caves whose shell has grown into a spike of stone as long as a man's arm. It hangs point downward among the true stalactites and listens, and when footsteps pass underneath it lets go. Few rise again who are struck by that fall, but if it misses, the creature lies helpless upon the floor and must inch back toward the wall to begin its long climb once more.

lurker_above.name: Lurker Above
lurker_above.lore: Broad and flat as a manta ray, the lurker above clings to the ceiling, where its hide copies the colour and grain of the stone, and it can hang so for months without feeding. When something warm walks beneath, it lets go, falls like a wet blanket and wraps itself tight. Many a careful delver has been taken in this way, who tried every tile of the floor and seldom thought to look up.

trapper.name: Trapper
trapper.lore: Cousin to the lurker above is the trapper, which makes its bed upon the floor. It spreads itself thin across a chamber and matches the flagstones so exactly that it will sometimes raise a lump in its middle, shaped like a chest, to serve as bait. It waits for a weight upon its centre and then folds shut as a fist closes, and for this very reason veteran delvers go prodding the floor before them with a long pole.

roper.name: Roper
roper.lore: Like a stalagmite to look upon, the roper lies in wait with six sticky strands that it can put forth as far as fifty feet. Where a strand takes hold it drains away the victim's strength, and all the while it draws him steadily toward an enormous mouth full of teeth. There is a dreadful understanding in these creatures, and they seem to delight in the struggles of their prey.

carrion_crawler.name: Carrion Crawler
carrion_crawler.lore: Pale green and as long as a horse, the carrion crawler is a caterpillar with eight wet tentacles in a ring about its mouth. It eats the dead and so keeps the corridors clean of them, which might be counted a service if it had not a liking for fresh food as well. One touch of a tentacle stiffens a limb, and its trail of slime upon the stone is the mark of a hunting ground.

rot_grub_swarm.name: Rot Grub Swarm
rot_grub_swarm.lore: In midden heaps and among the ribs of the dead the rot grubs seethe by the hundred, fat white maggots as long as a finger, which feel the warmth of a body and chew their way toward it. One that reaches skin burrows in at once and makes for the heart. The accepted remedy is a hot brand laid upon the spot without delay, and none who has had need of it has ever complained of the scar.

otyugh.name: Otyugh
otyugh.lore: The rubbish pit of the dungeon is the home of the otyugh, where it eats whatever falls in, and there are keepers who feed one on purpose. It has three stumpy legs and a barrel of a body that is mostly mouth, two long tentacles ridged with thorns, and a third stalk to carry its eyes above the muck. All the filth that it has ever swallowed is carried in its bite, and a wound from it goes bad very quickly.

xorn.name: Xorn
xorn.lore: A stranger from the Elemental Plane of Earth, with three arms and three legs, the xorn is at home in the solid rock of its own country. It has a keen nose for metals and gems, which are its food, and though old tales speak of bargains struck with one for gold, down here it will fight whoever carries them.

gnoll_pack_lord.name: Gnoll Pack Lord
gnoll_pack_lord.lore: The hyena, as the bestiaries of the Middle Ages relate, digs up graves and imitates human voices to call men out of their houses at night. Gnolls are that beast risen on two legs, and the pack lord is the biggest of them, scarred from every challenge he has won. Beneath his eye the pack fights the harder, but if he is slain the rest will fall to quarrelling over who shall succeed him.

lizardfolk.name: Lizardfolk
lizardfolk.lore: Since before the dungeon had walls the lizardfolk have dwelt in the same wet caves, a scaled people of the marshes, as tall as men. Their hunters feel neither hatred nor pity for an intruder, but see in him first meat, then tools, and last a threat to the nest, and nothing that they kill is wasted. Cold makes them sluggish, and for that reason they shun the icy levels.

lizardfolk_shaman.name: Lizardfolk Shaman
lizardfolk_shaman.lore: Hung about with snake skulls and turtle shell, the eldest of the warren speaks for the spirits of marsh and egg. He brews venom from swamp adders and can spit it farther than a man throws a knife, and the tribe does nothing until he has read the signs. If the shaman should fall, the hunters stop where they stand and wait for an omen, which without him will never come.

troglodyte.name: Troglodyte
troglodyte.lore: The Greeks heard tell of tribes that dwelt in caves along the Red Sea, and named them 'troglodyte', which is cave-goer. The dungeon's troglodytes have earned the word more grimly, squat grey lizard-men who have never seen the sun. In fear or anger a troglodyte sweats an oil so rank that grown warriors are doubled over by it. They go raiding for meat and steel, and the tribe devours those of its own who grow weak.

kobold_sorcerer.name: Kobold Sorcerer
kobold_sorcerer.lore: German miners knew the kobold as a spiteful sprite of the deep shafts, and after him they named the troublesome ore cobalt. The small scaled kobolds of the dungeon claim dragons for their ancestors, and now and then one is born who can prove it, with fire at his fingertips. The tribe honours such a one as royalty, though it expects him still to run first.

spells.name: Darkness
spells.cast: {The} spits a word, and your light gutters out.

bullywug.name: Bullywug
bullywug.lore: Bullywugs are the frog-men of the flooded levels, a slick, loud, pop-eyed people, and one of them can clear a moat at a bound and will most often land spear first. Every petty chief calls himself a king and demands tribute from the next pool over, so that they are forever at war with one another. Stronger monsters hire them cheaply, paying them in lands that no one else desires.

kuo_toa.name: Kuo-Toa
