kuo_toa.lore: Long ages in the dark beside the sunless seas have broken something in the minds of the kuo-toa, that fish-headed folk whose bulging eyes never close and whose skins glisten with slime. They build gods of driftwood, bones and rumour, and then worship what they have built so fiercely that their priests work true wonders in its name. Their shields they smear with a glue, which grips fast any blade that strikes upon them.

behir_lesser.name: Lesser Behir
behir_lesser.lore: The behir is a blue-scaled serpent forty feet long that runs upon a dozen clawed legs, as easily up the face of a cliff as along a floor. Lightning gathers behind its teeth and comes out in a single straight stroke, and whatever lives through that it wraps about and squeezes. It hates dragons beyond all reason, and will forsake its kill in order to go and fight one.

catoblepas.name: Catoblepas
catoblepas.lore: Near the springs of the Nile, wrote Pliny the Elder, lived the catoblepas, whose name is Greek for 'the one that looks downward'. It was a sluggish beast, with a head so heavy that it hung always toward the ground, and he counted this a mercy to mankind, since any who met its eyes fell dead. Here below it grazes on poisonous weeds, and woe to those who stand before it when, now and then, it lifts its head and looks up.

opener.wind_up: {name} heaves {his} heavy head up off the ground.

cockatrice.name: Cockatrice
cockatrice.lore: From an egg laid by an old rooster and brooded by a toad the cockatrice is hatched, if the bestiaries of old speak true. It has the head and wings of a cock upon a serpent's body, and flesh that it touches stiffens toward stone. The same books name two things of which it stands in terror, the weasel, which alone can fight it unharmed, and the crow of a rooster, which is its death.

darkmantle.name: Darkmantle
darkmantle.lore: With its tentacles drawn up the darkmantle hangs from the roof of a cave, and seems but one stalactite more. When a lantern passes beneath, it spills a blackness that no flame can push back, and drops to wrap its webbed body about the nearest head. The victim is left blind and smothering, wearing his enemy as a hood, and his friends are slow to swing for fear of striking him.

ettercap.name: Ettercap
ettercap.lore: To speakers of old Scots a spider was an 'ettercap', from the Old English 'attercoppe', which is poison-head. The ettercap of the dungeon is a hunched grey creature with a spider's fangs and spinnerets, but his habits are a shepherd's, and giant spiders are his herd. He strings snares across every corridor of his range, and when prey is taken he waits until it has worn itself out before he comes to bite.

grick.name: Grick
grick.lore: Wedged in a crack of the rock, whose very colour it wears, the grick lies ready to strike at whatever passes. It is a rubbery worm as thick as a man's thigh, with four barbed tentacles about a snapping beak, and its hide gives like wet leather, and magic will hurt it worse than any blade. Once it has fed it sleeps for days in its hole, but while it is hungry it will follow a company of travellers for miles.

hook_horror.name: Hook Horror
hook_horror.lore: Delvers who hear a clicking in the dark will count the different rhythms, for by them may be known the number of hook horrors in the pack. The creatures talk by clacking their hooks against the cave wall, and the sound carries far. Each stands nine feet tall, with the armoured body of a beetle and the beak of a vulture, and has in place of hands two bony hooks as long as scythes.

phase_spider.name: Phase Spider
phase_spider.lore: Alongside the solid world there lies a border realm of mist, and out of it the phase spider hunts. It is pale blue and banded and as large as a pony, and it steps through, bites and steps back before a sword can answer, so that its victims can tell only of an empty corridor and a sudden pain. Assassins pay richly for its venom, though the gathering of it has cost more lives than ever the venom took.

wyvern.name: Wyvern
wyvern.lore: English heralds took care to part the wyvern from the dragon, for a dragon has four legs and a wyvern only two, with wings for forelimbs and a tail that is knotted and barbed. The living beast has neither a dragon's mind nor its breath, but makes amends for both by the fury of its temper. It swoops and pins its prey with its talons and drives the tail sting in from above, and the poison is swift in its work.

skeleton_archer.name: Skeleton Archer
skeleton_archer.lore: These bowmen fell at their posts and were ordered to rise again. They have no sinew left with which to draw a string, yet the bow bends and the shaft flies as true as ever it did in life. Arrows sent in answer rattle through the ribs and out at the farther side, and a mace will serve much better. Their quivers never run dry, though no one has ever seen them being filled.

skeleton_warrior.name: Skeleton Warrior
skeleton_warrior.lore: Some kingdom long buried had these for its men-at-arms, and they wear its rusted mail and hold yet the shield wall that their captain taught them, for the drill has outlasted the flesh. They advance in step and cover one another, and when the sword is turned aside they bash with the rim of the shield. The spell that raised them is older than any that a living warlock can read.

skeleton_mage.name: Skeleton Mage
skeleton_mage.lore: There was once a wizard who would not put down his books even at the bidding of death. Now the robes hang upon bare ribs, and when the skeleton lifts its hand a pale light crawls among the finger bones. It knows its spells still, though it has forgotten why it learned them, and necromancers prize such a skull, because it keeps a whisper of all that was ever committed to its memory.

burning_skeleton.name: Burning Skeleton
burning_skeleton.lore: Men who bargained with the demons of fire and were paid in full became the burning skeletons, or so the tradition of the dungeon holds. Each is clothed in a flame that neither consumes the bones nor ever goes out. The blaze is both weapon and shield to it, and all that it touches catches fire, but cold water will hiss upon it and crack the heated bones.

death_throes.line: {The} bursts in a gout of flame!

frost_skeleton.name: Frost Skeleton
frost_skeleton.lore: A company of soldiers froze upon a winter march and has never thawed. Rime crusts their bones with blue and white, icicles hang from their jaws, and wherever one walks a low mist follows about its ankles. Its touch fastens ice upon the flesh, yet a torch will quickly undo it, since the frost is all that holds its joints together.

zombie_hulk.name: Zombie Hulk
zombie_hulk.lore: When a necromancer has need of a battering ram he takes the largest corpse to hand and fills it with dark power until the muscles swell and split the skin. The hulk is slow, and has never any need of haste. He plods to a door, a wall or a line of shields and beats upon it with fists as great as anvils until it lies flat.

plague_zombie.name: Plague Zombie
plague_zombie.lore: In the years of the Black Death the gravediggers could not keep pace, and the dead were laid in pits by the hundred. Those who climb out of such a pit carry the sickness with them yet, black of finger and foul of breath, and by a scratch or a bite they pass on the fever of which they died. Fire was of old the remedy for a plague house, and it will serve against these also.

rotting_zombie.name: Rotting Zombie
rotting_zombie.lore: The cheapest spell that a necromancer knows will raise a rotting zombie. Sinew and bad magic are all that hold him together, and pieces drop from him as he walks. He has neither skill nor thought, but comes shuffling forward with his arms held out and stops for no wound short of ruin. One alone is merely a trouble, but a corridor full of them is like a wall that has teeth to bite.

ghast.name: Ghast
ghast.lore: Much cleverer than his cousin the ghoul is the ghast, for enough of his mind remains that he can lay an ambush, post a lookout and lead the pack that feeds beside him. His claws lock the muscles of whatever they scratch, and the reek of an opened grave rolls before him so thickly that soldiers retch before they can raise a shield. He keeps tokens, moreover, of the hunts that he remembers best.

aura.line: The reek of the opened grave rolls off the Ghast, and you retch.

gravehound.name: Gravehound
gravehound.lore: Kings of old had their hunting dogs buried with them, that the pack might run beside them in the next world, but it was tomb robbers who woke these. They are bone and dried hide now, and they hunt just as they did in life, for one drives the quarry while two take the flanks, and when their jaws close on a hamstring they do not open again.

poltergeist.name: Poltergeist
poltergeist.lore: Poltergeist is a German word that means 'noisy ghost', and it is given to the spirit of one who died bewildered and has remained so. It has no shape to show but only a temper, by which doors slam and crockery flies and a chair will skate across the room to break against the wall. No eye has ever seen one, though anyone may see what it throws, and from what quarter it was thrown. It has no wish to hunt the living, but rages at them because they are free to leave.

alarm.line: Something knocks loudly on the walls.
alarm.line_unseen: Something knocks loudly on the walls.

revenant.name: Revenant
revenant.lore: William of Newburgh, the English chronicler of the twelfth century, recorded the histories of several revenants, wicked men who climbed from their graves by night to plague their towns until the neighbours dug up the bodies and burned them. One cause alone brings a revenant back, and that is a wrong which he means to repay. He will walk through the cuts of swords to reach the throat that he remembers.

allip.name: Allip
allip.lore: If a mind has broken before the body died, the remnant of it may linger as an allip, a twist of darkness in the rough shape of a person. It mutters without pause, now half a prayer, now a child's rhyme, now a list of names, and those who listen find themselves following the thread, and so it enters into their minds. Upon any that it touches there falls a stupor, heavy and without dreams.

haunting_presence.name: Haunting Presence
haunting_presence.lore: Some terrible thing befell in this room, and a little of the person who suffered it has never departed. The presence has neither face nor voice, but may be known by a cold place in the air, by a stillness as of breath held, and by the certainty that one is watched from the corner. Then the dread descends all at once, and strong men find that they are running before they have resolved to run. No one has ever seen it, though those who have eyes for the unseen tell of a grey smudge in the corner, about the height of the one who died there.

fetch.name: Fetch
fetch.lore: In Irish lore a fetch is the exact double of a living man, and when it was seen in the morning it promised him long life, but when it was seen at dusk it foretold that his death was near. The fetches of the dungeon have made a trade of that omen. One of them will put on your own face when you look upon it, and will walk toward you smiling, to drink your life at a touch.

shade.name: Shade
shade.lore: At the edge of the world, where Odysseus sailed to question the dead, the shades crowded about his trench of sheep's blood and were thin and voiceless until they had drunk. Such are the ghosts of which Homer sang, memories without strength that hunger for warmth. To the shades below that draught was never given, and so they gather wherever the light is poor and make it dimmer still.

will_o_wisp.name: Will-o-Wisp
will_o_wisp.lore: Marsh travellers in every part of Europe knew the pale light that bobs before them on the path like a lantern and leads straight into the bog. The learned named it ignis fatuus, 'foolish fire', and country folk called it Will with the wisp, or Jack with the lantern. In the dungeon such a light is a spiteful ghost that feeds upon the terror of those who are lost, and its touch jolts like lightning.

soul_shadow.name: Soul Shadow
soul_shadow.lore: Should many die together in terror, by massacre or in the fall of a mine, it may be that their souls are tangled and cannot part, and then the knot becomes a single being. Faces surface and sink in the mass of its darkness, and they agree with one another in nothing but their pain. It folds itself over the living and pulls, and whatever it tears free is added to the multitude within.

death_echo.name: Death Echo
death_echo.lore: A murder or a last stand may strike so hard that the moment is stamped into the very stone, and afterward the place remembers it and plays it over again, with the same scream and the same fall. This is a death echo, and no ghost stands behind it. Whoever walks into that scene is given a part to play, and the echo strikes at him as it struck at the first.

vampire_thrall.name: Vampire Thrall
vampire_thrall.lore: The madman Renfield, in Bram Stoker's novel, served Count Dracula from a cell in the asylum, eating flies and begging that his master would take notice of him. Every vampire keeps servants of that sort, mortals who have been fed a few drops of the master's blood and are stronger than they ought to be, and wholly incapable of disloyalty. A thrall has still some manner of pulse, and he would gladly spend it to buy his master one more night.

nosferatu.name: Nosferatu
nosferatu.lore: Emily Gerard, a Scottish writer who dwelt in Transylvania, set down the word nosferatu in 1885 as the name by which that country knew the vampire, and Bram Stoker carried it into Dracula. Nothing courtly survives in this breed. He is bald, rat-toothed and long-fingered, a creature of plague cellars, and the rats come at his call as they came off his ship at Wisborg. He hates the dawn above all things, and has found in the dungeon a country where it never rises.

strigoi.name: Strigoi
strigoi.lore: From the Latin strix, the screech owl that drank blood by night, Romanian villagers made the word strigoi, and they gave it to a troubled man who would not rest in death. When he climbs from his grave he goes first to his own home and feeds on his family before the neighbours. Grave sickness is in his claws, and the old remedies against him were garlic in the mouth, a stake through the heart, and fire.

jiangshi.name: Jiangshi
jiangshi.lore: The hopping corpse of China is the jiangshi, who goes still in the robes of a Qing official. Death has stiffened his limbs, so that he must come forward by bounds, holding both arms straight before him. He finds the living by their breath, and a traveller who holds his breath may pass unseen. A paper talisman pressed to his forehead stops him cold, and peach wood, mirrors and the crow of a rooster will all drive him back.

talisman.line: You hold up the written page, and the Jiangshi stops dead, as if a talisman had been pressed to its forehead.

vrykolakas.name: Vrykolakas
vrykolakas.lore: On the islands of Greece the restless dead are called vrykolakas. Such a corpse does not rot, but swells as tight as a drum and walks the village by night, knocking at doors and calling a name a single time, and whoever answers is dead within days, so that the islanders learned never to answer a first knock. About the year 1700 the French botanist Tournefort watched while the people of Mykonos burned one.

demi_lich.name: Demi-Lich
demi_lich.lore: So many ages may pass over a lich that the body crumbles away and leaves only the skull, to be the house of a mind that cannot die. Such is the demi-lich, which has passed almost wholly beyond the life of the flesh and has its soul gathered into the gems that are set in the sockets of its eyes. With no more than a wail it can make captive the souls of the living, and the magic at its command is beyond all mortal understanding.

lich_thrall.name: Lich Thrall
lich_thrall.lore: At the lych-gate of the churchyard a coffin used to rest before burial, for lich in Old English is a corpse. When a great lich has need of a steward, a doorkeeper and a spare pair of hands, he raises up some lesser sorcerer to serve him as his thrall. That servant remembers his spells and his oath and nothing besides, and his cold fingers lock the joints of anyone they touch.

death_mage.name: Death Mage
death_mage.lore: Though King Saul had himself outlawed the art, as Scripture tells, he went in disguise by night to the witch of Endor and bade her call up the dead prophet Samuel, and Samuel came and told Saul that he would die the next day. The death mage has made that forbidden trade the study of his life, and so as to learn it the better he has gone halfway into the grave.

spells.name: Grave Ward
spells.cast: {The}'s chant ends: grave-dust rises about {him} and hangs in the air.

bone_witch.name: Bone Witch
bone_witch.lore: Baba Yaga the Bony-Legged, of whom they tell in Russian tales, has a hut that stands on chicken legs behind a fence of human bones with a skull on every post. This witch is of her kind, but has gone further and kept nothing of herself save the bones. She hangs her lair with what her enemies leave behind them, and throws the sharper pieces. Spear points slip between her ribs, but a hammer will find bone there to break.

necromancer_lord.name: Necromancer Lord
necromancer_lord.lore: None could slay Koschei the Deathless, the sorcerer of Russian tales, for he kept his death outside his body, hidden in a needle, in an egg, in a duck, in a hare, in an iron chest under an oak on the island of Buyan. A necromancer lord has learned the same craft. The dead are his servants, and somewhere among them walks the one that carries for him the thing he fears to lose.

pale_master.name: Pale Master
pale_master.lore: There are necromancers who will not wait for death, and such a one is the pale master. As each part of him fails he replaces it from the grave, with a dead man's hand stitched at the wrist, with borrowed ribs and with eyes that no longer blink, and by every graft he grows colder and harder to tell from his servants. He knows exactly how a body comes apart, and his touch stops a limb as surely as a surgeon's knife.

wight_lord.name: Wight Lord
wight_lord.lore: Thorolf Lame-Foot, of whom the Icelandic Eyrbyggja Saga tells, was a bitter old man who would not stay in his grave. He walked the valley killing shepherds and cattle, and those he killed were seen walking in his company, until his body was burned to ash, which alone could end it. A wight lord rules after that fashion, and every victim that he drains is joined to his household.

barrow_wight.name: Barrow Wight
barrow_wight.lore: Grettir the outlaw, as his saga relates, broke into the mound of Kar the Old and found the dead man seated upon his throne among his treasure. Kar laid hold of him, and they wrestled through the dark until Grettir cut off his head. Of that same order of the dead is the barrow wight, a chieftain who will never give up his gold, and whose grip will stop the breath of the living.
barrow_wight.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} barrow and watches you go.

cairn_wight.name: Cairn Wight
cairn_wight.lore: In the Scottish Highlands each passer-by would add a stone to the cairn that was heaped above the dead, and to promise a man a stone on his cairn was to promise that he would be remembered. The dead beneath a neglected cairn remember that they have been forgotten. This wight had neither hall nor gold, but only a pile of rocks upon a hillside, and he resents the living all the more because of it.
cairn_wight.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} cairn and watches you go.

crypt_thing.name: Crypt Thing
crypt_thing.lore: To certain tombs was given a warden of the undead, made expressly to guard them and yet bring no harm upon the dead who rest within. The crypt thing, as he is named, does not assail intruders openly, but bewilders them by magic as though they had been snatched away and set down elsewhere, so that they forget which way they came and stumble lost and alone. There is no reasoning with such a guardian, nor will any bribe move him.

grave_guardian.name: Grave Guardian
grave_guardian.lore: Champions of old swore as death drew near that they would keep watch over holy ground, and they were buried standing at the door of the crypt with sword in hand. It is their own oath that holds them there, and no necromancer's art. Some spark of the blessing that was laid upon them remains, so that other dead things shrink away from them, and they strike down all who come to dig, robber and crusader alike.
grave_guardian.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} grave and watches you go.

tomb_guardian.name: Tomb Guardian
tomb_guardian.lore: When Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of China, went into his tomb, some eight thousand soldiers of fired clay went with him for a guard, and no two had the same face. Lesser kings could not afford such clay, and they used men in its stead. Thus was the tomb guardian made, a picked soldier sealed in with his lord and bound to one doorway forever, and the nearer a thief comes to the burial chamber, the more fiercely he will fight.
tomb_guardian.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} tomb and watches you go.

ossuary_horror.name: Ossuary Horror
ossuary_horror.lore: The bones of tens of thousands of the dead were piled in pyramids at Sedlec in Bohemia, and strung into a chandelier in which, men say, every bone of the human body may be found. But bones kept in such multitudes forget to whom they belonged, and a whole charnel house may then get up and walk. Such is the ossuary horror, a rolling drift of skulls and long bones, and all that it slays it gathers into the heap.

mohrg.name: Mohrg
mohrg.lore: A murderer who dies unrepentant and unpunished may rise again as a mohrg, to do in death as he did in life. His ribs hang open, and where the heart should be lies coiled a long purple tongue, of which a single touch will lock every muscle in the body. All whom he slays get up within a few days and follow after him, and for that reason a mohrg is seldom left to walk alone for long.

huecuva.name: Huecuva
huecuva.lore: Huecuvu was the name that the Mapuche of Chile gave to spirits of blight and sickness, but in the deep places it belongs to a priest who broke his vows and died unforgiven. He goes still in the rags of his vestments, and he can put on the semblance of a living cleric to draw the trusting near. Wherever he scratches, the wound will fester, and there is nothing left that he fears save honest prayer.

lesser_death.name: Lesser Death
lesser_death.lore: Thanatos was the name of Death among the Greeks, and Sleep was his brother. Sisyphus once tricked him into his own chains, so that for a time none upon earth could die, and Heracles wrestled him beside a grave and won back Queen Alcestis. The lesser death is but a small shadow of that power, a reaper sent out for one soul at a time, and if Death himself was overcome, as the stories show, then it too can be beaten.

greater_shadow.name: Greater Shadow
greater_shadow.lore: Odysseus sailed to the edge of the world to question the dead, and there he dug a trench and filled it with the blood of sheep. The shades came crowding about it to drink, for blood alone could give them back their voices. A shade that has drunk through many centuries becomes a greater shadow, which spreads through a chamber like spilled ink and draws the strength out of every arm within it.

nightshade_spawn.name: Nightshade Spawn
nightshade_spawn.lore: Even the lesser offspring of the true nightshades are mightier than nearly all the undead that a delver is likely to meet, and this spawn is of their number. It is the very power that is enemy to life, clothed in a body, and it corrupts and defiles whatever is about it. At its coming the green things wither and fires sink low, and hope fades from the hearts of all who are near.

forsaken_shell.name: Forsaken Shell
forsaken_shell.lore: If the soul is torn by violence from a body, the body may yet be set walking as an empty vessel, moved by necromancy and by nothing else, and then it is called a forsaken shell. It keeps neither the memory nor the nature of the one who dwelt in it. There are necromancers who make such shells by design, when they have need of the soul for some other work and would not let a useful body go to waste.

hollow_one.name: Hollow One
hollow_one.lore: Those who trade away their souls in dark bargains do not rest when they die, but walk as hollow ones in a hunger without end. They seek the souls of others to fill the place where their own once lay, yet no soul will fill it for long. They are creatures more to be pitied than hated, for that emptiness can never be sated, and it has driven them out of their wits.

charnel_hound.name: Charnel Hound
charnel_hound.lore: By the old custom of England and of Scandinavia, the first to be buried in a new churchyard must stay and guard it, and so the builders would bury a dog there beforehand, to spare any human soul the duty. Folk called that guardian the church grim. The necromancers have copied it in the charnel hound, for which they wire the bones of a whole pack of dogs into one tracker that never tires and never loses a scent.

dread_knight.name: Dread Knight
dread_knight.lore: Paladins were the dread knights once, until they fell, and the power that heaven had lent them was twisted into an unholy strength. In death they keep all the skill at arms and all the craft of war that they had in life, and few of the undead are more perilous in battle. Light itself seems to sink into their armour, and whoever meets that gaze feels upon him the weight of condemned souls.

bone_archer.name: Bone Archer
bone_archer.lore: High on a ledge a dead bowman was set and bidden to shoot at whatever is warm. The bone archer whittles its shafts from its own spare ribs and never runs short, for the dungeon furnishes it with more, and an arrow shot back at it will mostly pass through the gaps between its bones. It will not come close to fight, but waits with all the patience of one that has nowhere else to go.

skeletal_giant.name: Skeletal Giant
skeletal_giant.lore: Seven cubits long was the coffin that the Spartans dug up at Tegea, as Herodotus relates, and they bore the huge bones home as those of the hero Orestes. Many such finds were made in the ancient world, and men naturally judged from them that giants had once walked the earth. Some of those bones have now been raised to walk again, and a fist of such bones is as great as a millstone and falls with a millstone's weight.

undead_dragon_lesser.name: Lesser Undead Dragon
undead_dragon_lesser.lore: Cadmus slew the dragon of Ares at the spring of Thebes and sowed its teeth, and armed men sprang up from the furrows, for the bones of a dragon do not lie quiet. This one was raised whole by a necromancer who had more ambition than wisdom. The fire that burned in its breast is quenched, and when it opens its jaws upon a foe it is the cold of the grave that it breathes.

lich_dragon_spawn.name: Lich Dragon Spawn
lich_dragon_spawn.lore: Though a dragon lives a thousand years it fears the end no less, and some of the oldest and proudest have let a lich bind their souls into a gem of the hoard, that they might rise again as bone and cold sorcery. The spawn of such dragons were hatched dead from eggs laid before the rite, and have never drawn a living breath. They have all of a dragon's cunning with none of its warmth, and their bite will stop the heart.

ethereal_filcher.name: Ethereal Filcher
ethereal_filcher.lore: Between this world and the next the ethereal filcher slips to and fro, an undead thing without a body, and steals from the living. Bright and magical things draw it, and it carries them away to its hidden lairs in the ether, for its fingers pass through a closed pack as easily as through air. It is seldom fierce unless it is cornered, and once it has its prize it will flee sooner than fight, but if it is slain, whatever it took will fall out of it again.

nightmare_shade.name: Nightmare Shade
nightmare_shade.lore: Sleep had three sons who shape the dreams of men, as Ovid sings, and while Morpheus plays the parts of human folk, his brother Phobetor, the Frightener, puts on the forms of beasts and monsters. A nightmare shade is an evil dream that has outlived its dreamer, who died in terror. It looks into a living mind, searches out the thing that is most dreaded there, and clothes itself in that shape.

soul_eater_spawn.name: Soul Eater Spawn
soul_eater_spawn.lore: In Egypt men feared to die a second death. For in the Hall of Judgment the heart was weighed against the feather of Ma'at, and if it was heavy with wrongdoing it was thrown to Ammit, who had a crocodile's head, the forequarters of a lion and the hindquarters of a hippopotamus, and the soul she ate was no more. The soul eater spawn are small and hungry things of her kind, but they await no verdict before they feed.

dread_wraith.name: Dread Wraith
dread_wraith.lore: After a wraith has fed for centuries it no longer troubles to wear a shape that eyes can see. The dread wraith stands half a step outside the world and reaches through, so that a traveller feels first the cold and next the hand upon his heart, and all the while sees nothing. Old soldiers therefore counselled that one should swing at the place where the cold is felt. Its wail freezes the limbs, and the air about it stays dark and bitter long after it has gone, but fire and holy light can find it out where the eye cannot.

nightwing.name: Nightwing
nightwing.lore: Mightiest of all the nightshades is the nightwing, a shadow in the likeness of a bat, but so vast beyond belief that the stars are blotted out as it passes overhead. It is wrought wholly of the power that is enemy to life, and it defiles the lands beneath its wings, killing all that grows and fouling the springs and rivers. The ancient writings warn that wherever a nightwing appears, a season of death and great calamity follows after it.

crystal_ooze.name: crystal ooze
crystal_ooze.lore: Seams of gems are the haunt of the crystal ooze, a clear, slow jelly that grows a rind of crystal wherever it rests, as sugar candy grows upon a string. It can scarcely be seen there until the wall begins to move, and all that it touches it coats in a crust that sets fast and stiffens the joints. Miners therefore try a doubtful vein with a hammer, for true crystal rings beneath the blow, but the ooze will crack.

green_slime.name: green slime
green_slime.lore: From damp ceilings the green slime hangs like wet moss until something warm walks beneath it, and then it lets itself fall. It devours cloth, leather, wood and flesh alike, turning all into more green slime, and whoever tries to scrape it away does no more than spread it. Old delvers carry a torch against its coming, for fire and hard frost are the two things that will kill it.

yellow_mold.name: yellow mold
yellow_mold.lore: On old wood, and on bones older still, the yellow mold lies as a dry crust the colour of sulphur. One footstep will burst it, and the cloud of its spores fills first the lungs and then the head, so that men who breathe it see doors that are not there as clearly as they see their own friends. It burns with a bright orange flame, and fire is the only safe way to clear a room of it.

brown_mold.name: brown mold
brown_mold.lore: Warmth is food to the brown mold, as damp is to others of its kind, so that the air about it is bitter cold and a hand held near grows numb. Let none bring a torch against it, for fire feeds it, and a burning brand cast into a patch may double it in a breath. It is frost that kills it, and at the touch of a sudden cold it turns grey and is dead within moments.

gibbering_slime.name: gibbering slime
gibbering_slime.lore: The gibbering slime is a heap of pale jelly all covered with mouths, of which none is finished and none is ever silent. They repeat the scraps of every voice it has swallowed, prayers and bargains, a child's counting rhyme, and someone calling out for a lamp. If you stand long beside it the words will begin to sound like sense, and then beware, for in that moment it reaches out to take you.

toxic_jelly.name: toxic jelly
toxic_jelly.lore: Poison runs clear through the toxic jelly, a bright green and trembling thing that has no need of fangs. It folds itself over whatever blunders into it and lets the venom soak in. Rats that drink from a pool it has crossed are dead before they reach their holes, and so when wary delvers come to a corridor with no rat in it at all, they search it well, in case a jelly has passed that way.

death_throes.line: {The} bursts in a spray of venom!
death_throes.warn_line: {The} quivers and turns a sickly green.

giant_scorpion.name: giant scorpion
giant_scorpion.lore: Orion the hunter boasted that he would slay every beast upon earth, and the Earth sent a scorpion to sting him. Both were set among the stars on opposite sides of heaven, and Orion still sets when the Scorpion rises. The scorpion of the dungeon is as large as a pony, and it uses its claws only to hold the prey still, while the tail above them does the deadly work.

giant_wasp.name: giant wasp
giant_wasp.lore: No hunting wasp kills outright what it has caught, but stings it into stillness, drags it home and lays an egg upon it, that the grub may hatch upon fresh meat. The nest is of grey paper chewed from wood, and by watching wasps at that labour the naturalist Reaumur conceived that paper could be made from trees. In the dungeon the same craft is practised by wasps as large as hounds.

giant_beetle.name: giant beetle
giant_beetle.lore: Beetles have their foremost wings hardened into cases that close over the back like a clasped book, and on one that is as big as a boar these make a shield that will turn the edge of a sword. Its jaws work like the tongs of a smith. Yet it is neither clever nor quick, and whoever can deal a blow heavy enough to crack the shell will soon have made an end of it.

giant_mantis.name: giant mantis
giant_mantis.lore: Mantis is the Greek word for a prophet, and the creature was so named because it holds its forelegs folded like hands at prayer. It can turn its head and look straight behind it, as no beetle or wasp can do, and it strikes more swiftly than an eye can blink, closing those spined forelegs like a trap. Here it has grown to the height of a man, and it waits for its prey as patiently as ever it did.

spider_queen.name: spider queen
spider_queen.lore: So skilled at the loom was Arachne of Lydia that she challenged Athena herself, and her tapestry showed the gods at their worst, with never a flaw in all the work. Athena rent it and changed the girl into a spider, to hang and weave forever. Of that line the spider queen is a monstrous daughter, and her brood goes hunting where she sends it, while all her hall is draped with silk and with the prey that the silk holds fast.

phase_spider_lesser.name: Lesser Phase Spider
phase_spider_lesser.lore: There is a wrong side to the air, and from it the phase spider hunts. It steps out of the world, walks to where its prey is standing and steps in again with its fangs already closing, and it is gone before any sword can answer. The young, which are the lesser of the race, can make but a short hop and must rest between one and the next. Their webs shimmer faintly, and in them hang things that are not wholly there.

web_spinner.name: web spinner
web_spinner.lore: Yard upon yard of silk the web spinner makes, stronger than a steel wire of the same weight, and it will stretch like a bowstring before it breaks. With this the spinner closes a corridor from wall to wall, and then it sits back within a crack and leaves the web to do the fighting, for it bites only what is already tangled. Whoever carries a torch may undo all its labour in a few moments.

death_beetle.name: death beetle
death_beetle.lore: Egyptians laid a scarab of stone over the hearts of their dead, graven with a spell that bade the heart speak nothing against its owner at the judgment. And in the sickrooms of England, when the deathwatch beetle ticked in the timbers, folk took it for an omen that the watch beside the bed would soon end in death. Both natures meet in the death beetle, a black-shelled giant of the tombs whose rattle makes the limbs grow heavy.

giant_lizard.name: giant lizard
giant_lizard.lore: Many a lizard bears on the crown of its head a pale scale that serves as a third eye, which sees no shapes but knows light from dark and gives warning of a shadow passing over. The giant lizard is as long as a rowing boat, and it lies upon warm stone beside the vents of the dungeon. Cold makes it sluggish, but when it is warmed through it has a swiftness that none would look for in a creature of such bulk.

basilisk_lesser.name: lesser basilisk
basilisk_lesser.lore: Pliny described the basilisk as a serpent of Cyrene no longer than twelve fingers, with a white mark like a crown upon its head, whose breath withered the bushes and split the stone, and which a weasel could slay. Those who wrote after him added that it hatched from a cock's egg brooded by a toad, and that a mirror or the crow of a rooster would be its death. While it is young, its stare has power only to lock the limbs.

rock_python.name: rock python
rock_python.lore: Greatest of the serpents of Africa is the rock python, which can swallow an antelope whole, horns and all. It has no need to crush its prey, for each time the animal breathes out the coils draw tighter, until the heart can drive the blood no longer, and then the jaws creep forward over the meal, first one side and then the other. In the dungeon it lies among fallen stones, and may easily be taken for one more of them.

komodo_brute.name: komodo brute
komodo_brute.lore: It was long believed that the Komodo dragon killed by the foulness of its mouth and waited for the wounds to fester, but the truth is more dreadful, for in its lower jaw are glands of a venom that will not let the blood clot. Its teeth, edged like saws, open the wound, and when the prey has wandered off, growing weaker, it follows the scent at its leisure. The komodo brute is of that same race, but of a larger breed.

giant_frog.name: giant frog
giant_frog.lore: A frog has its tongue rooted at the front of the mouth, so that it can be flung out and home again faster than a blink, and to swallow it draws its eyes down into its skull and pushes the morsel along with them. The giant frog, which is of the size of a calf, deals in this fashion with prey as big as a helmet, and it sits waiting in black water with nothing but those eyes to be seen.

mud_crawler.name: mud crawler
mud_crawler.lore: Along the rivers under the earth lives the mud crawler, a squat, plated reptile, something between a snapping turtle and a crocodile. It lies in the silt until the mud dries on its back into a second shell, from which a sword's edge glances aside. On land its feet are slow but its hooked claws are swift, and once they are set it holds fast and leaves its great weight to do the rest.

swamp_serpent.name: swamp serpent
swamp_serpent.lore: Where the passages are flooded the swamp serpent swims with all its thick body upon the surface and its head held high. Like the cottonmouth of the southern swamps it gives warning before it strikes, coiling and throwing back its head to gape until the white lining of its mouth is seen. No other courtesy is to be had of it, and its venom breaks down the blood and flesh all about the place where it has bitten.

sea_snake.name: sea snake
sea_snake.lore: Certain cousins of the cobra went back into the water long ago and became the sea snakes. Their tails have flattened into paddles, one lung runs nearly the length of the body, and some can draw air through the skin and stay beneath for hours. Drop for drop their venom is among the strongest of any serpent's, and it stills the muscles. They have found the flooded lower halls of the dungeon well suited to their needs.

dire_lion.name: dire lion
dire_lion.lore: Some thirty thousand years ago the painters of Chauvet cave drew by torchlight upon the rock a whole pride of lions in profile, stalking bison, and the males without manes. For lions hunted in those days through all of Europe, and those lions of the caves stood taller than any that live now. A few of that race the dungeon has preserved, and they hunt in its darkness as their kind has always done.

dire_bear.name: dire bear
dire_bear.lore: Through many thousands of winters the cave bears slept so deep underground that their fur polished the rock where they squeezed past, and the marks of their claws are there yet, higher than a man can reach. The dire bear is that same beast, or one very like it. It does not go out in search of trouble, but it will make trouble enough for anything that walks into the chamber where it sleeps.

wolf_pack_leader.name: wolf pack leader
wolf_pack_leader.lore: Every wolf pack is a family, a mated pair and their grown young, and the one who leads is the parent, who chooses the trail and begins the hunt, though others may be fiercer in a fight. The leader's howl carries for miles and tells each wolf in hearing where to be. Men who hear that cry close at hand in the dark grow so afraid that they forget whatever they had purposed.

werewolf.name: werewolf
werewolf.lore: King Lycaon of Arcadia doubted that his guest was truly Zeus, and to make trial of him, as Ovid tells, he served him human flesh at table. Zeus brought down the house in fire, and the king fled howling into the fields while grey fur spread over his arms, and he was a wolf, though with the same savage eyes. That ancient doom lies upon every werewolf, and men have found no surer answer to it than silver.

werewolf_alpha.name: werewolf alpha
werewolf_alpha.lore: Sigmund and his son Sinfjotli, as the Volsunga Saga relates, found two wolfskins hanging in a hut of the forest and put them on, and could not take them off again. They ran as wolves and spoke in howls, until Sigmund in his rage bit his own son in the throat, and when at last the skins came loose they burned them. But the alpha never burned his skin, and he has worn the shape of the wolf for centuries by his own choice.

werebear.name: werebear
werebear.lore: In the last battle of King Hrolf Kraki there fought a huge bear that no weapon could bite, and it was Bodvar Bjarki, the greatest of the king's champions, whose body sat all that while in a trance far behind the line. A friend shook him awake, and the bear vanished and the battle was lost. His father had been cursed to a bear's shape by day, and the werebears of the dungeon carry that curse, though they have no such cause as Bodvar's to fight for.

wererat.name: wererat
wererat.lore: Wherever men store grain and cast out scraps the rats will thrive, and the wererat has taken their lesson to heart. He lives in the drains beneath the halls of his betters, where he steals and listens and sells what he has heard. If it comes to fighting he prefers to put a knife in the back and be gone down some hole too small for pursuit. His bite carries a fever with it, and sometimes the curse itself.

weretiger.name: weretiger
weretiger.lore: The harimau jadian, in the telling of Malay villagers, was a man who became a tiger after dark. The men of Kerinci in the highlands of Sumatra were reputed to do so, and travellers out of that country were closely watched at night. Many, it was said, could change at will, which the wolf-men of Europe could not. The weretiger hunts as tigers do, alone, and springs from behind when he has long and patiently stalked his prey.

winter_wolf.name: winter wolf
winter_wolf.lore: Skoll and Hati are the two wolves that run across the sky in the tales of the Norse, the first pursuing the sun and the second the moon, and at the world's end each shall take its prey. Winter wolves are counted among their kindred, white beasts as high as horses, cold to the bone and clever enough to speak. The frost giants keep them for hounds, and their breath will freeze a man where he stands.

blink_dog.name: blink dog
blink_dog.lore: Travellers count it a good omen to meet with blink dogs, which live in packs and have wits of their own, and are so swift that they seem not to cross the ground between. They appear beside a foe, bite and are gone again, so that it is very hard to bring one to bay. Yet for all their wild manner of fighting they are deeply loyal, and they may be won as friends.

death_dog.name: death dog
death_dog.lore: Two heads had Orthrus, the brother of Cerberus, who guarded the red cattle of Geryon at the western edge of the world until Heracles came for the herd and slew him with one blow of his club. The death dogs are that same breed, much fallen from its old estate, and they keep company with the dead. Both their heads will bite, and the wounds that they make will fester and rot instead of healing.

giant_eagle.name: giant eagle
giant_eagle.lore: Etana, king of Kish, had no heir, and his tale was already old in Mesopotamia when Homer sang. He rescued a great eagle from a pit, and in gratitude it bore him toward heaven upon its back to seek the plant of birth, so high that land and sea dwindled to nothing beneath them. Eagles as great as that one still build their nests above the deepest shafts of the dungeon.

roc_chick.name: roc chick
roc_chick.lore: Sinbad's shipmates, upon his fifth voyage, came to a white dome on an island and broke it open with stones, and they roasted the chick inside, for it was the egg of a roc. Then the parents returned, each bearing a boulder greater than the ship, and sank it. Such chicks as live to be hatched soon stand taller than a horse, and they will eat anything that they can hold down.

roc_adult.name: Adult Roc

carry_off.line: The Roc's talons close on you and it lifts you into the dark!
carry_off.nowhere: It finds nowhere to set you down, and you fall where you were.

roc_adult.lore: With his own turban Sinbad tied himself to the leg of a sleeping roc and so escaped a desert island, for the bird never felt his weight. Marco Polo had word of such a bird from the seas near Madagascar, one strong enough to lift an elephant on high and let it fall to break upon the rocks. Its wings will span a hall from side to side, and when it stoops upon its prey the wind of its coming arrives before it.

stirge_swarm.name: stirge swarm
stirge_swarm.lore: Romans of old feared the strix, a bird of night that slipped into nurseries to drink the blood of infants, and Ovid tells how one was driven from the cradle of the infant prince Proca with a branch of whitethorn. From that bird the stirge has both name and habits, being a bat-winged thing the size of a fist with a beak like an awl. One would be a small nuisance, but stirges are never known to come singly.

tengu_warrior.name: tengu warrior
tengu_warrior.lore: The crow-headed tengu of the mountains of Japan are a proud and quarrelsome people who despise arrogance in everyone but themselves, and there are no finer swordsmen living. Their king, Sojobo, was master to the boy Ushiwakamaru, who in the legend slipped out of his temple on Mount Kurama each night to learn the sword, and who grew to be the great general Minamoto no Yoshitsune. They bear fans of feathers, and with these they can raise a gale.

thunderbird_lesser.name: lesser thunderbird
thunderbird_lesser.lore: Among the peoples of North America, from the Great Lakes to the Pacific coast, they tell of the Thunderbird, whose wingbeat is the thunder and from whose opened eyes the lightning flashes. It makes war without end upon the horned serpents and water panthers of the deep places, and this lesser cousin has followed that war beneath the earth. Sparks creep over its feathers, and at its cry the teeth will rattle in your head.

pixie_swarm.name: pixie swarm
pixie_swarm.lore: Pixy-led was the word in Devon and Cornwall for a traveller who had wandered all night in circles on a moor he knew well, and his cure was to turn his coat inside out. A single pixie is a mischief-maker a finger high, but a swarm is a cloud of them, armed with thorns and with a dust that brings sleep upon the spot, and they have a great dislike of armour and of all who wear it.

redcap.name: redcap
redcap.lore: Along the Scottish Border, in ruined peel towers where blood was shed for centuries, dwells the goblin called the redcap. He is like a short old man, with long teeth, iron-shod boots and a pikestaff, and he keeps his cap red by steeping it in the blood of travellers. Border folk said that no human strength could stop him, but that Scripture or a cross would send him shrieking away. Down here he has grown bolder, and it is better to bring iron.

will_o_wisp_lesser.name: Lesser Will-o'-Wisp
will_o_wisp_lesser.lore: Ignis fatuus, the foolish fire, was its name in Latin, but country people called it Jack of the Lantern, or else Will of the Wisp, after a man named Will who carries a wisp of burning straw. It is a pale flame that bobs over the marsh by night, always a little farther on, until the one who follows is waist deep in the bog. Underground it favours pits for that same mischief, and blades pass through it.

green_hag.name: green hag
green_hag.lore: Jenny Greenteeth was the name by which children in Lancashire were warned away from ponds, for she waited under the duckweed with long arms, and on the River Tees she was Peg Powler of the green hair, whose suds are the froth upon the water. Every green hag is a drowner of that kind. She can wear the look of a kindly old woman, or of a young one, until the moment when her hands close upon you.

spells.name: Evil Eye
spells.cast: {The} fixes you with the evil eye.

spells.name: Vanish
spells.cast: {The} cackles and is gone, four paces off.

sea_hag.name: sea hag
sea_hag.lore: Beowulf dived for most of a day through a haunted mere before he came to the hall of Grendel's mother. The sword that he carried would not bite upon her, and he slew her at last with a blade of giants' forging that hung on her own wall. Sea hags are women of her sort, out of the cold deeps, with the look of the drowned, and their faces are hard to behold and harder afterward to forget.

spells.name: Vanish
spells.cast: {The} cackles and is gone in a smell of brine.

annis_hag.name: annis hag
annis_hag.lore: Black Annis, who dwelt in the Dane Hills near Leicester, had a face of blue and claws of iron. With them she dug herself a cave out of the sandstone, and in the oak at its mouth she crouched to snatch away lambs and children at dusk. Mothers said that the grinding of her teeth was heard from far off, in time for them to bar the door. The annis hags are all of her kind, huge of body and brutally strong.

spells.name: Evil Eye
spells.cast: {The} fixes you with the evil eye.

spells.name: Vanish
spells.cast: {The} cackles and is gone, four paces off.

night_hag.name: night hag
night_hag.lore: Mare was her name among the old Germanic peoples, and it is preserved in our word nightmare. She comes by night to sit upon the sleeper's chest and press out his breath, so that he wakes and can neither move nor cry out. She will ride the same victim night after night until nothing of him is left to ride, and for this cause country people used to keep iron by the bed against her.

spells.name: Nightmare
spells.cast: {The} croons a lullaby of bad dreams.

spells.name: Vanish
spells.cast: {The} cackles and is gone, four paces off.

satyr_trickster.name: satyr trickster
satyr_trickster.lore: Satyrs are the goat-legged following of Dionysus, drinkers and dancers and thieves of all that is left unguarded. Their wild cousin, the god Pan, pursued the nymph Syrinx until she was changed to a stand of reeds, and from those reeds he cut the first panpipes. When a satyr sets such pipes to his lips a traveller's head will spin. He would sooner rob than kill, though he goes laughing to either work.

dryad_guardian.name: dryad guardian
dryad_guardian.lore: Drys is the Greek word for oak, and a dryad's life is bound up with her tree. When King Erysichthon felled an oak in the holy grove of Demeter, the nymph within it cursed him with her last breath, and the goddess sent upon him a hunger that no feast could fill. The guardians have not forgotten that tale. Roots rise up where they point, and they will not wait for the axe to fall before they strike.

leprechaun_hostile.name: hostile leprechaun
leprechaun_hostile.lore: The leprechaun is shoemaker to the fairies of Ireland, found by the tap of his hammer. A man who holds him with his eyes may make him show his gold, but if that man looks away for a moment the leprechaun is gone. A farmer once tied a red garter to the bush that marked the spot and went for a spade, and on his return he found a garter upon every bush in the field. This one has been seized so often that he is weary of it and has turned against all comers.

bargain.line: {The}, cornered, holds up a fat purse: 'Let me go and it's yours!'
bargain.accept_line: {The} tosses the purse at your feet and is gone in a flash of green.
bargain.refuse_line: 'Then you'll get nothing!' {The} squares up to you.

spriggan.name: spriggan
spriggan.lore: Cornish folk held the spriggans to be the ghosts of the giants of old. They have charge of the treasure buried in cairns and hill forts, and though they seem but small and ugly old men, they can swell to a giant's size when the digger's spade strikes stone. They also raise storms over the standing crops and steal whatever is left unwatched, so that the gold they guard is seldom rightfully their own.

boggart.name: boggart
boggart.lore: A boggart so plagued one farmer of Yorkshire, souring his milk and pinching his children, that the weary man loaded his cart to move away. When a neighbour asked if he was leaving, a voice from within the butter churn answered that yes, they were flitting. At that the family unpacked and stayed, for a boggart cannot be left behind. He can only be driven out, and a horseshoe hung over the door is said to help.

water_elemental.name: water elemental
water_elemental.lore: Paracelsus the physician taught that each of the four elements has a people of its own, and the spirits of water he named undines. But the water elemental is the element itself, with none of their manners. It rears out of a flooded hall as a standing wave that has something like a face, falls on its prey with the weight of a river and drags it under. Fire does it but little harm, but lightning runs through every drop of it and does it great harm.

air_elemental.name: air elemental
air_elemental.lore: Since men first felt the wind they have given it names. The Greeks had four, Boreas, Notus, Eurus and Zephyrus, and said that King Aeolus held the rest shut within a cave, and Paracelsus called the spirits of the air sylphs. An air elemental is a whirlwind with a will of its own, quick as a thrown knife and invisible as the wind of which it is made. It is full of grit and splinters that flay whatever it wraps around. You see nothing of it until it has struck you, and even then you see only the dust that it carries.

ice_elemental.name: ice elemental
ice_elemental.lore: Out of ice the world had its beginning, as the Norse told. The rivers from Niflheim froze layer upon layer in the great gap, and where sparks from the realm of fire met the rime, the frost giant Ymir took shape in the thaw. A little of that first cold still walks abroad as the ice elemental. Its touch sheathes a limb in frost, and of all the arguments that may be brought against it, it understands only fire and the hammer.

magma_elemental.name: magma elemental
magma_elemental.lore: Zeus ended his war with the monster Typhon by casting Mount Etna upon him, and the Greeks held that the mountain smokes and burns because Typhon struggles beneath it still. The magma elemental is of such burning stuff, molten rock that has learned to walk. Floors of stone glow where it has trodden and all that it touches burns, and there is nothing but bitter cold that will make it stiffen and crack.

death_throes.line: {The} bursts in a spray of molten rock!

void_elemental.name: void elemental
void_elemental.lore: Ginnungagap, the yawning gap, was all that was before earth and sky, as the Norse poets sang, and in it was neither sand nor sea nor grass, but only emptiness between the ice and the fire. Some scraps of that emptiness were never filled, and these are the void elementals. Each has the look of a hole cut in the air, and whatever light or sound goes into it does not come out again.

shambling_mound.name: shambling mound
shambling_mound.lore: Reeds, creeper and bog moss, all rotting and wound about a living root, make up the shambling mound, which walks upright, knowing no reason why it should not. It smothers what it catches and lets the body rot into its own bulk. Cold does no more than slow that rot, and lightning wakes it, so that a mound struck in a storm rises larger than before, but of fire it is sorely afraid.

assassin_vine.name: assassin vine
assassin_vine.lore: In the branches of another tree the strangler fig of the tropics sprouts, and it sends its roots down about the trunk and squeezes for years, until the host has died and rotted away within a hollow lattice of fig. The assassin vine has not the patience to wait so long. It lies along a wall like any creeper until something warm brushes by, and then it loops and tightens, and by this means its roots are richly fed.

thorn_slinger.name: thorn slinger
thorn_slinger.lore: Narrow places are the chosen ground of the thorn slinger, a squat, pale shrub whose seed pods are packed tight with barbed thorns. A footfall near at hand is enough to make it loose them all together, and the sap that coats them burns in the blood. Having no power to give chase, it plants itself in a doorway and waits until those who travel the dungeon come to it of their own accord.

myconid_worker.name: myconid worker
myconid_worker.lore: Fairy rings were what country folk called the rings of mushrooms in their meadows, where the fair folk were thought to have danced, but beneath the earth the rings get up and walk. The myconid workers are waist-high mushroom folk who tend the fungus beds of their circle and desire only to be left alone. If you crowd one, it will puff out a cloud of spores that fills the head with things that are not there.

death_throes.line: {The} bursts in a cloud of spores!

myconid_sovereign.name: myconid sovereign
myconid_sovereign.lore: What we call a mushroom is only the fruit, for the true body is a web of threads running through the soil, and in the mountains of Oregon a single honey fungus spreads through miles of forest floor as one living thing. At the heart of such a web is the myconid sovereign. Every mushroom in all its caverns is a part of it, and it thinks with all of them at the same time.

death_throes.line: {The} bursts in a great cloud of spores!

yellow_musk_creeper.name: yellow musk creeper
yellow_musk_creeper.lore: Clouds of yellow pollen rise from the musk creeper, and they so overpower the wits of those who breathe them that the victims are drawn helpless into the reach of its grasping tendrils. Thralls without any minds of their own stand guard about it and fetch rotting matter to enrich its roots. The musk alone, without a blow struck, is enough to bring most beasts into a tame and wandering confusion.

gas_spore.name: gas spore
gas_spore.lore: Many a veteran of the dungeon has perished by mistaking a gas spore for a beholder, which this floating pod of fungus much resembles at a glance. If it is punctured anywhere it bursts asunder in a cloud of poisonous spores, and within hours the bodies of those it has slain are hosts to new pods of its kind.

death_throes.line: {The} bursts in a cloud of choking gas!

violet_fungus.name: violet fungus
violet_fungus.lore: Violet of cap and as tall as a child, the violet fungus might be any mushroom of the caves, until its four ropy branches begin to feel about in the dark. Flesh that they touch grows soft and grey, as fruit does around a bruise. It roots where creatures have died and sees to it that there shall be more such deaths, and other fungi grow thick about it to share in the spoil.

pegasus_corrupted.name: corrupted pegasus
pegasus_corrupted.lore: Pegasus sprang from the neck of Medusa when Perseus had cut off her head. Bellerophon tamed him with a golden bridle given by Athena, and where his hoof struck Mount Helicon the spring of the Muses welled up. This winged horse came of that noble line, but some power in the deep found it and darkened it, so that its coat has turned the colour of soot and its hooves leave a chill where they have trodden.

unicorn_corrupted.name: corrupted unicorn
unicorn_corrupted.lore: When a serpent has poisoned a pool, say the old bestiaries, the beasts wait at the brink until the unicorn comes to dip its horn, and the water is made clean. They say also that no hunter can take it, but only a maiden whom it trusts. This one gave its trust and was betrayed, and now its horn is black and twisted and poisons all that it once made pure.

sphinx_lesser.name: lesser sphinx
sphinx_lesser.lore: An avenue of stone sphinxes, hundreds in number, once joined the temples of Karnak and Luxor at Thebes in Egypt, crouched in two facing rows for more than a mile as guardians of the road. The lesser sphinx is a guardian still, with the body of a lion, a sharp tongue and little patience. She will not wait to hear her riddle answered, but uses it to confound the mind, and she quickly wearies of her prey.
sphinx_lesser.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} road and watches you go.

nue.name: nue
nue.lore: The young Emperor Konoe fell sick with terror, for each night a black cloud settled over his palace. So the Tale of the Heike relates, and it tells how the archer Minamoto no Yorimasa shot into the cloud and brought down a beast with a monkey's head, a raccoon dog's body, a tiger's legs and a snake for its tail, and how his retainer I no Hayata made an end of it. That beast was the nue, whose cry is like a thrush calling in the night and brings evil dreams.

peryton.name: peryton
peryton.lore: Jorge Luis Borges set down the legend of the perytons, winged stags in the plumage of birds and exiles from drowned Atlantis, each of which casts the shadow of a man. Only by killing a human being can a peryton win back its own shadow, and this it may do but once. A sibyl, they say, foretold that perytons would bring down Rome. The one that dwells here has yet to make its kill, for its shadow still walks upon two legs.

carbuncle.name: carbuncle
carbuncle.lore: Spanish explorers in Paraguay swore that they had glimpsed the carbuncle at night, a little beast with a jewel in its forehead that shone like a live coal. In 1602 the priest Barco Centenera wrote that he had hunted it through the forests and never laid a hand on one. None could say what the creature looked like, for they had seen only the light, and it is while the eyes are dazzled by that flash that it bites.

sea_dragon_spawn.name: sea dragon spawn
sea_dragon_spawn.lore: Olaus Magnus drew his great map of the northern seas in 1539, and the waters off Norway he filled with serpents coiled about ships, for so the sailors told him they had seen. The young of the sea dragons are hatched in black trenches and come up the flooded rivers into the deep halls. Even one that is half grown can crack a ship's hull, and the water that it spits will strike a man as cold as sleet.

goblin_shaman.name: goblin shaman
goblin_shaman.lore: Whatever goblin has eaten the wrong mushroom, and lived, and come back talking with things unseen, is thereafter the goblin shaman of his band. He wears a mask cut from a great mushroom cap and shakes a rattle of knucklebones, and from well behind his kin he screeches orders and curses in one breath. His hexes are crude, and yet they take hold, and a warband that has a shaman fights twice as boldly as one that has none.

spells.name: Smoke Ward
spells.cast: {The}'s chant ends: greasy smoke wraps about {him}, and blows slide off it.

spells.name: Smoke in the Eyes
spells.cast: {The} flings a pinch of smoke at your face.

goblin_king.name: goblin king
goblin_king.lore: No crown is inherited among the goblins. Whoever outlives every rival becomes the king, and this he commonly contrives by arranging for someone bigger to do the killing. His crown is made of bent copper coins wired together with the teeth of the last king. He rules by the loudness of his voice, and when his shriek goes ringing down three corridors, every goblin who hears it would sooner face a crusader than face the king afterward.

hobgoblin_captain.name: hobgoblin captain
hobgoblin_captain.lore: Hobgoblins drill, where their lesser kin the goblins swarm in disorder. Their captains win that rank upon the battlefield, each promoted over the body of the officer before him, and each bears the banner of his company strapped to his back, that the line may always know where to form. A captain makes no headlong charge. He sends two soldiers around the flank and waits until retreat has been cut off, and only then does he advance behind his shield.

hobgoblin_warlord.name: hobgoblin warlord
hobgoblin_warlord.lore: The warlord of the hobgoblins governs by a soldier's code, and one law in it stands above the rest, that the coward shall die first, and by the hand of his own captain. Every plate of his armour carries a trophy of some enemy whom he slew himself, for he holds that trophies taken by others are of no account. He has read the ground before ever battle is joined, and at his roar a wavering line will stand once more like a wall.

bugbear.name: bugbear
bugbear.lore: A 'bug' in Middle English was a goblin or bogey, such as nurses named to frighten children into bed, and thus the bugbear has lent his name to every nameless dread. The creature himself is seven feet of fur and muscle, and yet he walks without a sound. He likes his prey to be afraid before he takes it, and a corridor that has suddenly grown quiet is all the warning that he will give.

bugbear_chieftain.name: bugbear chieftain
bugbear_chieftain.lore: At the belt of a bugbear chieftain hang the skulls of all who challenged him, and among them is that of the chieftain before him. By this means he holds his land, and the lesser monsters round about pay him tribute in meat and keep out of his path. He fights with a spiked morningstar and begins with a roar to freeze the blood, for he is too lazy to give chase and knows that a frightened enemy is the slower.

orc_berserker.name: orc berserker
orc_berserker.lore: Berserkir was the Norse name for warriors who fought in a trance and bit the rims of their shields, and who were said to feel neither fire nor iron, and the orc warbands have kept both the word and the custom. Their berserker goes in first, alone and howling, with no shield and no thought of coming back. A few heartbeats afterward the rest of the band comes pouring into whatever gap he has torn.

orc_warchief.name: orc warchief
orc_warchief.lore: None is born a warchief among the orcs. Any warrior of the band may challenge for the title, whereupon the two fight to the death and the winner keeps the loser's hammer. He who bears it now has answered that challenge many times over. Orcs despise clever tactics as the work of cowards, yet a warchief lays his ambushes with true cunning, though he will give them no other name than hunting.

bandit_captain.name: bandit captain
bandit_captain.lore: Soldiering was the bandit captain's trade until he judged that the pay was better on the other side of the law. Now he has claimed a stretch of corridor for a toll road, and he takes his due in coin or in blood. He makes no show in his fighting, but picks out the most dangerous of his opponents and puts a thrown dagger into that one before he closes with the sword.

dark_cultist.name: dark cultist
dark_cultist.lore: For the service of a thing that whispers from below, the dark cultist gave up name, family and trade. The little ritual that he has learned is enough to make a prayer bite like a blade, and upon his knife is a curse that clouds the eyes. He hunts for relics on his master's behalf and counts his own life a small price, though he knows full well that heaven is closed to him.

spells.name: Whispered Dread
spells.cast: {The} whispers what waits for you below.

mercenary_veteran.name: mercenary veteran
mercenary_veteran.lore: The veteran has outlived three paymasters and most of his company besides. He has no cause and bears no grudge, but stands in this place because someone in the deep pays him in gold. His sword is plain and his shield is dented, yet in thirty years he has learned exactly where a guard will open, so that he wastes no stroke, and he will not pursue any fight that he sees he cannot win.

battle_mage.name: battle mage
battle_mage.lore: To make one tenth of the wizard's art swift, the battle mage has thrown the other nine tenths away. Down both his arms run tattooed channels, inked so that fire or frost may leave his hand in the time it takes to point, and as the inking was painful, so is every casting. He wears little armour and keeps his distance from all enemies, knowing that at close quarters he is no more than a scholar with sore arms.

spells.name: Arcane Shield
spells.cast: {The}'s chant ends: a shimmer of force wraps about {him}.

hill_giant.name: hill giant
hill_giant.lore: Smallest and dullest of giantkind are the hill giants, though even they stand twice the height of a tall man and can throw a boulder the size of a barrel. They den in caverns and eat what they catch, and their hoards are sorted by no rule, save whether a thing is shiny, or big, or fit to eat. It is rare for a hill giant to bear malice toward those he falls upon, for he is driven only by a hunger that never leaves him.

stone_giant.name: stone giant
stone_giant.lore: Grey as the rock in which they live, the stone giants can stand so still that travellers walk past and suppose them part of the wall. They are carvers, and whole galleries of the deep caverns are covered with their slow and patient reliefs. For the sunlit world they have only contempt, and whoever climbs down out of it they hold to be a trespasser, to be answered with a thrown boulder.

cloud_giant.name: cloud giant
cloud_giant.lore: Jack climbed his beanstalk to a giant's castle in the sky, and in this the old tale spoke truly, for the cloud giants build their halls upon the heads of the storms. From that height they look down upon the folk below, both with their eyes and in their hearts. The few who are met underground are exiles, or seekers after some ancient treasure, and they are too proud to heed small creatures until one gets in their way.

storm_giant.name: storm giant
storm_giant.lore: Thunder comes with every stroke of a storm giant's sword, for these are the greatest of giantkind, and they keep the weather as lesser lords keep hounds. So long are their lives that they remember the first digging of these halls and speak of it as of a thing done lately. What brings such a one into the deep is known to himself alone, and it would be most unwise to ask him a second time.

cyclops_brute.name: cyclops brute
cyclops_brute.lore: Polyphemus the shepherd was the most famous of the one-eyed race. He devoured six of the crew of Odysseus, and was blinded by that hero with a sharpened olive stake as he slept off the wine. The brutes below keep no flocks and have not even such manners as his. One eye is a poor judge of distance and their thrown boulders often go astray, but at arm's length their fists do not miss their mark.

two_headed_ogre.name: two-headed ogre
two_headed_ogre.lore: One body serves the ogre's two heads, and they agree in nothing, whether it be which way to walk, whose turn it is to sleep or who shall have the first bite. But when anything fit to eat walks in, the quarrel ceases. Each head takes charge of an arm and a club, and he who could not decide upon his supper fights like two ogres standing in one place. At every hour, moreover, one of those heads is keeping watch.

ice_troll.name: ice troll
ice_troll.lore: Mountain and frost were the home of trolls in the tales of the Norse, and this breed has held fast to the cold, haunting flooded caverns where the meltwater runs in from the glaciers. His flesh when cut will close again before the swordsman's eyes, and his claws leave frostbite where they fall. Fire was ever the answer to a troll and it is the right one still, for a wound that has been burned remains burned.

drow_warrior.name: drow warrior
drow_warrior.lore: In cities that have never seen the sun the dark elves trained this warrior from his cradle. He bears a short, light blade, beautifully made, but the weapon to fear is the little crossbow in his other hand. Its bolts are tipped with a venom of sleep, for the dark elves have far greater need of captives for their mines and their altars than they have of corpses.

drow_mage.name: drow mage
drow_mage.lore: Shadow, in a city that has no daylight, is the very stuff out of which things are wrought, and the mages of the dark elves spend centuries in learning to shape it. They make of it bolts that blind, and pale fires that drift and cling about an enemy until his wits are muddled. Their spellbooks are written in silver ink upon black pages, and scholars of the upper world will pay dearly to possess one.

spells.name: Shadow Step
spells.cast: {The} steps into a shadow and out of another, four paces off.

drow_priestess.name: drow priestess
drow_priestess.lore: Priestesses bear rule among the dark elves, and all others obey them. This one serves a spider goddess who rewards treachery and punishes failure, and she carries a whip whose lashes are living snakes. Her blessing can raise a household to power in a season and her curse can end a bloodline in a night, and though she has bestowed both, it is in the curse that she has taken the greater pleasure.

spells.name: Spider's Hold
spells.cast: {The}'s prayer ends, and threads you cannot see bind your legs.

minotaur_warrior.name: minotaur warrior
minotaur_warrior.lore: Descended from the first Minotaur, who was a prisoner of the Labyrinth, the minotaur warriors have made of the maze a fortress. Such a one can never be lost underground, and he uses that gift without mercy, for he will give ground down a side passage, go about in a circle and come upon his enemy from behind. He fights with the double axe after the manner of Crete, and he finishes the work with his horns.

young_black_dragon.name: young black dragon
young_black_dragon.lore: Swamps and drowned cellars are the lairs of black dragons, which spit acid where their cousins breathe fire, and even a young one has the full measure of that family's spite. It likes to hold its prey under the water until the struggling stops, and then to leave the meal to soften. Already it has begun to count coins, for every hoard must have a beginning, and it will gladly make a start with an adventurer's purse.
young_black_dragon.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} hoard and watches you go.

young_red_dragon.name: young red dragon
young_red_dragon.lore: All things under the sky, as red dragons believe, are their own and are merely lent to others. A young one has the whole of that pride and only a part of the size. The heat of its lair can be felt from two rooms away, and the stone about its bed has melted and set again like wax. It looks for tribute from all who come there, and if none is offered it takes it by force.
young_red_dragon.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} hoard and watches you go.

adult_blue_dragon.name: adult blue dragon
adult_blue_dragon.lore: Order is dear to blue dragons, though justice is not. An adult maintains a web of servants, spies and tributaries, each in his appointed place, and it takes any disturbance of that order for an insult to itself. Lightning is its breath, a single white stroke that leaps from one armoured body to the next. It plans every battle beforehand, and you may be sure that it has already planned the battle it will fight with you.

adult_red_dragon.name: adult red dragon
adult_red_dragon.lore: Greed, pride and cruelty have come to their full growth in the adult red dragon. For centuries it has stripped the lands about it, and it sleeps upon the spoil, a bed of coin and plate deep enough to drown in, of which it knows every piece. The dragon in Beowulf burned a kingdom for the theft of a single cup, and this one would do the same without pausing to think upon it.

drake_fire.name: fire drake
drake_fire.lore: Fire drakes are the poor relations of dragons, having four legs, a furnace in the belly and no more wit than a mastiff. They hunt and eat and sleep upon whatever glitters. Their spittle is a gobbet of burning pitch, far short of a true dragon's breath, though it will set a cloak or a rope bridge alight. Stronger monsters keep them as watchdogs and feed them upon trespassers.

drake_cold.name: frost drake
drake_cold.lore: Down where the glaciers press in upon the deep levels the frost drake has its home, and the rime never melts from its scales. It clings to the ceiling above a passage and breathes down a freezing fog, and then it drops upon whatever has ceased to move. Its lair is easily known, for the walls are glazed with ice, and the meals of a month ago may be seen standing in them like flies in amber.

yuan_ti_pureblood.name: yuan-ti pureblood
yuan_ti_pureblood.lore: The snake god of the serpent folk died long ago, but his death has troubled their faith not at all, and they worship him still. Those among them who are called purebloods pass at a glance for human, and only a patch of scales at the neck or a slow, unblinking stare betrays them. They join caravans and companies of delvers as guides, and every word that they hear they carry back to the temple.

wyvern_greater.name: greater wyvern
wyvern_greater.lore: Two legs, two wings and a barbed tail are the marks by which heralds know the wyvern, whereas a true dragon goes upon four legs. It has no breath to use as a weapon and feels no lack of one, for the wings of a greater wyvern can fill a corridor from wall to wall, and the sting at the end of its tail swings over its back like a scorpion's, bearing venom enough to stop the heart of a horse.

naga_guardian.name: naga guardian
naga_guardian.lore: Hooded like cobras and wise as kings are the nagas of the old stories of India, serpent lords who guard treasure and sacred waters. This one was set over some vault or tomb centuries ago, and since that day it has never left its post. There is no stone of the place that it does not know, and it looks upon any stranger there as a householder looks upon a thief.

shadow_master.name: shadow master
shadow_master.lore: Hunger without a mind is all that a common shadow is, but the shadow master has drained so many of the living that it remembers, dimly and wrongly, that it once had a name, and the memory has taught it patience. It glides along the unlit side of a corridor like a fish through water and strikes from behind, and at its touch strength and warmth depart together. Torchlight and holy things, however, will drive it back.

void_crawler.name: void crawler
void_crawler.lore: Things come through where great magic has worn the world thin, and one of them is the void crawler.
