Its many-limbed shape is never wholly present, so that a sword will pass through an arm that was there a moment before. To be near it bends the senses, and those it touches see doors that are not there as clearly as they see their own friends. While they stand staring, unable to tell false from true, it feeds.

ruinous_djinn.name: ruinous djinn
ruinous_djinn.lore: Jinn were created from smokeless fire, say the old Arabian accounts, and the tales add that King Solomon sealed the rebels among them in vessels of brass and cast them into the sea. Through all his centuries in the bottle this one was going mad. He is free at last and has no home to which he may return, and therefore he breaks whatever he finds, walls and doors and chains, and anyone who reminds him of a jailer.

undead_colossus.name: undead colossus
undead_colossus.lore: A necromancer once had need of a wall thrown down, and the corpses of giants lay ready to his hand. He stitched their limbs together with ship's cable and burned runes of binding into the hide to hold them, and so the colossus came to be. He spent no care upon it, for he meant it to be used up. It has no thought at all, and it will go on forever obeying the last order that it was given.

elder_werewolf.name: elder werewolf
elder_werewolf.lore: Petronius told of a soldier who turned wolf among the tombstones, and the Greeks held that the first of all such men was King Lycaon, whom Zeus cursed. This one has changed so many times that the man comes back no more. He leads a pack with a soldier's cunning and bites for the hamstring, and when ordinary steel has wounded him the flesh closes behind the blade, but a wound made by silver does not close.

abyssal_champion.name: abyssal champion
abyssal_champion.lore: Champion is a title that demons earn by slaughter, and the price of it is a thousand mortal warriors, each one counted and the weapon of each one kept. The bearer seeks out skilled fighters by design, for a title built on easy victims is worth nothing in the Abyss. Its sword burns with hellfire, and it salutes in mockery before it strikes, but in all its battles it has never yet met the opponent for whom it is searching.

bone_titan.name: bone titan
bone_titan.lore: Several giants' skeletons went to the making of the bone titan, wired bone upon bone until the skull scrapes a thirty-foot ceiling, and the floor shakes as it walks. A necromancer who can raise such a thing will not waste it on a single doorway, but sets it to hold a whole wing of the dungeon. Blades skitter from its ribs and do little hurt, yet a heavy hammer, patiently applied, will take it to pieces.

spectral_lord.name: spectral lord
spectral_lord.lore: There are some among the dead who refuse to depart. The spectral lord was a warlord or an archmage whose ambition outlasted the body, and it has had centuries in which to brood. It wears yet the shape of its armour or its robes, drawn in pale light, through which steel passes as through smoke. The despair of the grave is in its wail, and it holds the living in the same contempt that it felt for them in life.

chaos_troll.name: chaos troll
chaos_troll.lore: Trolls have the gift of healing, but this one dwelt too near a rift, and now the gift works amiss. Where an arm is severed he grows two, and a cloven skull will close about a second face that looks the other way. With every wound he becomes larger and less sane, and his claws carry the same disorder into the mind. Fire and acid will seal his flesh, and there is nothing else that slows him.

wyrm.name: wyrm
wyrm.lore: Wyrm is the oldest word in the English tongue for a dragon, and the Beowulf poet gave it to the guardian of the hoard that slew his hero. It well befits the old and heavy kind found here, serpents grown too vast to fly, who drag their bellies along tunnels that they have worn smooth. They were breathing fire before these halls had doors, and the long ages have but made them better at it.

elder_mind_flayer.name: elder mind flayer
elder_mind_flayer.lore: Robed and shaped like a man, but with the head of an octopus, the mind flayer eats the minds of others. This elder has fed for centuries on scholars, generals and kings, and has kept all that they knew. Its thought strikes like a hammer and leaves the victim unsure of the hour that is past. It holds fighting to be beneath it, so that if ever you find it fighting, something has already moved it to great anger.

void_leviathan.name: void leviathan
void_leviathan.lore: No hook could hold the Leviathan, the sea beast of the Book of Job, but the void leviathan is larger and comes from no sea. It swims in the dark between the worlds and squeezes through wherever magic has torn a hole. Some part of its length is always elsewhere, and therefore neither chain nor ward can bind it. It is drawn to warmth from afar, and swallows down whatever gives out any heat.

elder_beholder.name: elder beholder
elder_beholder.lore: One great eye is set in the beholder's floating orb of flesh, above a mouth full of teeth, and for a crown it has lesser eyes on stalks, in each of which lies a different death. The elder has grown more stalks with age and has learned to use them all at once. It trusts nothing and forgets nothing, and somewhere in its lair there is a careful list of everything it has ever met, set in order by danger and by flavour.

dread_wyrm.name: dread wyrm
dread_wyrm.lore: While this dragon was yet growing something poisoned it, and neither body nor mind was ever finished, so that it has the bulk of a great wyrm and the temper of a hatchling. It knows what it ought to have become, and the knowledge has soured into a rage that burns hotter than the fire of any dragon in health. None may bargain with it, for nothing has ever been found that it desires so greatly as revenge.

abyssal_overlord.name: abyssal overlord
abyssal_overlord.lore: A whole layer of the Abyss is the realm of each overlord, a country of fire and screaming where lesser demons fight one another through eternity, since nothing else is permitted them. When such a lord climbs into the mortal world it brings that country along with it, so that stone runs like wax about its feet and all directions lose their meaning. Of all things upon earth, holy ground alone does not bend before it.

elder_dragon.name: elder dragon
elder_dragon.lore: At five hundred years a dragon has come no further than middle age. An elder has outgrown the rashness of youth and has not yet settled into the long sleep of the truly ancient, and this is therefore the most perilous season of its life. It can lay a town level in an afternoon, and is wise enough to choose that afternoon with care. So old is its hoard that the coins of forgotten kings lie in it.

aura.line: The dread of {the} falls on you like a shadow. You turn to run!

lich_sovereign.name: lich sovereign
lich_sovereign.lore: There was a king who would not die, and he found means to have his wish. He hid his soul in a phylactery beneath the ruins of his old capital, and now as a lich sovereign he rules the dead even as he ruled the living, by ledgers, wherein every intruder is recorded and assessed and a manner of disposal is assigned to him. The crown remains upon the skull, and the court bows down to him as of old.

demon_emperor.name: demon emperor
demon_emperor.lore: Hell has many lords and they are never at peace, and whoever is emperor among them holds the throne by ceaseless war upon rivals and upon the mortal world, and by schemes that are laid across the centuries. One thing is required of every claimant to the title, that it shall have destroyed a civilization with its own hands. This deed the emperor lists among its honours, as a knight might list a tournament he had won.

world_serpent.name: world serpent
world_serpent.lore: Odin threw a serpent into the sea, as the Norse relate, and there it grew until it girdled the whole world and bit upon its own tail. The coils that fill these halls are of that kindred, lying where the foundations of the earth are laid bare, and they are older than any kingdom overhead. Their scales turn a sword as a cliff turns the rain, and when one of them shifts in its sleep the very ground is shaken.

entropy_wraith.name: entropy wraith
entropy_wraith.lore: Even a wraith will wear through if it is left long enough, and what then remains is the entropy wraith, a hole in the shape of a ghost with nothing behind it. It bears no malice, having forgotten how, but all things near it come apart, mortar from stone, colour from cloth and memory from the mind. Behind it follows something older than death, which is the emptiness that was before the first day.

asterion_minotaur.name: Asterion the Minotaur
asterion_minotaur.lore: Asterion, whose name means 'the starry one', was the son of Queen Pasiphae and the white bull of Poseidon. King Minos hid his shame within the Labyrinth that Daedalus built, and fed it with seven youths and seven maidens sent from Athens as tribute, until Theseus put an end to that tribute and found his way out again by Ariadne's thread. In these depths no such thread is easily come by, and the bull-headed prince is hungry still.
asterion_minotaur.enrage_message: Asterion lowers his horns and comes on, and he will hide no longer within the walls.
asterion_minotaur.fury_message: Asterion's breath comes harder and his blows fall heavier, and every moment that this lasts favours the bull.

medusa_gorgon.name: Medusa the Gorgon
medusa_gorgon.lore: Medusa was a mortal woman of great beauty, as Ovid has it, until by Athena's curse her hair became living snakes, and thereafter whoever met her eyes was turned to stone. Perseus came for her with a shield of polished bronze, and watching only her reflection he struck off her head with a curved blade, and the winged horse Pegasus sprang from her blood. Yet her garden of statues grows larger with every year that passes.

fafnir_dragon.name: Fafnir the Dragon
fafnir_dragon.lore: Gold made a dragon of Fafnir, who had been a dwarf. He murdered his father Hreidmar for the cursed treasure of Andvari and lay down upon it, and there his shape was changed. His breath poisoned the heath all about him and his scales turned every edge. But Sigurd dug a pit in the track by which Fafnir went to drink, and as the dragon crawled overhead he drove the sword Gram upward through the soft belly.

fenrir_wolf.name: Fenrir, Wolf of Ragnarok
fenrir_wolf.lore: Fenrir the wolf was Loki's son, and the gods bound him with Gleipnir, a ribbon that the dwarves made of six things which do not exist, among them the sound of a cat's footfall and the roots of a mountain. He would not suffer it unless a god laid a hand within his jaws for a pledge, and this Tyr did, and lost the hand thereby. It is foretold that at Ragnarok the wolf shall swallow Odin himself.

abaddon_destroyer.name: Abaddon the Destroyer
abaddon_destroyer.lore: Two names are given him in Revelation, Abaddon in Hebrew and Apollyon in Greek, and both signify the Destroyer. He is the angel of the bottomless pit and king over the locusts that pour from it when the fifth trumpet sounds, having faces like men, teeth like lions and tails that sting like scorpions. His is the last floor of all, and beyond him there is no deeper place to which you might descend.

arachne.name: Arachne
arachne.lore: Against Athena herself Arachne of Lydia matched her weaving, and Ovid confesses that the goddess could find no flaw in it. What was worse, the tapestry showed the misdeeds of the gods. Athena rent it and struck the weaver with the shuttle, and Arachne was changed into a spider, to hang and spin forever. Her thread is as perfect now as it was then, and she still bears ill will to any who find fault with her work.
arachne.omen: Some weaver has measured every doorway on this floor for a web.

talos.name: Talos
talos.lore: Hephaestus forged Talos of bronze to be the warder of Crete, and three times a day the giant ran about the island, hurling rocks at any ship that drew near. A single vein went from his neck down to his ankle, and it was closed with one bronze nail. When the Argonauts came there Medea laid a spell upon him, so that the nail came out and all his ichor poured away like molten lead.
talos.omen: The floor is warm along a path that circles the level, as though some heavy thing walks its rounds there.

echidna.name: Echidna
echidna.lore: Half fair-cheeked nymph and half speckled serpent was Echidna, in Hesiod's telling, and she dwelt in a cave beneath the earth and never grew old. By Typhon she bore the most dreadful brood in all the tales of the Greeks, Cerberus and the Lernaean Hydra, the Chimera and the two-headed hound Orthrus, and most of her children fell to Heracles. But the mother of monsters lives on in these depths, and she has not left off nesting.
echidna.omen: The walls here are scored with claw marks of a dozen different shapes.

erlking.name: Erlking
erlking.lore: A father rode hard through the night with his fevered son in his arms, as Goethe sang in his ballad. The boy saw in the mist a crowned figure who whispered of games and golden robes, but the father saw only fog and willows, and when they reached home the child was dead. The Erlking makes his offers yet in that soft voice, and cold iron is as hateful to him as ever it was.
erlking.omen: A child's voice calls out of the dark, and a man's voice sweetly answers it.

camazotz.name: Camazotz
camazotz.lore: The Hero Twins had to pass a night in the House of Bats in Xibalba, as the Popol Vuh of the K'iche' Maya relates, and they hid inside their blowguns. But Hunahpu put out his head to see whether the dawn had come, and Camazotz, the death bat, took it off at the neck, and the lords of the underworld hung it in their ball court. Now he has come hunting in these halls for another head.
camazotz.omen: Out of the light, some large thing shifts upon the ceiling and then is still.

cacus.name: Cacus
cacus.lore: Cacus the fire-breather, as Virgil sings, was a son of Vulcan, and he lived in a cave of the Aventine Hill with the heads of his victims hung about its door. He stole the cattle of Hercules and dragged them in by their tails, that the tracks might point the wrong way, but their lowing betrayed him. Then Hercules tore the roof from the hill, plunged down through the smoke and strangled the thief.
cacus.omen: Hoof prints in the dust point backwards, away from the place where the cattle went.

the_sphinx.name: The Sphinx
the_sphinx.lore: Upon a rock above the road sat the Sphinx of Thebes, who had a woman's face, a lion's body and an eagle's wings. She asked each traveller what goes on four legs at morning, on two at noon and on three at evening, and those who could not say she devoured. When Oedipus gave her the answer she cast herself from the cliff, but in the time since then she has learned harder riddles than that one.
the_sphinx.omen: Answers are scratched upon the wall here, and every one has been crossed out.

rangda.name: Rangda
rangda.lore: Rangda is the widow-witch of Bali, with wild white hair, tusks and a tongue that hangs to her waist. The leyaks, sorcerers who fly by night, obey her commands, and she wages a duel without end against Barong, the lion-like guardian of the villages. In the temple dance her spell turns the warriors' own daggers against them, and since neither side ever wins, the dance must always begin anew.
rangda.omen: Offerings of rice and flowers lie rotting at every corner of this floor.

nemean_lion.name: Nemean Lion
nemean_lion.lore: Hercules had for his first labour the slaying of the Nemean Lion. His arrows glanced from its golden hide and his sword bent upon it, so he drove the beast into its cave, blocked one of the two mouths and choked it with his bare arms, and only its own claws would cut the pelt that he wore ever after. Edges are wasted on such a hide, but a crushing blow will do it grievous harm.
nemean_lion.omen: A broken sword lies by the stairs, bent double, and there is no blood upon it.

baba_yaga.name: Baba Yaga
baba_yaga.lore: Baba Yaga dwells in a hut on chicken legs behind a fence of bones, topped with skulls whose eyes glow by night. Her teeth are of iron, and when she goes abroad she flies in a mortar, rowing with the pestle and sweeping away her trail with a broom. In the Russian tales she will sometimes help a hero who is courteous and finishes her tasks, as Vasilisa did, but those who are rude to her she puts into the oven.
baba_yaga.omen: The floor has been swept clean in one long line, as if by a broom.

jormungandr_juvenile.name: Jörmungandr (Juvenile)
jormungandr_juvenile.lore: Loki's serpent child was cast by Odin into the sea, where it grew until it encircled Midgard and took its own tail in its mouth. Thor hooked it once with an ox head for bait, and the giant Hymir cut the line in terror. At Ragnarok, as the prophecy runs, Thor will slay it at last, walk nine steps and fall dead of its venom. This serpent is but a young one, yet the venom in it is the very same.
jormungandr_juvenile.omen: What seemed a dry riverbed across this floor is a serpent's skin, newly shed.

sets_jackal.name: Set's Jackal
sets_jackal.lore: Set murdered his brother Osiris and scattered the pieces of him across Egypt, and for the throne he strove with Horus through eighty years of trials. He is lord of the red desert, of storms and of strangers. Anubis, the jackal who weighs hearts, guides the dead with care, but the jackals of Set are his dark reflection, rising out of the desert night to hunt the living for their sport.
sets_jackal.omen: Red sand has drifted against the walls, though no desert lies within a hundred floors of this place.

green_knight.name: The Green Knight
green_knight.lore: To Camelot upon a New Year's Day there rode a giant knight, green from his hair to his horse, who offered his own axe to any that would trade blow for blow. Gawain struck off his head, but the knight took it up, reminded Gawain of their meeting appointed for a year thence and rode away. He was Sir Bertilak, enchanted by Morgan le Fay, and whatever bargain he makes he keeps to the letter.
green_knight.omen: Holly grows here out of the bare stone, laden with berries.
green_knight.revive_message: The Green Knight stoops and lifts his head by the hair, and sets it again upon his shoulders. "Now it is my turn."

charybdis.name: Charybdis
charybdis.lore: Over against the cliff of Scylla lies Charybdis, who swallows the sea three times a day and three times spews it back, so that the strait boils like a cauldron. Circe counselled Odysseus to steer for Scylla and lose six men sooner than lose the ship. Yet afterward, alone upon a raft, he was drawn in, and he saved himself by clinging to a fig tree above her mouth until the timbers rose to him again out of the whirl.
charybdis.omen: All the puddles upon this floor lean in one direction.

ravanas_arm.name: Ravana's Arm
ravanas_arm.lore: Ravana, king of Lanka, who carried off Sita the wife of Rama, had ten heads and twenty arms. In the war that came of that deed Rama's arrows struck off his heads and each one grew again, until a weapon given by the gods found his heart. But this one arm did not die with the rest of him. It drags itself along by its fingers, and there is in its grip all the strength that the king once had.
ravanas_arm.omen: Five long furrows are gouged side by side across the floor, wider than a doorway.

wendigo.name: Wendigo
wendigo.lore: In the northern forests the Algonquian peoples tell of the wendigo, who is born when one that is starving eats human flesh in the dead of winter. He is a gaunt giant with a heart of ice, and he grows with every meal, so that his hunger always outruns his feeding and he is never full. Cold walks before him, and it is with fire that the old stories teach men to melt his heart.
wendigo.omen: It is colder here than it should be, and you feel a sharper hunger than you knew upon the stair.

wild_hunt_captain.name: Wild Hunt Captain
wild_hunt_captain.lore: Hounds and horns were heard in the sky on winter nights all across the north, and folk barred their doors. The Germans said that Wotan led those riders, and the English named Herne the Hunter, or old King Herla, who cannot dismount. To see the Hunt was an omen of death, and whoever was caught in its path must ride with it thereafter. Its captain has sounded his horn already, and the chase is begun.
wild_hunt_captain.omen: A horn sounds very far off, and then again, somewhat nearer.

anansi.name: Anansi
anansi.lore: Anansi the spider desired all the stories of the world, and for them Nyame the Sky God asked a price that none could pay: Onini the python, Osebo the leopard, the Mmoboro hornets and a fairy that no one could see. He caught all four by talk and trickery, and from that time the Akan have called every tale a spider story. He does not fight fairly, nor has he ever had need to do so.
anansi.omen: A thread is stretched across the stair at your ankle, and it hums as you step over it.

nidhoggr_fragment.name: Níðhöggr Fragment
nidhoggr_fragment.lore: Beneath that root of Yggdrasil which reaches to the spring Hvergelmir lies Níðhöggr, gnawing, and up and down the trunk runs the squirrel Ratatoskr, bearing insults between the dragon and the eagle at the top. When Ragnarok is past, the seeress of the Voluspa beholds him flying still with corpses beneath his wings. Even this fragment of him has patience enough to gnaw its way through anything in the world.
nidhoggr_fragment.omen: Roots as thick as pillars come down through the ceiling, and some creature has been gnawing them.

seal_demon_wrath.name: Amon, Demon of Wrath
seal_demon_wrath.lore: Amon is written in the old grimoires as a Marquis of Hell, a wolf with a serpent's tail who vomits flame and has forty legions at his command. He stirs up feuds and, when it pleases him, mends them again. Abaddon set him at the First Seal, knowing that nothing which is kept in anger will ever leave willingly. His body smoulders like a banked forge, and his fists come down white with heat.
seal_demon_wrath.enrage_message: Amon's flame turns from red to white, and now he holds back nothing of his wrath.
rage_messages: The air about Amon grows too hot to breathe.

seal_demon_pestilence.name: Buer, Demon of Pestilence
seal_demon_pestilence.lore: Fifty legions serve Buer, a President of Hell, who teaches philosophy and the virtues of every herb, as the grimoires say, and is shown in an old engraving as a lion's head ringed by five goat legs, rolling like a wheel. But the learning of a physician may be turned to harm as well as to healing, and he that knows which leaf will cure a fever knows also which will kindle one. Such is the demon that guards the Second Seal.

seal_demon_famine.name: Mammon, Demon of Famine
seal_demon_famine.lore: The Gospel warns that no one can serve both God and mammon, a word that in Aramaic means only wealth, and the writers of the Middle Ages made of it Mammon, a prince of Hell and the demon of avarice. He guards the Third Seal as famine, which is the other face of greed, when the granary stands locked while the village starves. Bread turns stale in his presence and strength ebbs out of the arms, and he can never be satisfied.

seal_demon_war.name: Bael, Demon of War
seal_demon_war.lore: First among the kings of Hell in the Lesser Key of Solomon stands Bael, ruler of the east and master of sixty-six legions, who appears with the heads of a man, a toad and a cat. He speaks in a hoarse voice, and he can teach a man to walk unseen. He holds the Fourth Seal in plate of iron that was hammered from the swords of the fallen, and never in any battle has he yielded up the field.

seal_demon_death.name: Samael, Demon of Death
seal_demon_death.lore: Venom of God is the meaning of Samael's name. The old tales of the rabbis make him the angel of death, who stands at the bedside with a drop of gall upon the point of his sword, and their tradition never wholly settled whether he fell. Abaddon has settled it for him and bound him to the Fifth Seal, and his touch is as cold as a grave that was dug for one person and no other.

seal_demon_earthquake.name: Beleth, Demon of the Earthquake
seal_demon_earthquake.lore: Trumpets sound before Beleth, a king of Hell, as he rides upon a pale horse with eighty-five legions at his back, and the grimoires give warning that he arrives in fury. It is written in Revelation that when the Sixth Seal opens there is a great earthquake, the sun turns black as sackcloth and the moon becomes like blood. Beleth carries that hour with him wherever he goes, and the floor is split asunder where his horse treads.

seal_demon_silence.name: Abyzou, Demon of Silence
seal_demon_silence.lore: Sleep never comes to Abyzou, who wanders the world out of envy, and the Testament of Solomon tells how that king had her hung by her hair before the Temple. Of the Seventh Seal it is written in Revelation that when it opened there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. That seal is now in her keeping, and in the stillness that surrounds her prayers and spells alike die before they can be spoken.

abyssal_locust.name: abyssal locust
abyssal_locust.lore: John beheld them rising out of the smoke of the pit, locusts shaped like horses armed for battle, with faces like men, hair like women, teeth like lions, and wings that sounded like chariots charging. They were told to harm no green thing, but only people, and Abaddon is their king. A single one would be a small affliction, but it is never one at a time that they come.

heavenly_angel.name: heavenly angel
heavenly_angel.lore: Called down by the Scales of Michael, an angel of the heavenly host comes in a column of white light and wastes neither word nor movement. He has but one errand, which is to meet the locusts of the pit, one for one, and burn them out of the world. Where angel and locust touch, both vanish together in holy fire, and afterward the air is sweet with the smell of rain.

hell_bovine.name: Hell Bovine
hell_bovine.lore: Beyond the veil there lies a pasture where the grass is ash and the cattle walk upon their hind legs. A hell bovine stands as tall as a man and grips a rough halberd between its fore hooves, with more skill than a creature without thumbs has any right to. It lowers its horns before it charges. What the herd desires no one has ever learned, for there is only one thing that it ever says. Moo.

cow_king.name: Cow King
cow_king.lore: Over that herd a king is set. His horns are gilded and his cape was once of royal purple, and he rules the hell bovines of the secret pasture with an iron hoof. Adventurers whisper that to slay him brings terrible luck, and that everyone does it anyway. He leads the stampede from the front, so that the ground shakes before he comes in sight. Moo.

skeleton_champion.name: skeleton champion
skeleton_champion.lore: There were warriors of old who drilled so long that their lessons sank into the bone. Such a champion, when it has died and been raised and stripped of all else, remembers every parry and cut that ever it learned, with neither fear nor weariness to spoil them. Arrows rattle through its ribs, but a mace is the proper weapon against it, for bone that cannot bleed may yet be broken.

dire_wolf_alpha.name: dire wolf alpha
dire_wolf_alpha.lore: The dire wolf is no beast of fable. Heavier than any wolf now living, with jaws made to crack bone, it hunted once in the world above, and thousands perished in the tar pits of La Brea, lured thither by trapped prey. In the deep places the breed never died out, and the alpha, as high as a pony at the shoulder, leads its pack through the tunnels by scent alone, in utter darkness and without a sound.

troll_brute.name: troll brute
troll_brute.lore: Among trolls the brute is reckoned very great of body and very small of wit, and he brings but one thought to battle, which is to strike heavily. His wounds heal faster than those of his lesser cousins, so that a gash closes in moments and a severed hand has grown again within the hour. Fire and acid give the only hurts he cannot mend, and he has learned to fear a torch and little else.

elder_basilisk.name: elder basilisk
elder_basilisk.lore: Pliny wrote of the basilisk as the king of serpents, crowned with a white mark, and told how a horseman once speared one, and the venom ran up the lance and slew both the rider and his horse. This elder has grown as great as an ox. Whatever limb it bites will stiffen and turn grey, and about its lair stands a ring of statues that no carver ever made, since all of them were living once.

greater_earth_elemental.name: greater earth elemental
greater_earth_elemental.lore: From the deepest strata, where the rock has never seen the light, this elemental was summoned, and it rises out of the floor in the rough likeness of a man, with boulders for fists, a slab for a breast and gravel grinding in every joint. Swords are notched upon it, and lightning runs harmlessly through it to the ground. But the miners know its bane, for whatever a pick and a sledge can do to a quarry face they can do to this also.

fungal_horror.name: fungal horror
fungal_horror.lore: A patch of mould upon a dead adventurer was the beginning of this horror, and it has fed and spread without ceasing ever since. Now the colony fills a whole chamber and thinks its slow thoughts, and it can move when it chooses. It breathes out clouds of spores that sicken the lungs, and afterward it settles over the fallen to digest them at its leisure, but like every dry growth it burns very readily.

corrosive_ooze.name: corrosive ooze
corrosive_ooze.lore: Those who have met the corrosive ooze describe a heap of grey-green slime that hisses upon the floor and feeds first on metal, so that a sword left in it for a few breaths is drawn out pitted and thin, and mail fares no better. Having neither eyes nor front nor any fear, it flows toward whatever is warm, and veterans go against it with torches, or with some weapon that they can bear to lose.

orc_warlord.name: orc warlord
orc_warlord.lore: Where a warchief commands one warband, the warlord commands the horde, and to his single banner every band and chief is sworn by fear and by love of plunder. He has fought in hundreds of battles and bears the scars of most. His armour was forged from the melted weapons of enemies whom he slew, and it gains another plate with each victory. When he lifts up his war cry, ten thousand feet begin to march.

veteran_knight.name: veteran knight
veteran_knight.lore: He took his vows in youth and has kept perhaps the half of them, and now, after thirty years of campaigning, all who rode out with him are dead. The wars have left him masterwork plate, an arm that does not tire and no illusions whatever. He lets each edge slide from his armour and saves his own strokes for the gaps in other men's, but a hammer troubles him more than any blade.

greater_fire_elemental.name: greater fire elemental
greater_fire_elemental.lore: Twice the height of a man stands this pillar of living flame, and the heart of it is as white as a forge under the full blast of the bellows. Where it lingers, the stone slumps and runs, and blades pass through it and come out glowing, having cut but little. There is no hatred in it, since burning is the whole of its nature, and nothing diminishes it so swiftly as cold.

chimera_alpha.name: chimera alpha
chimera_alpha.lore: Homer sang of the Chimera as a lion before, a serpent behind and a goat in the midst, breathing terrible fire. Bellerophon slew the first of that name from the back of Pegasus, and some say that he lodged a lump of lead in her throat, so that her own flame melted it. This one has lived long enough to grow to a monstrous size, and in that time her heads have learned to take turns in battle.

bone_colossus.name: bone colossus
bone_colossus.lore: Hundreds of dead soldiers went to the making of the bone colossus. The necromancer did not trouble to sort them, so that it has skulls for knuckles and shinbones for fingers, and whole ribcages are packed into its breast like kindling. It walks with the sound of hail upon a roof, and it flings at its foes the small bones that shake loose at every stride. Spears and arrows can do little against it, but hammers will break it apart.

demon_knight.name: demon knight
demon_knight.lore: This knight was a paladin until, on the worst night of his life, he knelt to pray in the wrong chapel and rose with hellfire running down his blade. Nothing of his long training has left him, neither the footwork nor the guard nor the patience behind the shield. His faith alone is gone, and in its place he has set a hatred of all who kept theirs, but holy water will still blister his armour.

gelatinous_titan.name: gelatinous titan
gelatinous_titan.lore: A gelatinous cube is a clear and quivering block that sweeps a corridor clean of all that lives. This one has fed so long that it fills the passage from wall to wall and from floor to ceiling, with old swords and skeletons hung within it like fruit in aspic. The eye can scarcely find it until it is very near, and whatever it touches grows numb and is afterward dissolved.

phase_spider_matriarch.name: phase spider matriarch
phase_spider_matriarch.lore: Other spiders must travel by length, breadth and height, but the phase spider knows a fourth road, by which it steps out of the world, walks unseen about its prey and steps in again behind, with fangs already bared. The matriarch has hunted so for centuries and has hung her webs on both sides of the veil. Her venom is swift in its working, but fire will clear away her silk and put her to flight.

manticore_elder.name: manticore elder
manticore_elder.lore: Ctesias the Greek, physician at the court of Persia, described this beast, whose name in old Persian means man-eater. It has a lion's body the colour of cinnabar, a man's face with three rows of teeth, and a tail that shoots spines like arrows. An elder bears dozens of them, and each grows again when it is spent. It likes best to slay from a distance and draws near only when it would feast.

war_troll.name: war troll
war_troll.lore: Someone in an older day conceived the thought of setting trolls in an army, and so the war trolls came to be. They are bred for size and drilled until they will hold a line, and plates of iron are bolted straight through their hides, for the flesh heals about the bolts in a single night. They carry clubs studded with nails, and a troll whom no common wound can slay makes a soldier beyond price, so long as none upon the field has fire.

frost_giant_jarl.name: frost giant jarl
frost_giant_jarl.lore: Out of Ymir the ice-giant sprang the jotnar of Jotunheim, whom the Norse called frost giants, and they have been at war with the gods since the world began. A jarl among them is a chieftain, the lord of a hall and a war band. His mail is of glacial iron, blue-black, and his beard is hung with icicles, and the edge of his great axe smokes with a cold so bitter that it kills what it cuts.

fire_giant_king.name: fire giant king
fire_giant_king.lore: Surtr rules over Muspelheim, the land of fire, and the Norse tell that at Ragnarok he shall burn the world with a sword brighter than the sun. Of his kindred is the fire giant king, who holds court at a forge beside the magma, where his skin has been baked as dark and hard as slag. Neither the hammer in his hand nor the breath in his breast has ever been known to cool.

elder_vampire.name: elder vampire
elder_vampire.lore: Austrian army officers once opened graves in Serbian villages and found the dead ruddy and unspoiled, and by their reports the word vampire came into English in the 1730s. This elder is far older than any such report. He keeps the fine manners of a court that has long ceased to be, and he feeds without haste, with all the patience of one who has outlived every hunter sent to destroy him.

death_knight_lord.name: death knight lord
death_knight_lord.lore: For breaking his oath this commander was denied his grave, and he drills in the darkness as he drilled in life, each stroke exact and his armour in parade order over naked bone. The cold upon his blade is the cold of the tomb where he should be lying. He bears the living no hatred, but his orders have never been withdrawn, and he will carry out those orders upon all who come.

arcane_golem.name: arcane golem
arcane_golem.lore: Rabbi Loew of Prague, as Jewish legend relates, shaped a man of river clay and woke it with a holy word, and by rubbing out one letter he turned 'truth' into 'dead' and so stopped it. A later maker learned that craft and none of the reverence. This golem is covered with script that shines whenever it strikes, and there is no one living who remembers which letter must be erased.

abyssal_hound.name: abyssal hound
abyssal_hound.lore: Long of leg and black as a burnt beam are the hunting dogs of the pit, and embers show between their teeth. They run in packs and bring down their quarry as wolves bring down an elk, one going before to hold its eyes while the others close upon the flanks. Hellfire is in their bite, and nothing will turn them aside but cold and consecrated ground.

dread_sphinx.name: dread sphinx
dread_sphinx.lore: Upon a rock outside Thebes sat the Sphinx of old and strangled every traveller who failed her riddle, until Oedipus answered 'Man' and she cast herself from the cliff. The dread sphinx learned another lesson from that tale, and she waits no longer for any answer. Her riddles cling in the mind like burrs until the hearer is unsure of his own name, and then her lion's claws finish what they began.

lich_lord.name: lich lord
lich_lord.lore: Koschei the Deathless, as the Russian tales have it, hid his death within a needle, the needle in an egg, the egg in a duck and the duck in a hare, and locked all in a chest beneath an oak. In like manner the lich lord hid his soul, and he has had centuries in which to better the hiding. What walks these halls is but a robed skeleton, patient as a scholar, whose touch takes all movement from the limbs.

corrupted_treant.name: corrupted treant
corrupted_treant.lore: This treant was once a shepherd of the forest, slow to wrath and older than the kingdoms above, until the water at its roots was poisoned and the rot rose through the heartwood into its very thought. Now its bark is hard and black, and its roots grope beneath the flagstones for the ankles of those who pass. Clubs and arrows barely mark it, but an axe will bite, and fire will serve better still.

skeleton_horde.name: skeleton horde
skeleton_horde.lore: Dozens who fell in one lost battle have risen together, and they keep their formation still. Shoulder to shoulder they advance as a rattling wall of rust and bone, while the rear ranks cast the splintered ribs of the fallen over the heads of the foremost. An arrow will pass between their ribs, but they have no defence against a heavy mace, nor against a prayer.

spectral_dragon.name: spectral dragon
spectral_dragon.lore: When a dragon dies upon its hoard and will not let it go, the fury may outlast the flesh, and there remains a pale shape of wings and jaws with cold fire behind the ribs. That breath scorches no skin, for what it burns is the part of a man in which his hope is kept, and the claws of such a spirit pass through a shield as though it were only mist.

demon_captain.name: demon captain
demon_captain.lore: By outliving those set above it, and by arranging the deaths of a few, this captain rose through the lower hosts. Its blade was forged in the pit and has not yet cooled, and it fights like a veteran, wasting no motion and indulging no pride. Lesser fiends obey it out of fear, and for no better reason it renders obedience to its own masters.

iron_sentinel.name: iron sentinel
iron_sentinel.lore: Dwarven smiths built the iron sentinels to stand at their vault doors and ask no wages, and within each iron shell gears as fine as any watchmaker's turn upon a core that has not run down in a thousand years. All the dwarves who held the passwords are dust, yet the sentinel asks for them still, in a voice like a rusted hinge, and it holds silence to be the wrong answer.

ancient_vampire_lord.name: ancient vampire lord
ancient_vampire_lord.lore: Ages before any spoke the word vampire, the Greeks dreaded the lamia and the Romans the strix, creatures of the night that drank the blood of sleepers, and this lord claims to remember the coining of both those names. His hunting ground was his own before the first chronicle was written. He looks upon crusaders as a lord of the manor looks upon poachers, and he will punish their trespass in his own person.

elder_storm_giant.name: elder storm giant
elder_storm_giant.lore: Above the clouds the eldest storm giants had their halls and settled their quarrels with thunder, but this one came down long ago for reasons that he does not share. Lightning creeps over his skin like St. Elmo's fire upon a mast, and the whole of its charge is gathered into his hammer. When he does no more than clap his hands, the blast of it can cast a knight to the ground.

primordial_fire_elemental.name: primordial fire elemental
primordial_fire_elemental.lore: Heraclitus of Ephesus taught that the world is an ever-living fire, kindled in measure and quenched in measure, and this is some portion of it that was never quenched. It has burned since before there was a hearth to hold it, white at the core and as loud as a furnace. Stone glows where it goes by and all that can take fire is set alight, and deep cold is the one thing from which it will shrink.

primordial_ice_elemental.name: primordial ice elemental
primordial_ice_elemental.lore: Before earth or sky was made there was Niflheim, the world of mist and ice, and its frozen rivers met the sparks of Muspelheim in the great gap, as the Norse poets sang. A piece of that first cold never thawed, and here it walks. The breath freezes in the air around it, torches gutter and armour grows brittle, and a careless hand will lock fast to the hilt of its own sword.

demon_general.name: demon general
demon_general.lore: One step below the princes of the pit stands the demon general, commander of legions and master of sieges that have outlasted most kingdoms. By the long habit of its trade it studies each opponent before it kills him. Its blade burns and its touch rots, and at a word from it the lesser fiends go forward to die. It looks to be obeyed in all things, and in all those wars it has seldom been surprised.

zombie_legion.name: zombie legion
zombie_legion.lore: It was Haitian folk who gave the world the tale of the zombie, a body raised by sorcery and made to labour without rest or will. Here a necromancer has raised a whole graveyard at once and yoked it to a single command. The dead come on in a slow press, too closely packed to fall, and those they cannot claw they bury beneath their weight, and it is fire, or a blessing, or a broad edge that will clear them away.

dracolich.name: dracolich
dracolich.lore: Even a dragon, who may live a thousand years, fears the ending of them, and so this one struck a bargain with necromancers. It drank what they brewed and bound its soul in a hidden vessel while the flesh fell away, and the bones retained both the cunning and the hoard. In place of flame it breathes now a grey and killing mist, and it has all of time in which to make use of it.

mythic_hydra.name: mythic hydra
mythic_hydra.lore: Two heads grew from the Hydra of Lerna for every one that Heracles struck off, until his nephew Iolaus seared the stumps with a burning brand. The last head could not die at all, and that one the hero buried beneath a rock beside the road. This beast is of the same blood and has had centuries in which to grow, so that its heads strike from every side, and one among them spits acid.

corrupted_angel.name: corrupted angel
corrupted_angel.lore: When the tail of the dragon swept a third of the stars from heaven and cast them down, as Revelation tells, this angel was among them. He kept his sword and his soldier's training, but the light that shone from him of old has soured into a glare that blinds. The cruellest part of his doom is that he remembers what he was, and he shares that torment freely with all whom he meets.

titan.name: titan
titan.lore: The Titans reigned before the Olympians, until Zeus and his brothers had warred on them ten years and the thunderbolts prevailed. Zeus chained the vanquished in Tartarus, as far beneath the earth as earth is beneath the sky, and Hesiod says that a bronze anvil would fall nine days to come there. The dungeon has been dug deep enough to find one of them, and he has not forgotten the lightning that laid him low.

shadow_assassin.name: shadow assassin
shadow_assassin.lore: From Alamut the Old Man of the Mountain sent out his killers with a dagger apiece, and for two centuries princes slept uneasily. This order learned the same trade and went further, for its brethren bartered away their own shadows for the right to walk within them. Nothing is seen of such a killer until the blade arrives, but bright flame leaves him nowhere to stand.

plague_ooze.name: plague ooze
plague_ooze.lore: Into the lower waters of the dungeon the plague pits drain, and from what ran out of them this thing has gathered itself, coloured like a bruise and moving against the slope like spilled oil. Metal pits and leather rots at its touch, and those it brushes sicken within the hour. It has neither eyes nor malice but only hunger, and it may be dried by fire or cracked by frost.

death_throes.line: {The} bursts in a spray of plague!

abyssal_behemoth.name: abyssal behemoth
abyssal_behemoth.lore: In the Book of Job it is written of Behemoth that his bones are like bars of iron and his tail sways like a cedar. The pit bred its own answer to that beast and set it to the breaking of walls. It is as great as a gatehouse and plated in scorched hide, the fire of its breath turns mortar to slag, and whole armies have been routed by the mere sound of its tread.

arch_lich.name: arch-lich
arch_lich.lore: Few sorcerers achieve the rite that makes a lich, and fewer endure so long afterward that they weary of it. Through uncounted centuries the arch-lich has refined a single art, and he has scattered the vessels of his soul so widely that he no longer remembers them all. Spells break against him, his gaze unmakes and his touch stills the limbs, and he holds all visitors to be an interruption of his studies.

spells.name: Grave-Hold
spells.cast: {The} speaks one cold word, and your limbs lock.

elder_dracolich.name: elder dracolich
elder_dracolich.lore: Eldest of all the dead dragons is this one, a cathedral of black bone with witchlight in the sockets of its eyes. It was ancient already when it gave up its flesh, and it has been dead far longer than ever it lived. The lesser undead gather to it as courtiers to a king. Its breath is a darkness that lays a curse on whatever survives it, and with its tail it can bring a vaulted roof to the ground.

primordial_titan.name: primordial titan
primordial_titan.lore: First of all things came Chaos, as Hesiod wrote, and after it broad-breasted Earth, whose eldest children were so monstrous that Ouranos their own father hid them away in her depths. To that first brood this titan belongs, who is older than Kronos and was never given a name. He has only the rough shape of a man, and when he stamps his foot the stone rings for a mile about.

void_wyrm.name: void wyrm
void_wyrm.lore: Too far into the dark between the stars this dragon flew, and it brought some of that darkness back with it. Its scales have no colour, but only an absence from which the eye slides away, and instead of fire it breathes a rending wrongness that makes men see what is not there. Its bite steals strength rather than flesh, yet it is solid still to lightning and to a spear-point.

infernal_lord.name: infernal lord
infernal_lord.lore: As a baron holds his fief by oath, tribute and terror, so a lord of the pit holds his, answering to none but the princes. This one has ruled for ages over a province of the damned, and he came up to behold the war with his own eyes. He bears a greatsword wreathed in hellfire and wears his cruelty as openly as a signet, and he sees no need to make haste in anything.

celestial_guardian.name: celestial guardian
celestial_guardian.lore: Cherubim and a flaming sword were set by God east of Eden, as Genesis tells, to guard the way to the tree of life. Guardians of that order stand here before the deepest vaults. They have never fallen and they bear no malice, but their charge is to bar the way, and they will try a crusader's worth with the blade as readily as that of any other.

entropy_elemental.name: entropy elemental
entropy_elemental.lore: All things in the world run down at last, for fires cool, iron rusts and mountains wear away into sand, and here that slow law has put on a shape and learned haste. To the eye it is only a patch of grey and seething air, but whatever it touches ages a century in a breath, so that blades pit, straps crumble and strong arms grow frail. It does all this without hatred, bringing each thing early to its end.

dread_knight_legion.name: dread knight legion
dread_knight_legion.lore: An entire company of oathbreakers was damned together, and it is under discipline still. They ride in a wedge on horses of bone with lances levelled, and the air before them grows cold enough to wither the grass. In life they broke a charge of the faithful, and in death they repeat the deed night after night against anyone who enters their ground, but holy water and fire will scatter their line.

abyssal_dragon.name: abyssal dragon
abyssal_dragon.lore: Stolen as an egg from some dragon's clutch, it was hatched in the pit and reared on brimstone, and it has a dragon's size and greed with a demon's delight in suffering. Its hide is the hue of cooled slag, the fire it breathes is hellfire, its claws are as long as scythes and its bite festers. Saint George would know the shape of it well enough, but he would have small liking for the smell.

flesh_colossus.name: flesh colossus
flesh_colossus.lore: A necromancer who had lost all patience gathered up a battlefield and stitched it into one body, three men high, a patchwork of a thousand soldiers with a dozen faces sunk in its shoulders. It mends its hurts with whatever it slays, pressing in the new flesh as a potter presses clay. It was lightning that first stirred it to move, and lightning will just as readily stop it.

locust_swarmlord.name: locust swarmlord
locust_swarmlord.lore: Out of the smoke of the bottomless pit John saw the locusts rise, shaped like horses armed for battle, with the faces of men and the teeth of lions, and wings that roared like chariots. Abaddon, the angel of the abyss, is their king, and this is one of his captains. When it would call the swarm its jaws ring like a gong, and never yet has the swarm failed to answer that summons.

pit_executioner.name: pit executioner
pit_executioner.lore: Abaddon has his headsmen, who were judges while they lived and sold their verdicts to kings, so that the pit gave them the work which they had earned. Each has his hood riveted fast and never sets down his cleaver, and none reads out a sentence before he carries it out. They believe, and not wholly without reason, that everyone who is brought before them is guilty of something.

void_seraph.name: void seraph
void_seraph.lore: Isaiah beheld the seraphim above the throne, and each had six wings, two to cover the face, two to cover the feet and two with which to fly. This one fell and kept its wings, and when it lowers the upper pair there is but a hollow behind them where a face and a name used to be. Its voice is the hush of a star going out, and within that hush no spell can be spoken. Its gaze unmakes the place that a thing has in the world, so that whoever it falls upon is forever slipping out of the spot where he stands.

apocalypse_herald.name: apocalypse herald
apocalypse_herald.lore: Seven angels with seven trumpets were shown to John in his Revelation, and at each blast a ruin came upon the earth. From them this creature stole the notion, but it could steal none of their authority. The horn has grown into its breast, so that it sounds with every breath, and it bears a sickle for the harvest that it is always proclaiming. Men who hear it believe that the end has come, and they flee.

wormwood_blight.name: wormwood blight
wormwood_blight.lore: At the sound of the third trumpet a great star fell burning upon the rivers and springs, and John gives its name as Wormwood and writes that a third of the waters were turned bitter, and many died of drinking them. Where the ash of that star settled there grew this pale and spreading thing, which drinks the light and breathes out bile. Its spores poison whatever they touch, and the star's ash sheds from it even now and stings the eyes until they are blind.

iron_horseman.name: iron horseman
iron_horseman.lore: Four riders appeared to John, one upon a white horse, one upon red, one upon black, and Death upon a pale horse with Hades following after. The iron horseman is none of the four, but of the kind that rides in their dust, with armour welded shut and man and steed grown into one shape of iron. Given a straight run it lowers the lance and charges and will turn aside for nothing, and its hooves leave men senseless on the ground. Do not stand, therefore, at the end of a long corridor when it is near.

orc_archer.name: orc archer
orc_archer.lore: Shortbows of yew and gut are the arms of the orc archers, with arrows fletched in crow feathers that kennel smoke has stained black. The warband chooses them from among its runts, too weak for the front line but patient enough to hold a draw, and an archer who strikes a clergyman at sixty paces is given an extra hide against the winter.

orc_priest.name: orc priest
orc_priest.lore: No single god has the worship of the orc clergy, who call on whatever spirit answers loudest. This priest bound a battlefield ghost into the haft of his club, and it screams whenever blood is spilled. His fellows find comfort in that sound, and they march to it.

spells.name: Blood Ward
spells.cast: {The}'s prayer ends: {he} daubs {himself} with blood, and blows turn on it.

orc_marauder.name: orc marauder
orc_marauder.lore: To raid caravans and outlying farms a chieftain lends out his marauders, armed with boarding axes and shields set with spikes. They train by running downhill at full speed in all their armour, for this teaches them the only lesson of which they have need, that when once the charge has begun, to halt is a worse death than anything that waits at the bottom.

orc_warbringer.name: orc warbringer
orc_warbringer.lore: It is the warbringer who bears the banner of the warband, a long pole hung with the bones of cousins who disappointed him, and with it a great curling horn taken from an aurochs of the south. Stone is no hindrance to the voice of that horn. A luckless company hears it several corridors away before ever they see who blew it, and by then the whole warband is running toward the sound.

dread_orc_champion.name: dread orc champion
dread_orc_champion.lore: Single combat is the law by which the dread tribes of the deep tunnels choose a champion, and afterward they chain him to the tribal standard until a successor kills him. He patches his armour with the breastplates of those he has beaten, and by the time the patches outnumber the plates with which he began, he has forgotten the name that his mother gave him.

goblin_sniper.name: goblin sniper
goblin_sniper.lore: In chimneys and cracks of the ceiling the goblin snipers make their nests, with crossbows balanced upon their knees. A sniper will hold his shot if the mark stands too near a kinsman, though caution has no part in it, for the goblins believe that when a bolt has killed a cousin the bolt-mother weeps a whole season through, and none wishes to bear that on his conscience.

goblin_warpriest.name: goblin warpriest
goblin_warpriest.lore: Above every other commandment the warpriests of the goblins preach this one, that goblins shall not eat each other for three days after a feast, and the upholding of it consumes most of their strength. They swing brass censers crammed with smouldering kobold hair and chant in counting-rhyme, that the flock may follow, and when the sermon fails they blind their enemies with the smoke.

spells.name: Smoke Ward
spells.cast: {The}'s chant ends: greasy smoke wraps about {him}, and blows slide off it.

hobgoblin_marshal.name: hobgoblin marshal
hobgoblin_marshal.lore: Alone of all the goblin-kin, hobgoblins keep their ranks, dress their lines and stand fast when pressed, like a Roman legion seen in a cracked mirror of iron, and this is the work of marshals who rule each cohort by strict drill. A marshal can halt a knight in mid-stride with one bellowed order, but if he should fall, the training of years is undone in a single howling minute.

goblin_kingslayer.name: goblin kingslayer
goblin_kingslayer.lore: Once in a long generation a goblin clutch brings forth a runt who lives by having more wit and patience than the rest, and he takes up the killing of rulers as his livelihood. Kobold pretenders pay the kingslayer in captives and hobgoblin generals in steel. His shortsword is poisoned and he never works without two cousins near at hand, and never yet has the same throne hired him a second time.

skeleton_necromancer.name: skeleton necromancer
skeleton_necromancer.lore: Having outlived his apprentices and afterward his own body, this necromancer still had the art of binding spirits to bone, but the art of speech was lost to him. When he calls to his servants now there comes only a clattering of teeth in the wrong order, and yet they understand him as well as ever they did.

bone_collector.name: bone collector
bone_collector.lore: For a few centuries the bones of every adventurer who failed in this reach of the dungeon have gone to the making of the bone collector, laced together with rawhide and dried tendon. Since each rib remembers a different breast, the whole of it seems to breathe in seventeen rhythms at once, and it is forever searching for one piece more.

skeleton_lich.name: skeleton lich
skeleton_lich.lore: A true lich keeps its soul in a hidden vessel, but the vessel of this one cracked centuries ago, and so it is no true lich at all. There remains only the habit of necromancy in a skeleton that has forgotten the reason for it, and yet the dead still come at its summoning, and its cold still bites.

banshee_lich.name: banshee lich
banshee_lich.lore: Among the old families of Ireland it is told that when one of their blood must die, the bean sidhe, the woman of the fairy mound, comes in the night to keen outside the house. One such came to mourn a sorcerer of evil fame and was bound by mischance into his bones, so that all the craft of the lich is nourished now upon her grief. Within her wail are all the warnings that she could not give in time, and there are few who have heard it three times and lived.

kobold_trapsetter.name: kobold trapsetter
kobold_trapsetter.lore: German miners blamed the kobold for cave-ins, foul air and ores that poisoned the smelter, and they named the metal cobalt after him. The trapsetters of the warren have been faithful to that old renown. They love a wound that bleeds slowly, a nicked hamstring or a dart in the forearm, so that whoever flees from them sinks down at last far away from his friends.

kobold_dragonshield.name: kobold dragonshield
kobold_dragonshield.lore: Plates from the belly of a dead red dragon overlap all about the dragonshield, so heavy that he can scarcely run and so thick that he has no need to. He plants himself in the mouth of the corridor while the warren's archers shoot past his ears, and his greatest pride is that he has never once ducked his head.

kobold_pack_leader.name: kobold pack leader
kobold_pack_leader.lore: Too clever to die young and too small to be worth a challenge, the oldest survivor of a warren becomes its pack leader. He wears a brass whistle on a thong, and one short blast means hide and two mean rush. Three blasts mean abandon the warren and begin again somewhere downhill, and that is a signal he has given only once in his life.

alarm.line: {The} barks an order, and the warren stirs!
alarm.line_unseen: A barked order echoes, and something stirs.

gnoll_archer.name: gnoll archer
gnoll_archer.lore: Old bestiaries say of the hyena that it could counterfeit human speech and call a man out of his house by name. The archers of the gnolls have its laugh but none of its cunning. They carry longbows stolen from elves and fletch their shafts with hyena down, and they shoot to cripple, because the pack would have its prey walk the last mile upon its own feet.

gnoll_fang_of_yeenoghu.name: gnoll fang of Yeenoghu
gnoll_fang_of_yeenoghu.lore: Upon the brows of his most savage worshippers Yeenoghu, the Beast of Butchery, sets a hairline of red, the sign of the fang, and he who bears it never retreats from any fight. The gnolls say that one who runs will lose his teeth, tooth by tooth, over the months that follow, and none has cared to put the saying to the proof.

gnoll_alpha_of_yeenoghu.name: gnoll alpha of Yeenoghu
gnoll_alpha_of_yeenoghu.lore: To become alpha, a gnoll must eat the demon-tainted flesh of the alpha before him and live. He who has done so stands a foot above his kindred, walks upon the knuckles of one hand and speaks the tongue of the pit in the voice of a child. For an axe he bears the thighbone of a stone giant, banded with iron from the cage in which he himself was held of old.

bandit_thug.name: bandit thug
bandit_thug.lore: Many a farmhand whose lord rode to war and never returned, and many a drunkard who learned that wayfarers cannot call the watch, has become the strong arm of a gang. Alone such a man is a coward, but with a kinsman at his shoulder he will fight to the last shilling.

alarm.line_unseen: A sharp whistle, not far off.

bandit_archer.name: bandit archer
bandit_archer.lore: Poachers in former days, the archers of a roadside gang are often its most useful men, being quiet and patient and content to pass an afternoon up a tree. They will shoot neither child nor priest, and in this they obey their grandmothers rather than conscience, having been warned how such debts are collected in the end.

bandit_thief.name: bandit thief
bandit_thief.lore: With the turning of the seasons thieves drift in and out of the bandit's trade, wintering in a warm gang and picking pockets in a market town in spring. They love a quiet boot and a turned back better than a duel, and a purse cut in passing better than either, and they have this saying among them: "the man who shows his sword has already decided he would rather not use it." When one of them has your gold he runs, and if you can catch him it is yours again.

bandit_kingpin.name: bandit kingpin
bandit_kingpin.lore: A kingpin upon his stretch of road is like a baron in his fief, for he takes payment for protection, gathers his debts and quietly removes his rivals. Some of these men were officers cashiered for treason and others were roadside preachers whose sermons soured, but all of them can read and write and reckon, and for that reason alone they lead.

cult_initiate.name: cult initiate
cult_initiate.lore: Most initiates were simple townsfolk until they drank of the wrong cup at the wrong vigil, and a year of the cult's catechism has taken from them the names of their own children. They go in robes of hemp with daggers of brass, and though their conviction is borrowed, it cuts no less deeply for that.

cult_priest.name: cult priest
cult_priest.lore: After an initiate has presided at so many dark rites that they trouble his dreams no more, he passes into the second rank and becomes a priest. Such men hide the true name of the cult even from their own kin, and when they are asked what they believe they quote scripture to which they do not hold, and watch the questioner's face to learn the answer.

spells.name: Binding Litany
spells.cast: {The}'s litany ends, and your feet will not move.

cult_zealot.name: cult zealot
cult_zealot.lore: Beyond what the cult names the third veil, pain goes unnoticed and conviction rules alone, and the zealot has passed through it. He holds his cleaver in both hands even when he sits at table, and he walks with the rolling gait of a man whose ribs have broken and knit again more times than he can count.

cult_hierophant.name: cult hierophant
cult_hierophant.lore: All the living memory of the cult is in the hierophant, who alone knows where its founder is buried and what was buried with her. He eats no longer with his initiates and performs the great rites by himself. When he summons his lesser brethren to die for him, he calls them by the names they bore as children.

ghast_eater.name: ghast eater
ghast_eater.lore: The ghoul is the ghul of Arabian tales, which haunts graveyards and desert roads and feeds upon the dead, and when a ghoul has eaten enough of its own kind besides, it becomes a ghast. A scratch from its claws will numb a limb, and so foul is the stench of it that even the other undead yield it the corridor.

draugr_wight.name: draugr wight
draugr_wight.lore: A draugr, in the speech of the sagas, is a barrow-king who will not lie still. Grettir the Strong broke into such a mound and wrestled among the grave goods with its dead lord, Kar the Old, and cut off his head. This one still holds the sword that was buried with him, and at his touch the warmth is taken from the living body and given over to the barrow.
draugr_wight.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} mound and watches you go.

grave_knight.name: grave knight
grave_knight.lore: Death found this knight with his oath unfulfilled, and he would not let the matter rest. Whenever his cause is spoken aloud within a mile of his cairn, he wakes. The thing he swore may be very small, a stolen horse or an unpaid wager, but it binds him as firmly as any great vow could do.

greater_imp.name: greater imp
greater_imp.lore: Ten years in the mortal world, unslain and unbanished, will make a greater imp out of a common one. Its tail thickens, its wings harden, and it acquires the speech of some third-rate ambassador. Some of them keep faith with an old contract, but the greater number keep faith with none.

demonic_imp.name: demonic imp
demonic_imp.lore: These imps no longer feign to be any mortal's familiars, but serve as couriers to a small infernal house, sent up to settle such scores as their betters will not stoop to. They carry true hellfire now in their stings, and talons so sharp that they could sign a contract upon whatever surface lay to hand.

imp_lord.name: imp lord
imp_lord.lore: In a petty court of Hell he holds a petty title, somewhat between a baronet and a keeper of accounts. His service has won him two privileges, to call up other imps for the unpleasant part of his labours and to decline any duel by pleading higher business elsewhere, and he avails himself of both very freely.

snake_charmer.name: snake charmer
snake_charmer.lore: Every charmer knows that the cobra is all but deaf to music and rises to the swaying of the pipe rather than to the tune. This one learned his craft in the bazaars of Samarkand and went beneath the earth when the caravans ceased to come. His drone is meant for human ears, so that those who listen begin to hear and see what is not there, and his basket is never found empty of serpents.

viper_priestess.name: viper priestess
viper_priestess.lore: Arthur Evans dug from the ruins of Knossos small figures of a woman with a snake raised in either hand, whose name no one knows, though the viper priestesses claim to know it. They serve a snake goddess older than the cities she once guarded. Their eyes seldom blink, and they tend their own wounded with a venom that has been bred through centuries to heal their kin instead of killing.

cave_troll.name: Cave Troll
cave_troll.lore: Sunrise turns to stone any troll that it finds above ground, say the Norse tales, and therefore the breed keeps to caves. This one has never seen the sun and has no mind to see it. His arms are long for close work and his ridged hide shrugs off clubs, and his wounds knit while the fight is yet going on, though the scars of burning and of acid do not.
cave_troll.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} cave and watches you go.

harrow_witch.name: Harrow Witch
harrow_witch.lore: The Harrow Witch came down from the heath when the kingdoms above forgot to fear her, and she has plied her craft in the lower halls ever since, with bones braided in her hair and old curses on her tongue. Her touch brings the rot and her hexes sap the strength from a sword arm, and so the wise settle their account with her from a distance.

spells.name: Harrowing Eye
spells.cast: {The} fixes you with the evil eye.

moss_sentinel.name: Moss Sentinel
moss_sentinel.lore: Some hand carved this stone to mark a boundary at a threshold long forgotten, and it was forgotten likewise, until the moss crept over it and gave it a body. It waits where it was set, and when anything draws near, the moss remembers what the stone was for. Arrows and hammers find little there to hurt, but a sharp edge will strip the green away, and fire will do it faster.

sable_serpent.name: Sable Serpent
sable_serpent.lore: Black as wet coal and silent upon stone, this is the snake that country folk called the sable serpent and would not name at all after dark. Like every snake it grows sluggish in the cold and seeks for warmth, which in a dungeon means the living. Its venom works slowly, and no other mercy is to be looked for from a meeting with it.

iron_patriarch.name: The Iron Patriarch
iron_patriarch.lore: Father to a line of tyrants, he outlived them every one. Sons, grandsons and usurpers were borne to the family crypt while he sat on, sealed in the plate of his coronation, until the kingdom itself gave out beneath him, and when the dungeon found him he was waiting still to give audience. His guards answer yet to his call, and to every visitor he grants a brief hearing that is ended with the hammer. Blades skate from the old plate, but lightning will find out the man within it.
iron_patriarch.omen: Someone has kept this floor swept and the torches trimmed, as though a court were to sit.
iron_patriarch.enrage_message: The Iron Patriarch rises from his throne, and the audience is at an end.
rage_messages: The Iron Patriarch remembers how he took the crown.
The Iron Patriarch fights as one who has outlived all his heirs.

mage_slayer_assassin.name: Mage-Slayer Assassin
mage_slayer_assassin.lore: Reared in the towers of the wizards to hunt down renegades, this order turned in time against the towers themselves. Wards are sewn into the lining of each slayer's coat, so that spells slide from him. His first cut is for the casting hand and his second for the throat, to stop the voice, and when those are made, say the brethren, what remains is no more than clerk's work.

stone_golem.name: Stone Golem
stone_golem.lore: Masons built it to guard the lower stair, and though they are long dead it guards the lower stair yet. There is no spark of thought behind that face, but only one command, cut too deep to wear away. Swords chip and arrows glance upon the granite, and he who would pass will fare better with a miner's hammer or a flask of acid.

plague_witch.name: Plague Witch
plague_witch.lore: In the years of the Black Death frightened towns laid the sickness upon witches and well-poisoners, and this woman in the green hood would have deserved the blame. She gathers the dying at the gate and brings them down with her, where they serve her and her craft keeps them upon their feet. When she falls, there will be none left to mend them.

spells.name: Ward of Plague Rags
spells.cast: {The}'s chant ends: buzzing flies swarm about {him}, thick as a cloak.

vine_horror.name: Vine Horror
vine_horror.lore: The vine horror grows wherever blood was spilled and none came to bury the dead. It hangs on the wall like a heap of dry creeper until some warm thing passes beneath, and then the tendrils drop and tighten and the thorns begin their work. Cold will not kill it and arrows pass through the tangle, so it must be cut at root and stem, or else burned.

lurking_horror.name: Lurking Horror
lurking_horror.lore: A greater cousin to the petty mimic, the lurking horror is schooled in patience and in chests, and for years it can hold the shape of a locked coffer without a twitch. Adventurers find it where they most hope to find such treasure as it feigns to be, and there they learn that the lid is a mouth and the hinges are teeth, and that the lock was never locked at all.

ettin_warchief.name: Ettin Warchief
ettin_warchief.lore: Forty years long the two heads upon these shoulders disputed everything, and together they led their clan to ruin, each blaming the other for the road they had taken, and the dungeon keeps what is left. The right head gives an order and the left revokes it, and yet by some means both clubs descend upon the same mark.

throne_sentinel.name: Throne Sentinel
throne_sentinel.lore: Court enchanters gave motion to this armour, which was cast for a king's bodyguard, and none has ever released it from its watch. No living foundry can match its smithwork. With halberd and shield it guards an empty throne, and when an opponent lands a clean blow it salutes him still, before it answers him in kind.

whispering_crone.name: The Whispering Crone
whispering_crone.lore: There was once a woman in a market town who told fortunes, and told them too plainly, saying which child would not see the spring and which husband would never come home, and for this the townsfolk buried her alive. In the darkness of the grave she went on whispering until, after some years, other things began to whisper back, and now skeletons and death knights come at her call like hounds to a huntsman. Her voice carries no farther than a breath, yet in it each listener hears his own death foretold with the day and the hour, and in no such telling has she yet been wrong.
whispering_crone.omen: A low voice begins close beside you as soon as you arrive, and it knows your name.
whispering_crone.enrage_message: The Whispering Crone breaks off her whispering.
rage_messages: The Whispering Crone speaks a name, and you know it for your own.
The friends of the Whispering Crone press closer about you in the dark.

demonic_trickster.name: Demonic Trickster
demonic_trickster.lore: Hell sends up its clever ones to negotiate, though they never do so. This demon best loves the moment just before, with the open hand and the reasonable smile, and then from an angle that should not exist there comes a blade of warped fire. It mocks as it fights, until those whom it assails are striking at the laughter instead of at the demon.

deep_one_priest.name: Deep-One Priest
deep_one_priest.lore: Certain villages of the coast bred a strain that might almost pass for human, wide of eye and flat of nose, with a shuffle in the walk. When their wells ran dry the priests climbed down them, and went on descending. They pray to something beneath the sea in a tongue full of water, and by that prayer their flock is held upright long after it should have fallen.

spells.name: Tide Ward
spells.cast: {The}'s chant ends: cold sea-water swirls about {him} and will not fall.

gilded_mimic.name: Gilded Mimic
gilded_mimic.lore: Age has taught the gilded mimic what adventurers truly seek, and it troubles itself no more with a single chest. It spreads itself out as the hoard of a king, spilled open as though some other company had won the fight already and departed in haste. There is true gold even in its false coins, which makes the deceit a costly one, and one that very seldom fails.

frostfang_giant.name: Frostfang Giant
frostfang_giant.lore: Jotunheim, beyond the river that never freezes, held the halls of the frost giants in Norse song, and from those halls the frostfangs were cast out. They came into the deeps seeking warmth and found another cold instead, which suited them well. They bear mauls of glacier ice and breathe a numbing fog, and they have never forgotten the slight that their kindred put upon them.

crypt_summoner.name: Crypt Summoner
crypt_summoner.lore: Forgotten by the world above is the school where this summoner studied, and he has been dead for longer than he was a scholar. To him necromancy is no more than the keeping of accounts: which corpse, which name and what wage is owed. He has had charge of those books a very long while and they balance, and any stranger who enters his crypt is written in at once among his possessions.

shadow_archer.name: Shadow Archer
shadow_archer.lore: The shadow archers are trained in towers drawn on no map. Their first lesson is the bow and their second is to be gone from where the arrow came from, but the third their masters keep to themselves. Their arrows are fletched with darkness and leave the eyes dim, but firelight will give such archers no place in which to hide.

veiled_inquisitor.name: Veiled Inquisitor
veiled_inquisitor.lore: He was sent long ago, by an authority that is no more, to find heretics who have themselves forgotten the doctrine, and so he makes it up as he goes. His scourge is real and so is his burning censer, but his creed is whatever he last declared it to be. He hides his face behind a veil, a thing of which no true servant of the Church has ever had need.

spells.name: Seal of Silence
spells.cast: {The} seals your lips with a word: no spell, no scroll.

spells.name: Binding Litany
spells.cast: {The}'s litany ends, and your feet will not move.

lava_elemental.name: Lava Elemental
lava_elemental.lore: Where the dungeon presses against a vein of magma, the fire will sometimes forget that it is only fire, and will rise up and walk. It wears a crust of black rock that cracks orange at each step, and arrows melt in it and hammers sink. It has no notion what walking may be for, but it has grown very skilful at burning those whom it has walked up to.

death_throes.warn_line: {The} swells and glows, about to burst.

blood_archon.name: Blood Archon
blood_archon.lore: The blood archons are fiends of an elder order, from the days when every bargain was written and sealed in blood. Kings have come to this one to buy victories and merchants to buy fair winds, and he has set down the name of each in a ledger bound in skin, and has exacted payment from them all in the end. In battle he opens his own vein and waits, for every stroke of steel is reckoned to his profit, but fire and a holy blessing will cancel the debt.
blood_archon.omen: A ledger lies open upon the stair, and its last entry is your name, with the amount left blank.
blood_archon.enrage_message: The Blood Archon closes his ledger.
rage_messages: The Blood Archon comes to collect his due.
The Blood Archon adds interest to your debt.

astral_horror.name: Astral Horror
astral_horror.lore: Through a door that someone left open in a dream came the astral horror, and it has not yet decided whether to depart. It has no fixed outline, but only some suggestion of eyes and of reaching thought. Minds near it grow muddled, and strength drains out of them like water from a cracked jug. It appears to be no more than curious, but few have survived its curiosity.

tiamat.name: Tiamat the Five-Headed Dragon Queen
