tiamat.lore: Tiamat was the salt sea, as the Babylonian Enuma Elish relates, and mother of the first gods and of the monsters that she afterward raised against them. But the young god Marduk drove the winds into her open jaws, sent an arrow down her throat and clove her body in two, and from it he made the sky and the earth. The storytellers of later ages gave her five dragon heads and named her queen of evil dragonkind, and in that shape she wakes beneath the dungeon. Each of her five crowned heads breathes a different ruin, frost, flame, lightning, acid or venom, and behind them all lies the oldest grudge in the world.
tiamat.omen: The air tastes of salt, and the stone is wet with something that is not water.

asmodeus.name: Asmodeus, Prince of Hell
asmodeus.lore: Seven husbands of Sarah were slain by Asmodeus, each upon his wedding night, as the Book of Tobit tells, until young Tobias, by the counsel of the angel Raphael, burned the heart and liver of a fish, and the smoke drove the demon to the far reaches of Egypt, where Raphael bound him. In later tradition he became a prince of Hell, who rules by contract rather than by fury. Every soul in his keeping has signed its own surrender, and the ruby rod in his hand seals each bargain, but the matter of the fish he has never forgiven.
asmodeus.omen: Somewhere on this floor a table is laid for two, and a bell is rung for dinner.

surtur.name: Surtur the Fire Giant Lord
surtur.lore: Upon the border of Muspelheim, the realm of fire, stands Surtur, whom the Norse poets called Surt, and the sword in his hand outshines the sun. It is foretold in the Voluspa that at Ragnarok he shall ride from the south with flame before him and behind, cut down the god Freyr and cast fire over all the earth until it sinks into the sea. That battle has not yet summoned him. He waits below for the sounding of the horn while the stone runs like wax around him, and cold is the one thing that a lord of fire has reason to respect.
surtur.omen: The stone here is warm and runs like wax.

ymir_last_spawn.name: Ymir's Last Spawn
ymir_last_spawn.lore: Of all the frost giants Ymir was the first, born where the ice of Niflheim met the sparks of Muspelheim. Odin and his brothers Vili and Ve slew him and built the world of his body, the soil from his flesh, the sea from his blood, the mountains from his bones and from his skull the dome of the sky. In that blood all his kindred drowned save Bergelmir and his wife. This giant claims descent from neither, but says that he was there before the flood, and he carries in his breath the cold of that first morning.
ymir_last_spawn.omen: Frost has grown on the inside of the walls.

hrungnirs_ghost.name: Hrungnir's Ghost
hrungnirs_ghost.lore: Strongest of the giants was Hrungnir, whose heart was of hard stone, three-cornered and sharp-edged, and whose head and shield were of stone likewise. Being drunk in Asgard he boasted that he would carry Valhalla home, and Thor met him in a duel at the border. The giant cast his whetstone and Thor cast Mjolnir, and the hammer shattered the stone in the air and went on to break Hrungnir's skull, but a splinter of the whetstone lodged in Thor's head and was there ever after. The ghost walks yet, hurling shards and demanding that the duel be fought again.
hrungnirs_ghost.omen: Chips of whetstone are scattered across the floor, as if thrown.

bonnacon.name: Bonnacon
bonnacon.lore: Paeonia is the home of the bonnacon, if the bestiaries may be believed, and it has the body of a bull and the mane of a horse. Its horns curl so far back upon themselves that they can hurt no one, a misfortune which Pliny noted with some sympathy, but the beast has another defence. As it runs it sprays dung across the ground behind it, and whatever this touches burns as if set alight. For three hundred years the monks painted this in the margins of their books, and the knight who pursues it there always has the look of one who deeply regrets the calling he has chosen.
bonnacon.omen: The floor ahead is scorched in long streaks, and a most evil smell rises from it.

calydonian_boar.name: Calydonian Boar
calydonian_boar.lore: King Oeneus of Calydon gave first fruits at harvest to every god but Artemis, whom he forgot, and in her anger she sent a boar against him. It was bigger than a bull, says Ovid, with bristles like the shafts of spears and tusks like an elephant's, and it trampled vines and corn alike. Half the heroes of Greece gathered for the hunt, and Atalanta's arrow drew the first blood and Meleager's spear made an end, but afterward they quarrelled over the keeping of the hide, and that quarrel killed more of them than the boar had done.
calydonian_boar.omen: The corridors here are ploughed up as if by a harrow, stone and all.

deadite.name: deadite
deadite.lore: Words read aloud from the Book of the Dead, as Sam Raimi's Evil Dead films tell, will wake a Kandarian demon in the woods, and it climbs into whoever is nearest, living or dead. Those it possesses are called Deadites. They wear the face of a friend and beg for help, and then they laugh and lunge with a strength and speed that no body should have. Ash learned by bitter trial that nothing short of taking one apart will stop it, and this one has been waiting in the corridor for someone kind to come by.

fresh_deadite.name: fresh deadite
fresh_deadite.lore: The Kandarian demon does not wait for a body to grow cold, as Sam Raimi's Evil Dead has shown, but climbs into whoever is nearest. In the first hours the possessed still have the voice and face of a friend, and are betrayed only by the white eyes and the laughter. A fresh Deadite has yet to learn what the body it wears can do, but already it is quicker than it should be, it means to swallow your soul, and nothing short of taking it apart will stop it. Left long enough in the dark, it will learn the rest and become the other kind of Deadite.

risen_deadite.name: risen deadite
risen_deadite.lore: Ash was bidden in Army of Darkness to say three words before he lifted the Necronomicon, and when he mumbled the last of them the graveyard answered, so that the old dead clawed their way up from the earth and marched as an army. These are what a botched reading raises here. They have lain too long to be quick or strong, and their bones break like dry sticks, but they come up out of the ground all at once.

black_knight.name: The Black Knight
black_knight.lore: A knight in black armour has taken upon himself the guarding of one small stone bridge, and no one has ever got from him the reason. He will neither move from it nor admit that he has lost. Travellers who simply go round by the other passage report that he shouts after them for a considerable while, and those who have fought him report that he shouts a great deal more.

huldufolk_raider.name: Huldufolk Raider
huldufolk_raider.lore: Icelanders tell of the huldufolk, the hidden people, who dwell within rocks and hills with farms and churches of their own and are seen only when they wish it. One tale says that Eve hid her unwashed children from God, and God decreed that what was hidden from Him should be hidden from men. The makers of roads in Iceland will even now bend a road about an elf rock rather than blast it. But the raiders of these depths no longer wait to be wronged. They walk beside a traveller unseen and lead him in circles, and when he is wholly lost they use the knife.

darkhelm_shade.name: Darkhelm Shade
darkhelm_shade.lore: For the three sons of Kronos the Cyclopes forged three gifts, the thunderbolt for Zeus, the trident for Poseidon and for Hades a helm of darkness that hid whoever wore it. Athena put it on at Troy so that Ares never saw her spear coming, and Perseus wore it when he slipped away from the Gorgons. Hades has a guard of the dead who wear lesser copies of that helm, and these he sends after any who carry off what belongs below. They bear yet the long spears with which they were buried, and the living feel the cold of the grave a moment before the point strikes home.

whirlwind_jinni.name: Whirlwind Jinni
whirlwind_jinni.lore: Of smokeless fire the jinn were made, as the Qur'an says, and Iblis and his tribe see men from where men cannot see them. The villagers of Egypt told the traveller Edward Lane that a jinni rides within every dust-devil that spins across the fields, and they cried 'Iron!' at one as it passed, because the jinn fear iron. This jinni rides his whirlwind along the corridors. A blow falls out of empty air, and by the time the dust has settled and a man has turned about, the rider is somewhere else.

nibelung_hoardwarden.name: Nibelung Hoard-Warden
nibelung_hoardwarden.lore: Alberich the dwarf, so the Nibelungenlied tells, guarded the Nibelung hoard and wore the Tarnkappe, a cloak that hid its wearer from sight and lent him the strength of twelve men. Siegfried wrested it from him and took the treasure, and afterward stood unseen at King Gunther's side to win Brunhild's games for him. Far below, the sworn wardens of Alberich still keep what remains, in cloaks cut from the same cloth, and no one ever sees a hoard-warden, but only a coin that lifts from the pile and afterward the falling of the pick.
nibelung_hoardwarden.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} hoard and watches you go.

ker.name: Ker
ker.lore: Hesiod painted the Keres on the shield of Heracles as dark spirits of death with white and gnashing teeth, fighting one another over the fallen, each greedy to drink the dark blood first. Homer set one upon the shield of Achilles, dragging a dead man through the battle by his feet. They never come alone. Any one of them is weak, as death is reckoned in these deeps, but there are always more of them than there are of you, and a wounded man draws the whole flock. Kill them swiftly, therefore, and many at a time.

hellmouth.name: Hellmouth
hellmouth.lore: Medieval painters showed Hell as a mouth, the gaping jaws of Leviathan, the beast of Job, out of whose mouth go burning lamps. On the Doom paintings over church arches and upon the stages of the mystery plays the damned were herded into it, while men worked the jaws with ropes and blew smoke from the throat. One such mouth lies flat in the floor of the deeps, and its open gullet looks exactly like a stair going down. Every floor has but one way down, so if ever you find two, be sure that one of them is such a mouth, and hungry.

mere_wife.name: Mere-Wife
mere_wife.lore: The Beowulf poet gave no name to Grendel's mother, but only a kind, merewif, the mere-wife, she-wolf of the deep. She rose out of the dark water to avenge her son, and when Beowulf followed her down she dragged him to her hall beneath the mere. There his borrowed sword Hrunting, which had never failed in battle, would not bite upon her hide, and he was forced to wrestle with her until he found a giant's blade on her wall. Her kind lie in wait beneath black water still, and a blade will glance off that hide, but a heavier weapon will not.
mere_wife.lair_line: {The} stops at the edge of {his} mere and watches you go.

endor_medium.name: Medium of Endor
endor_medium.lore: King Saul had driven every medium out of Israel, yet on the night before his last battle he put on a disguise and sought out the one who remained at Endor. At his word she called up the prophet Samuel, an old man wrapped in a mantle, who told Saul that on the morrow he and his sons would be with him among the dead. The craft has descended through all her line. When they call, whatever is listening in the dark comes up, and much of it cannot be seen, so kill the one who is calling before the room fills.

erinyes_greater.name: Greater Erinys
erinyes_greater.lore: Three were the Erinyes: Alecto the unceasing, Megaera the grudging and Tisiphone the avenger of murder. In Aeschylus they hunted Orestes for his mother's blood from Argos to Delphi and on to Athens, with snakes in their hair and blood weeping from their eyes, and they slept only when Apollo compelled them. At the last Athena appeased them with a new home beneath the city and a new name, the Kindly Ones, but none in these depths has made them any such offer. They come as three, strike and scatter and come again, and men take flight at the very look of them.

tiamat_blood.name: Blood of Tiamat
tiamat_blood.lore: When Marduk had caught Tiamat the salt sea in his net, as the Babylonian poem of creation tells, he drove the winds into her mouth and split her like a fish for drying, and of the halves he made sky and earth. Then he cut the channels of her blood, and the north wind bore it away to secret places, of which this is one. That blood still crawls, salt and venomous, and it remembers being divided, so that a small cut does no more than make two of it. A great blow, such as a long answer chain gives, leaves it no strength to divide.

hels_handmaid.name: Handmaid of Hel
hels_handmaid.lore: Snorri Sturluson told how the hall of Hel is furnished: her plate is called Hunger, her knife Famine and her bed Sickbed, and her servants are Ganglati and Ganglot, whose names both mean the slow-walker. Many maids serve Hel now, and all of them are slow. They walk among her dead mending what the living break, and by their touch the same slowness enters into a warm body. Wherever the dead keep getting up again, look for the maid behind them and put her down first.

stheno_gorgon.name: Stheno the Gorgon
stheno_gorgon.lore: Of three sisters Medusa alone was mortal, and death has no power over the others, Stheno the mighty and Euryale the far-roaming. Apollodorus gives them brazen hands and golden wings. When Perseus fled with their sister's head they rose from their beds and chased him over the sea until the helm of Hades hid him, and they have sought him ever since. The living turn rigid as stone beneath their gaze, and a killing blow lays either of them low for no more than a moment.
stheno_gorgon.revive_message: Stheno rises again, for death cannot hold an immortal.
stheno_gorgon.omen: Somewhere on this floor two women are hissing at each other, and then both fall silent.
stheno_gorgon.kill_chronicle: Put down Stheno the mighty Gorgon twice. She got up after the first.
stheno_gorgon.kill_pair_chronicle: Put down both of Medusa's sisters, twice each. May not last.

euryale_gorgon.name: Euryale the Gorgon
euryale_gorgon.lore: Pindar tells that Athena devised the music of the pipes to copy one sound, the shrill wailing that Euryale raised over her beheaded sister while the snakes in her hair keened along with her. Euryale has made no end of grieving or of hunting, and she goes nowhere without Stheno. Her wail drives men back and her gaze holds them where they stand, and like her sister she is immortal, so that she may be put down, but not for long. Against her a polished shield or a blindfold is worth more than any sword.
euryale_gorgon.revive_message: Euryale rises again, wailing, for death cannot hold an immortal.
euryale_gorgon.kill_chronicle: Put down Euryale twice, wailing for Medusa. Quiet after the second.
euryale_gorgon.kill_pair_chronicle: Put down both of Medusa's sisters, twice each. May not last.

gashadokuro.name: Gashadokuro
gashadokuro.lore: Japanese storytellers of the last century spoke of the gashadokuro, the starving skeleton, fifteen times the height of a man and built from the bones of all who died of hunger or in battle and lay unburied. It walks at night without a sound, and no warning is given but a ringing in the ears, gasha gasha, a moment before it bites off a traveller's head. This one has folded itself into a corner of the dungeon, where it may be taken for a heap of old bones until it stirs. A spear passes between such ribs, but a hammer will find bone there to break.

autolycus_heir.name: Heir of Autolycus
autolycus_heir.lore: Autolycus, the grandfather of Odysseus, outdid all men in thieving and in oaths that meant nothing, and had that gift from Hermes himself. He took a famous boar-tusk helmet out of a locked house and the cattle of Sisyphus out of a guarded field, and he changed their colour lest their owner know them, so that Sisyphus outwitted him only by carving his own name beneath their hooves. His heirs carry on the family trade. They brush against you and are gone, leaving purse or pack the lighter, but run them down and what they took is yours again.

strix.name: Strix
strix.lore: Ovid in the Fasti describes the strix as a bird of the night, big of head and staring of eye, with a beak made for snatching, grey feathers and hooked claws, that flies in darkness and drinks blood. Whether striges are born birds or are old women changed by a spell, he says that nobody knows. They came for the infant Proca in his cradle, but the nymph Cranae barred them out with a branch of whitethorn at the window. In these halls they hunt in threes, and while one sings you to sleep the others drink.

bronze_sentinel.name: Bronze Sentinel
bronze_sentinel.lore: Talos, the man of bronze, was made by Hephaestus to guard Crete, and three times a day he walked about the island, throwing boulders at any ship that came near. When men landed, he heated himself red-hot in a fire and embraced them. He had a single vein running from neck to ankle and stopped with one bronze nail, but Medea bewitched him with her eyes, the nail came out, and the ichor ran from him like molten lead. His copies guard the deep halls. Swords and hammers ring off them, so seek out the nail with a point or with a spell.

sown_warrior.name: Sown Warrior
sown_warrior.lore: Cadmus slew the dragon of Ares, and by Athena's counsel he sowed its teeth in a ploughed field, whereupon armed men rose out of the furrows, already clad in bronze and already wrathful. He threw a stone into their midst, and each blamed the man beside him, and they fought until only five were left. Jason reaped the same harvest at Colchis and overcame it by the same device. The sown men still rise in companies and fight as one, but if you confuse them, or throw something into the middle of them, they will turn on each other.

takshaka_brood.name: Brood of Takshaka
takshaka_brood.lore: Parikshit the king, of whom the Mahabharata tells, was cursed to die of a serpent's bite on the seventh day, and he shut himself in a tower upon a single pillar and admitted none but holy men. But Takshaka the serpent king sent his nagas in the guise of holy men bearing fruit, and hid himself within one fruit as a tiny worm the colour of copper. When the king took it up, Takshaka put on his true shape and bit. His brood still hide in fruit, so beware of any perfect apple that you find lying on a dungeon floor.

rakshasa_illusionist.name: Rakshasa Illusionist
rakshasa_illusionist.lore: Indrajit, the conqueror of Indra, was the son of Ravana, and he made war on Rama's army from within the clouds, where no arrow could find him. With the serpent noose, which was of living snakes, he bound Rama and Lakshmana helpless on the field, until Garuda, the enemy of every serpent, descended and the snakes fled from his shadow. By his maya the army of monkeys saw things that were not there. The rakshasa illusionists who learned from him keep their distance, tie you where you stand and fill your eyes with lies, so you must close the distance, or else kill them from where you are.

spells.name: Maya
spells.cast: {The} is not where you struck: {he} stands four paces off.

ushabti_overseer.name: Ushabti Overseer
ushabti_overseer.lore: An Egyptian of means took ushabtis with him to the tomb, little workers of blue faience, one for every day of the year, and on them was written the sixth spell of the Book of the Dead: 'O ushabti, if I am called to work in the land of the dead, you shall answer: Here I am.' Over every ten was set an overseer with a whip, to hold them to their labour. The overseers of these depths have outlived their masters, and still they read out the spell and still the workers answer. Break the one who has the whip, and no more will answer to the spell.

ushabti_worker.name: Ushabti Worker
ushabti_worker.lore: In the tomb it was a little figure of blue faience no bigger than a man's hand, but here below it has the stature of a man. It carries the hoe and the basket of sand that were painted upon it, and it obeys the sixth spell, answering 'Here I am' and going to its work. There is neither malice nor will in it, and if it throws the sand in your eyes, that is only because the overseer has bidden it.

sekhmet_lioness.name: Lioness of Sekhmet
sekhmet_lioness.lore: Mankind once plotted against Ra, and he sent forth his Eye against them as Sekhmet the lioness, who slaughtered until she waded in blood and would not stop. To save the rest, Ra had seven thousand jars of beer dyed red with ochre and poured over the fields, and she drank it for blood, fell drunk and forgot her wrath. Her lionesses were never given the beer. Their hot breath is the desert wind and each blow they strike makes the next one fiercer, so end the fight quickly, or walk away and let them cool.
sekhmet_lioness.fury_message: The eyes of the Lioness of Sekhmet go red, and she is wading in blood now.

ammit_devourer.name: Devourer of Hearts
ammit_devourer.lore: Anubis set the heart of each dead man upon a scale against the feather of Ma'at in the Hall of the Two Truths, and Thoth wrote down the judgment. Beside them crouched Ammit the Devourer, who had a crocodile's head, the forequarters of a lion and the hindquarters of a hippopotamus, and any heart heavier than the feather was hers to eat, so that its owner perished for ever. Her get still weigh every heart they meet, and their bite is gentle upon a clean conscience and savage upon a heavy one.

mazandaran_div.name: Mazandaran Div
mazandaran_div.lore: The Shahnameh tells how King Kay Kavus marched to conquer Mazandaran, and how the White Div answered him with sorcery. Darkness descended on the Persian host and a hail of stones fell out of it, and when it lifted the king and his men were blind. Then Rostam went alone through seven trials, slew the White Div in his cave, and with drops of the div's blood restored the sight of his king. The divs of Mazandaran still fight from a distance and put out the sight of men, so bring some remedy for the eyes, or else close in swiftly.

dahaka_wyrm.name: Dahaka Wyrm
dahaka_wyrm.lore: Azhi Dahaka, the dragon of the Avesta with three heads and six eyes, was made by the evil spirit to empty the world of good things. When the hero Thraetaona smote it with his blade, snakes, scorpions, toads and lizards poured from the wound, and he saw that if he cut it to pieces the world would be filled with vermin, and so he chained it beneath Mount Damavand instead. Its brood carries the same curse, and every cut or stab lets loose a swarm, so the wise will club it, or strike it with what is holy.

khrafstra_swarm.name: Khrafstra Swarm
khrafstra_swarm.lore: Zoroastrian books give the name khrafstra to the noxious creatures, snakes, scorpions, toads, lizards and stinging flies, that the evil spirit made to mar the good creation. It was accounted a good deed to kill them, and the priests kept a special stick for the purpose. This seething knot spilled out of the wound of a Dahaka, and from that hour it has not ceased to bite.

galla_demon.name: Galla
galla_demon.lore: When Inanna returned from the underworld, the galla came with her to seize one who should take her place. They eat no food, says the Sumerian poem, they drink no water and accept no gift, and they pull the wife from the husband's arms and the child from the father's knee. They pursued her husband Dumuzi across the steppe, and though the sun god turned him three times into a gazelle that he might escape, three times they found him. In gangs they come to grab and hold and drag away, and they will never give up the chase.

girtablilu.name: Scorpion-Man
girtablilu.lore: Gilgamesh came to the twin peaks of Mount Mashu, where the sun goes in and out, and found the gate kept by a scorpion-man and his wife, human to the waist and scorpion below, whose terror was overwhelming and whose glance was death. He told them truly of his grief and they let him pass, but in these depths they will ask no questions. They hunt in pairs, drawing bows as the Babylonian boundary stones show them. Their shells turn both blade and arrow and their sting stops a man where he stands, but a hammer will crack them.

asag_stone_warrior.name: Stone Warrior of Asag
asag_stone_warrior.lore: Asag was the demon of the mountains, so terrible that fish boiled alive in the rivers where he walked, and upon the mountains he fathered an army, and every soldier in it was a stone. So says the Sumerian poem Lugal-e, and it tells how the god Ninurta beat them with Sharur, his talking mace, and afterward judged each kind of stone, blessing some and cursing others, which is why stones are as they are. But some of that army was never judged, and blades, fire, frost and lightning do almost nothing to them, so do as Ninurta did, and bring a mace.

totentanz_dancer.name: Totentanz Dancer
totentanz_dancer.lore: After the Black Death the walls of churches were painted with the Dance of Death, a long chain of skeletons that led each a living partner by the hand, pope and emperor, peasant and child, and none of them ready. Bernt Notke painted thirty yards of it for Lubeck, and a piece survives in Tallinn. These dancers have stepped down from the wall. They circle and step and are never standing where you struck, and they take you by the hands until your feet begin to follow the steps. Whoever must fight them should set his back to a wall.

mara.name: Mara
mara.lore: Vanlandi the king broke faith with his Finnish wife, as the Ynglinga saga tells, and she paid a witch to send a mara against him. The mara trod on him as soon as he slept, and when his men held his head she trampled his legs, and when they held his legs she pressed upon his head until he died. From her name comes our word nightmare. A mara lays her weight on you until you sleep where you stand, and then she tramples, the harder upon a sleeper, and for this cause old households hung a knife of steel over the bed.

lyssa_madness.name: Madness of Lyssa
lyssa_madness.lore: Night was the mother of Lyssa, the spirit of raging madness, whose name is also the Greek word for rabies. Euripides tells that Hera sent her to drive Heracles out of his wits, and that Lyssa herself protested the injustice and yet obeyed, and when he came to himself it was among the bodies of his own family. Her madnesses wander the lowest halls, where they dart in, bite, turn the mind inside out and are gone before it turns back again. Against them a clear head is the only armour.

jorogumo.name: Jorogumo
jorogumo.lore: Edo storytellers gave the name of jorogumo to a spider that has lived four hundred years and has learned to take the shape of a woman. A woodcutter who rested by the Joren Falls in Izu felt threads winding about his ankle, and he tied them to a stump, which was torn from the ground and dragged beneath the water. In the dungeon she waits in the dark corners of rooms, and the first warning of her is silk about your feet, but she herself has a great fear of fire.

neferkaptah_risen.name: Neferkaptah
neferkaptah_risen.lore: Neferkaptah, a prince of Egypt, desired to read the language of the gods. From the river at Coptos he dug up the Book of Thoth, out of six boxes and from a serpent that would not die, and on the homeward journey the gods took his son and his wife in payment. Then he bound the book upon his breast and walked into the Nile after them, and Pharaoh buried him at Memphis with the book upon him still. Though he has been dead for long ages he holds to every bargain that he makes, and he expects that you will hold as faithfully to yours.

azarael.name: Azarael
azarael.lore: Among the Powers, the sixth choir of angels, Azarael was numbered until he fell with Lucifer, and Saint Michael chained him upon a floor of the deep to guard nothing, which was his punishment. Through the centuries he has practised sounding reasonable and has become very good at it. But when he is out of his chains he is reasonable no longer, and his skin is bronze from within, glowing like the door of a furnace.

locust_cultist.name: Locust cultist
locust_cultist.lore: The last roads down to the Pit are held by the Cult of the Locust for the Destroyer, whose name is Abaddon in Hebrew and Apollyon in Greek. Its soldiers bear black shields, and at every checkpoint they say the words, 'The Destroyer is merciful.' Most of them ceased to believe it years ago. Yet they say it still and compel all others to say it, for a lie on every tongue will hold a people in and spare the cult the building of a wall.

locust_herald.name: Locust herald
locust_herald.lore: From checkpoint to checkpoint the heralds of the Locust cult bear its orders, and to all other folk they bear its lies. As befits heralds, they travel light and talk well and fight but poorly. If one should tell you that he has deserted, he may even mean it, though his resolve will hardly outlast the week.

villager_mob.name: angry villager
villager_mob.lore: Matthew Hopkins went among the villages of eastern England in 1645 and 1646, calling himself Witchfinder General, and upon his word around a hundred people were hanged. He could not have done it alone, for at every hanging there stood a crowd of ordinary folk who were frightened and weary and sure. A villager alone with his pitchfork is no more than a farmer, but when twenty come on together they are such a crowd as that, and it is perilous to stand before them.

palace_guard.name: palace guard
palace_guard.lore: Dionysius, the tyrant of Syracuse, went in such dread of murder that he would be shaved by none but his own daughters, and in time he took the razors from them also. Cicero tells that he kept a bodyguard of foreign soldiers about the palace by night and day, well paid and well armed and trusted with nothing. So it is with the guard of every tyrant, who will come running when the bell is rung and will never ask who has rung it.

morrow.name: Morrow
morrow.lore: An acolyte of the Cult of the Locust, Morrow was taken in the robe of a captured priest and was chained at that priest's side. He knows the prayers well enough to deceive any stranger who knows them no better than he. It is a good while now since he was set free, and all that time he has been saving one of those prayers for the one who let him out.

old_nickel.name: Old Nickel
old_nickel.lore: In the mines of Germany there were two names for the spite of the deep shafts. Ore that poisoned the smelter and gave no silver was the kobold's work, and its metal is called cobalt still, while ore that looked like copper and gave none was Kupfernickel, Old Nick's copper, and its metal we call nickel. Old Nickel is a kobold of the upper shafts who will fight nothing that can fight back, yet he has killed more sleeping miners than the damp has. He comes smiling to travellers, calls himself their friend, offers to watch their backs and bids them rest. When a miner lay down near the hoard, the kobold crept up in the dark with a pick, and every nail, buckle and spearhead in his pile was stolen from someone who never woke. He counts the dead every night as he counts his iron. He kicks rats for sport, and to keep the drip off his iron he tore the leaves from a young Bloomsaur's back while it cried.
old_nickel.sight_sign: {The} wears a cloak of broad green leaves, beaded with water and torn ragged at the edges, and clutches a spear that was never his. He smiles up at you with small, greedy eyes and sidles closer.

stalker._doc: ai_pattern stalker_coward (Monster._stalker_turn; Brandon 2026-11-17). A FALSE FRIEND first: from first sight he comes up to the hero and stays 'friend_keep' tiles off (a step back if the hero comes beside him, never more), and never strikes. A hero in a 'prey_on' state (resting: the wait key this turn, senses.TURN.rested; or under that status) that he sees or is within 'hears_prey' tiles of, he darts in on at 'dash_steps' steps a turn, still smiling; the moment he reaches him the act drops for good (the reveal, _revealed, with a shout) and his blow that same turn (the sneak attack) never misses its roll and lands 'sneak_mult' times as hard; it can kill (Brandon: 'we're not running a charity here'). Struck first, the act drops too, with no sneak attack. As a friend he also helps, where it is safe: a monster at or under 'help_below' of its health, busy with the hero (beside him) or held fast, he darts in on, strikes once, and darts back, at most once in 'help_gap' turns; never one at full health, never one free to hit him back. Revealed, he strikes only a hero beside him, and then only when he cannot back off; a hero who comes at him he backs away from, toward his hoard, keeping 'keep' to keep + 'slack' tiles off; one who walks away he follows at that distance; a hero at rest or helpless he darts in on again. Out of sight, he follows to where he last saw or heard the hero (his footsteps carry round corners); neither seen nor heard for 'lose_after' turns, he goes back to his hoard. While the act holds, the hero's pets leave him be (lore_powers.at_peace). His lines: data/old_nickel.json.

old_nickel.kill_chronicle: Killed Old Nickel, iron-hoarder. Took back the Bloomsaur's leaves.
old_nickel._design_note: Winning-build plan 2026-11-13 section 3.8 (Brandon: greedy and mean, so no one feels bad killing him; secondary to the Emberpup's story), made a murderer of sleepers on 2026-11-17 (Brandon: 'he will murder people in their sleep for their things'). Placed every run on one floor from 1 to the Emberpup's (src/emberpup_encounter.py, BloomleafMixin), never in the pup's room; never in a random pool (peak_weight 0, quest_only, no spawn_chance). He does not start a fair fight (ai_pattern stalker_coward, see 'stalker'). He plays the false friend (Brandon: 'he initially approaches the player and tells him he'll protect him and watch his back'): he keeps two tiles off, offers to guard the hero's sleep and urges him to rest (data/old_nickel.json). He helps against a wounded monster busy with the hero, once and safely, to look the friend. When the hero rests, sleeps or is paralysed, confused or stunned, the act drops all at once: a shout, and a sneak attack three times as hard, the same moment (it can kill). After that he stalks at three tiles, backs off, strikes only cornered, and darts in again on a hero at rest; his later blows land half as hard again on a sleeper or a paralysed hero (bonus_vs). He drops the Bloomleaf Cloak, identified, and only that (item_chance 0). He has no cut of his own: a harvest borrows the nearest humanoid's of his depth (food_system._nearest_prime).

sk_zombie_bang_chan.name: Zombie Bang Chan

attacks.name: Four A.M. Demo Song
attacks.quip: It is forty minutes long, he wants notes, and you doze off halfway.

attacks.name: Encouraging Shoulder Slap
attacks.quip: You feel strangely motivated. Also hit.

sk_zombie_bang_chan.lore: Bang Chan was the leader of Stray Kids and the band's main producer, and more than a hundred of their songs were his work. For years he held livestreams that he called Chan's Room, and through all those years the fans begged him to go to bed. Death has not altered his habits in the least. He still has not slept, he has one more idea for the bridge, and he would dearly love your honest opinion of it this very minute, though it be four in the morning.
sk_zombie_bang_chan.kill_chronicle: Zombie Bang Chan lay down at last, to sleep.

sk_zombie_lee_know.name: Zombie Lee Know

attacks.name: Cat-Scratch Handoff
attacks.quip: Strictly speaking, the cat did that. He looks very proud of the cat.

attacks.name: Dance-Teacher Correction
attacks.quip: "Left foot. LEFT." You are no longer sure which one that is.

sk_zombie_lee_know.lore: Before ever he joined Stray Kids, Lee Know toured as a backup dancer for BTS, and he became the main dancer of his band. He has three cats, named Soonie, Doongie and Dori, and has never pretended to like anyone better than them. Death could take away his pulse but it could not take his cat, so that he will dance against you only when the cat has no need of him, and it has need of him nearly always.
sk_zombie_lee_know.kill_chronicle: Zombie Lee Know went down. His cat walked off.

sk_zombie_changbin.name: Zombie Changbin

attacks.name: Dumbbell Curl
attacks.quip: Arm day. Today, arm day is you.

attacks.name: Surprise Aegyo Charm
attacks.quip: A cute face, from the scariest face in the dungeon. It is too much. You just stare.

sk_zombie_changbin.lore: Changbin was one of the three of 3RACHA, who produced the band's songs, and as a rapper he once went by the name of SpearB. Upon the stage he goes in black from head to foot like a villain, and his leisure he spends at the gym, but off it he is renowned as one of the gentlest of the eight, and no one has believed in his villainy for a moment. Even in death he cannot play the part for long before he forgets himself and makes a cute face.
sk_zombie_changbin.kill_chronicle: Zombie Changbin fell, dumbbell first, making a cute face.

sk_zombie_hyunjin.name: Zombie Hyunjin

attacks.name: Hair Flip
attacks.quip: A curtain of long black hair whips across your eyes. Some of it is grave-dirt.

attacks.name: Whistle Song
attacks.quip: It is the catchiest tune you have ever heard, and now it lives in your head.

sk_zombie_hyunjin.lore: There was none in all the band so given to drama as Hyunjin, who was both dancer and painter. He brought long hair back into fashion among the idols, painted so well that Hugh Jackman praised him in public, and whistled upon many of the band's songs. He has held to all three customs as a zombie, though his hair flips are worse than they were, for there is now much of the graveyard in them.
sk_zombie_hyunjin.kill_chronicle: Zombie Hyunjin fell with one last hair flip.

sk_zombie_han.name: Zombie Han

attacks.name: Speed-Rap Song
attacks.quip: Two hundred words a second. You catch one "yeah", and your head spins.

attacks.name: Snack-Cheek Spray
attacks.quip: Crumbs. He has sprayed you with crumbs.

sk_zombie_han.lore: The third of 3RACHA was Han, a rapper and maker of songs who was counted among the swiftest rappers in Korea. The fans named him the quokka for the round cheeks that he loves to stuff with snacks. Being dead he has no more need to draw breath, and so he raps faster than ever, and no one on Earth has yet caught more than one word in four of all that he says.
sk_zombie_han.kill_chronicle: Zombie Han finished his very fast verse, then fell.

sk_zombie_felix.name: Zombie Felix

attacks.name: Black-Belt Roundhouse
attacks.quip: A perfect, textbook kick. It barely registers. He is very smol.

attacks.name: Unexpectedly Deep Roar
attacks.quip: From that tiny body comes a voice like a cave troll's. You freeze in shock.

sk_zombie_felix.lore: Two things that seem ill matched won fame for the dancer Felix: a voice so deep that it rattles the floor, and a small and sunny face full of freckles. He studied taekwondo for twelve years and earned a black belt and, by report, sixty-three medals, yet he is, alas, so smol that a roundhouse kick from that black belt lands like a moth against a lamp. He bakes brownies for his fellows besides, and it is wiser not to ask what goes into those that he has baked since he died.
sk_zombie_felix.kill_chronicle: Zombie Felix fell smiling, after one black-belt kick caught me.

sk_zombie_seungmin.name: Zombie Seungmin

attacks.name: Brutally Honest Whisper
attacks.quip: He says something devastating about your outfit. Your confidence shrinks, and so do your swings.

sk_zombie_seungmin.lore: As a boy Seungmin, the main vocalist of the band, longed to be a baseball player and pitched with his right hand, and in 2024 his hour came, when he threw the first pitch at a Team Korea game against the LA Dodgers. The fans call him the puppy, and he repays them with the most cutting jests in all the band. Though he is dead he pitches still, and while he pitches he will roast you without mercy.
sk_zombie_seungmin.kill_chronicle: Zombie Seungmin fell out of his last spin, faulting my outfit.

sk_zombie_i_n.name: Zombie I.N

attacks.name: Trot Song
attacks.quip: A wobbly old-fashioned ballad, the kind grandmothers love. It will not leave your head.

attacks.name: Braces Smile
attacks.quip: A dazzling smile full of braces catches the stage lights.

sk_zombie_i_n.lore: I.N is the youngest of the eight, whom the custom of K-pop bands names the maknae, and therefore the other seven will treat him as their baby until the end of time. He began as a little boy singing trot, an old-fashioned kind of Korean song, at church, and it may be heard in him still. Even in death he is the baby, and the others are forever stepping in front of him, to his very great embarrassment.
sk_zombie_i_n.kill_chronicle: Zombie I.N went down. The others had tried to shield him as they danced.

little_john.name: Little John
little_john.lore: Seven feet tall was John Little, who met Robin Hood upon a narrow bridge and would not give way to him, but knocked him into the brook with a quarterstaff. In jest the men of Robin named him Little John, and he was Robin's right hand ever afterward. When Robin lay dying at Kirklees and blew three weak blasts upon his horn, it was Little John who heard them and came to him.

will_scarlet.name: Will Scarlet
will_scarlet.lore: Will Scarlet, whom the oldest ballads name also Scarlok or Scathelock, was the swift and hot-tempered swordsman of the band, the first to fall upon the Sheriff's men and the first to laugh when the fight was over. It was he who brought Robin word of a friar at Fountains Abbey who could beat Little John.

friar_tuck.name: Friar Tuck
friar_tuck.lore: It was the curtal friar of Fountains Abbey who bore Robin Hood across a river and cast him down in the midst of it. Robin blew his horn for his yeomen, and the friar whistled for his dogs, but at length they made peace and the friar joined the band. He is a big and merry man of God who fights with sword and buckler, and he has never yet refused his supper.

much_the_millers_son.name: Much the Miller's Son
much_the_millers_son.lore: Even in the oldest ballads of all, Much, the miller's son, is among the men of Robin Hood, a young yeoman small and strong, who follows Little John wherever he goes and will never run from a fight.

alan_a_dale.name: Alan-a-Dale
alan_a_dale.lore: Alan-a-Dale was a minstrel who went in sorrow, for his sweetheart was to be wedded against her will to an old knight, until Robin Hood stayed the wedding at the church door and saw the right pair married. Thereafter Alan joined the band and sang for it, and he can use a bow as skilfully as a harp.

yeoman_archer.name: yeoman archer
yeoman_archer.lore: Clad in Lincoln green, each yeoman of Robin Hood bears a longbow as tall as himself. The ballads tell that when Robin winds his horn they come out of the greenwood by the dozen, and that their arrows do not miss.

king_arthur.name: King Arthur
king_arthur.lore: Arthur, the once and future king, lies asleep beneath the hill at Sewingshields in Northumberland, as the folk there say, with his queen, his knights and his hounds, until someone shall draw the sword, cut the garter and blow the bugle that lie upon the table by the door. Then he will rise up to fight, and the sword in his hand is Excalibur.

sir_lancelot.name: Sir Lancelot
sir_lancelot.lore: The Lady of the Lake fostered Sir Lancelot du Lac, and he became, as the French romances tell, the greatest knight of the Round Table and the best in every fight into which he rode.

sir_gawain.name: Sir Gawain
sir_gawain.lore: Upon a red shield Sir Gawain, the nephew of Arthur, bore the pentangle in gold. In the old romances his strength waxed with every hour from morning until noon, and when he had pledged his word to the Green Knight he was faithful to that appointment.

sir_percival.name: Sir Percival
sir_percival.lore: From the Welsh woods Sir Percival came to Arthur's court, a boy who had never seen a knight. He slew the Red Knight and took his red armour, and so rode forth to find the Grail.

sir_bedivere.name: Sir Bedivere
sir_bedivere.lore: Sir Bedivere is found at Arthur's side in the oldest Welsh tales, one-handed and none the slower for it. He stayed until the very end, the last of the knights beside the king, and it was he who cast Excalibur back into the lake.

sir_kay.name: Sir Kay
sir_kay.lore: Arthur had for foster-brother and steward Sir Kay, to whom the romances give a sharp tongue. Yet in the old Welsh tales he could go nine days and nights without sleep, and he could stand as tall as the tallest tree in the forest whenever he chose.

einherjar.name: Einherjar
einherjar.lore: When warriors fall in battle the valkyries of Odin choose the bravest, and these become the einherjar, the chosen dead of Valhalla. Every morning they arm and cut one another down in the yard, and at evening they rise whole and sit down to feast, until Heimdall shall blow Gjallarhorn. Then they will ride out by the five hundred and forty doors of that hall, eight hundred through each, to the last battle.

charlemagne.name: Charlemagne
charlemagne.lore: Charles the Great, the white-bearded emperor of the Franks, bore the sword Joyeuse. At Roncevaux he heard the horn of Roland thirty leagues off, and though he turned his army too late to save the rear guard, he avenged it upon the Saracens of Spain.

duke_naimes.name: Duke Naimes
duke_naimes.lore: Wisest of all the counsellors of Charlemagne was Duke Naimes. When the Olifant sounded and Ganelon made light of it, Naimes told the emperor truly that Roland was in battle, and that he who said otherwise had betrayed him.

ogier_the_dane.name: Ogier the Dane
ogier_the_dane.lore: After Roncevaux, Ogier the Dane, who was one of Charlemagne's great barons, led a column against the emir Baligant. The later legends say that he sleeps beneath the castle of Kronborg, waiting for the day when Denmark shall have need of him.

frankish_knight.name: Frankish knight
frankish_knight.lore: In mail, with lance and long shield, the knights of the Franks rode back to Roncevaux in Charlemagne's host, as the Song of Roland tells, and came too late. They found the rear guard dead, and they did not draw rein until they had driven the Saracens into the Ebro.

hraesvelg_eagle.name: Corpse-Swallower
hraesvelg_eagle.lore: Vafthrudnir told Odin, in their contest of wisdom, of the giant Hraesvelgr, the Corpse-Swallower, who sits in an eagle's shape at the end of heaven, and from whose wings comes every wind that blows over men. Snorri set him at the northern edge of the sky, and the great eagles of the rime halls are his brood. When they stoop it is as though a gale had grown talons, and upon the wind of their wings is borne the cold of the world's end.

rime_thurs.name: Rime-Thurs
rime_thurs.lore: Where the rime of the venomous rivers Elivagar met the warm air out of Muspell there grew, as Snorri tells, the first giant Ymir, and from him the rime-thurses are descended. When Odin and his brothers slew him his blood drowned all that race save Bergelmir, who escaped in a boat with his wife and fathered the old giants anew. A rime-thurs is of that oldest blood, elder than the frost giants of the jarls' halls, and it is foretold in the Voluspa that at Ragnarok Hrym shall lead them out of the east.

kallikantzaros.name: Kallikantzaros
kallikantzaros.lore: Through the twelve days of Christmas the villages of Greece keep the hearth burning, for those are the days when the kallikantzaroi come up. All the rest of the year they labour beneath the earth, sawing at the World Tree that upholds it. Each winter they have all but cut it through when they leave the work to climb up and make mischief, and while they are gone the tree heals. They are small and shaggy and black with soot, with red eyes and long nails. They have a great fear of fire, and holy water at Epiphany drives them all below again, but the winter of the rime halls has no end, and so their season of mischief has none.

oni.name: Oni
oni.lore: Horned and fanged, red or blue of skin, the oni are the jailers in the Buddhist hells of Japan, who go clad in loincloths of tiger skin and bear the iron club called the kanabo, and they punish the dead as King Enma sentences them. Some of them came up into the world, and the band of Shuten-doji on Mount Oe raided the capital until Minamoto no Raiko and his four retainers came among them in the guise of mountain monks, gave them drugged sake, and took the chief's head while he slept. On Setsubun every house still casts roasted beans out at the door to keep such creatures away, crying, 'Oni out, luck in!'

mushmahhu.name: Mushmahhu
mushmahhu.lore: For her war upon the younger gods Tiamat made eleven monsters with venom for blood, and third among them, as the Enuma Elish numbers them, was the Exalted Serpent, the mushmahhu. In older hymns of the Sumerians the god Ninurta is praised for capturing a serpent with seven heads and hanging it upon his chariot as a trophy. Its seven heads strike from seven sides, and a blade that bites deep is drawn back smoking with its blood.

kyubi_kitsune.name: Nine-Tailed Fox
kyubi_kitsune.lore: A thousand years a fox must live before it has nine tails and may take any shape it likes. Such a one, in the Japanese tale, became Tamamo-no-Mae, the loveliest and cleverest lady at the court of Emperor Toba, until the emperor fell sick and the court diviner Abe no Yasunari declared what she was. She fled, and an army hunted her down upon the plain of Nasu, where her spirit passed into a boulder that poisoned whatever touched it and was named the Killing Stone. Later tellers gave her earlier lives, as that of Daji, who ruined the last king of the Shang, and since the Killing Stone split in two in 2022 it is said that she is free again.

geryon.name: Geryon
geryon.lore: Virgil summoned Geryon out of the pit at the edge of the seventh circle, and Dante watched him come, with the face of a just man, kind and open, upon the body of a serpent painted all over with knots and wheels, two hairy paws, and a forked sting at the tip of his tail. Dante named him the filthy image of fraud, and he bore the two poets down through the dark to the ditches where cheats are punished. The Greeks had told of a Geryon also, a giant of three bodies whose red cattle Heracles took, and the poet kept his name but gave him a face so honest that it was itself a lie.

viy.name: Viy
viy.lore: Gogol wrote that the imagination of the common people had created a colossal being named Viy, the chief of the gnomes, whose eyelids hang down to the ground. His tale tells how the dead witch called him into the church on the third night, a squat thing caked in black earth, with a face of iron and arms and legs like roots. 'Lift my eyelids,' he said, and his servants lifted them. The student Khoma Brut had been warned not to look, but he looked, and he died of fright. Those lids are heavy and slow to lift, so that there is a moment before Viy sees you, and a mirror or a blindfold is the answer to him, for you must never meet his eyes.

image_of_the_beast.name: Image of the Beast
image_of_the_beast.lore: It is written in Revelation 13 that John saw a second beast come up out of the earth and bid the people make an image of the first beast, and give breath to that image, so that the image should both speak and cause all who would not worship it to be killed. Such images stand yet in the lowest halls, golden and speaking, and their voice is a command, so that a hero who will not bow is struck down by the word. Wax in the ears will keep the command out, and since the image is but a made thing, a hammer will unmake it.

polyphemus.name: Polyphemus
polyphemus.lore: On the island of the Cyclopes Polyphemus, a son of Poseidon, pastured his flocks, and he would roll before the mouth of his cave a stone that twenty-two wagons could not have moved. There he shut in Odysseus and his men and ate them two at a time, until Odysseus gave him strong wine and said that his name was Nobody, and while the giant slept drove into his one eye a stake cut from his own club of green olive wood, which was as long as the mast of a ship. Blinded, he flung a hilltop after the ship as it fled. Now he has his sight again, and of all the faces of those men he has not forgotten a single one.
polyphemus.omen: Sheep are bleating somewhere on this floor, and the air smells of wet fleece and new cheese.
polyphemus.kill_chronicle: Killed Cyclops Polyphemus, no wine needed. Kept clear of his club.

jackal.name: jackal
jackal.lore: Because they saw jackals nosing at the borders of their graves in the desert, the Egyptians made jackals the guardians of the dead: Anubis, who weighs the heart, and Wepwawet, who is called the Opener of the Ways. In the Indian fables of the Panchatantra the jackal is ever the trickster, who wins by his wit and never by his strength. Golden jackals hunt in pairs and small families, and not one of them will stand and fight, for each darts in to snap and is gone again before the blow can fall, while its mate comes in from the other side.

wolf.name: wolf
wolf.lore: By the strength of the pack the grey wolf runs down deer and elk, for the swiftest hold the eyes of the quarry while the rest close upon its flanks and go for the legs. It was a she-wolf, the story goes, that suckled the twins who founded Rome, and Norse warriors named their sons for wolves. Those of the dungeon are the same lean grey hunters, and no passage will deceive them: they will not file down a corridor onto a sword one at a time, but wait in the open until their prey comes to them.

cave_hyena.name: cave hyena
cave_hyena.lore: When William Buckland crept into Kirkdale Cave in Yorkshire in the year 1821, he found the floor strewn with the gnawed bones of elephants, rhinoceroses and hippopotamuses, and from the marks of teeth and the droppings he read what had befallen. For thousands of years the cave had been a den of hyenas, and they had dragged their kills within. The cave hyena of the Ice Age was bigger and heavier than the spotted hyena of Africa, its jaws cracked the bones of woolly rhinos, and its clans would run horses down for miles. Here below the breed has never died out, and a clan will hang back from strong prey, whooping to the rest, but closes in upon anything that bleeds.

mandrake.name: Mandrake
mandrake.lore: Theophrastus tells that the cutters of roots drew circles about a mandrake with a sword before they dug, and the herbals of later days add that it screams when it is torn from the earth, and that its cry kills all who hear. The wise would therefore tie a hungry dog to the root and walk away holding meat. Physicians boiled the forked root in wine, that a patient might sleep before the knife. Down here the roots have drawn themselves up on legs of their own, and they scream still when they die.

death_throes.line: The Mandrake shrieks as it dies, a cry that goes through stone!
death_throes.warn_line: A thin keening rises from the Mandrake's split root.

kappa.name: Kappa
kappa.lore: Children in the villages of Japan were kept from deep pools for fear of the kappa, a little water-imp with a beak and a shell and a dish of water set into the crown of its head. It drags swimmers and horses under and challenges travellers to wrestle, but it is exceedingly courteous. If you bow to a kappa it must bow in return, and as the water spills from its dish its strength drains away with it. Farmers floated cucumbers down the rivers to keep it friendly, and a kappa that is given a gift of food will leave the giver alone.

on_stunned.line: The water spills from the Kappa's dish, and its arms go slack.

appeased_by.line: The Kappa takes your offering, bows low, and goes back to its pool.

eloko.name: Eloko
eloko.lore: The Mongo people of the Congo forest tell of the biloko, small and hungry spirits that dwell in hollow trees, having grass for hair and leaves for raiment, and mouths that open wide enough to swallow a man's head. Each carries a little bell, and so sweet is its chime that a hunter forgets whither he was going and walks toward it, until he cannot move at all. Hunters in that forest wore charms to hide themselves, but a hunter in these depths must stop his ears against the bell.

asanbosam.name: Asanbosam
asanbosam.lore: High in the trees of the Ghanaian forest lived the sasabonsam that Akan hunters feared, long of leg, with teeth of iron, long matted hair, and feet that point both ways. It loved best to sit upon a high branch dangling its legs, that it might snare a hunter who walked beneath and haul him up among the leaves. Enslaved Akan people carried the tale across the sea, and in 1774 Edward Long set it down in Jamaica. Down here it hangs from the roof beams and the roots of the old halls, and nothing but a light will show it to you.

ahuizotl.name: Ahuizotl
ahuizotl.lore: Sahagun learned from his Aztec informants of the ahuizotl of the lakes, a sleek little water beast like a dog, which had the hands of a monkey and one hand more at the very end of its tail. When it had not fed it would cry like a child upon the shore, or make the fish leap to draw the fishermen close, and then the hand on its tail seized them and dragged them under. Days afterward the drowned were found, and none but a priest dared touch them.

khalkotauros.name: Khalkotauros
khalkotauros.lore: For Aeetes, the king of Colchis, Hephaestus forged two bulls of bronze with brazen hooves and mouths that breathed fire, and the king set Jason to yoke them and plough the field of Ares in a single day. Medea gave the hero an ointment that kept fire and bronze from his skin for that one day, and so he forced them to their knees. But the pairs that stamp through these halls have never in all their days submitted to a yoke.

cu_sith.name: Cu-Sith
cu_sith.lore: As big as a yearling bullock was the cu-sith, the hound of the fairies, so the Highlanders said, dark green and shaggy, with paws as broad as a man's hand and a long tail plaited flat upon its back. It hunted in silence, but when it chose it would bark three times with long pauses between. Whoever heard the first bark ran for a house and barred the door, for terror overtook all who were still in the open at the third. There are no houses in these depths, yet any wall will serve as well, and stone between you and the hound is shelter enough.

lines: The Cu-Sith barks once, and the sound rolls through the halls.
The Cu-Sith barks a second time. Get out of its sight!
The Cu-Sith barks the third time!
unseen: Somewhere out of sight a great hound barks once, slow and deep.
The hound barks a second time, nearer.
The hound barks a third time!
countdown_voice.safe_line: Stone stands between you and the Cu-Sith, and it falls silent.

bulgasari.name: Bulgasari
bulgasari.lore: A monk who lay in prison in the last days of Goryeo, so the storytellers of Korea relate, shaped a little beast out of grains of rice and gave it life. It ate the needle that he fed to it, and thereafter every needle, spoon, ploughshare and spear in the land, growing with each meal until no iron blade could wound it. Its name was read as 'the one that cannot be killed', yet the tellers say that fire was its end. Those that dwell here below are growing still upon whatever iron they find.

metal_eater.line: The Bulgasari's hide closes on your {weapon} and gnaws it.

vetala.name: Vetala
vetala.lore: It was laid upon King Vikramaditya, in the Twenty-Five Tales of the Vetala, to bear a corpse down from a tree in a cremation ground, and within it rode a vetala, which is a spirit that lives in the bodies of the dead. Upon the road it would tell a story that ended in a riddle, and each time the king answered, it laughed and flew back to its tree. Down here it has no need of a tree, for when one body falls it slips into the nearest dead one and rises up again.

corpse_hop.line: The Vetala laughs as its body falls, and the corpse nearby sits up.
corpse_hop.unseen: Somewhere close a high voice laughs, and a dead thing stirs.

nahual.name: Nahual
nahual.lore: Among the Nahua a sorcerer who could put on the shape of a beast was called nahualli. The informants of Sahagun said that such a man went abroad by night as a jaguar, a dog or a turkey to bring sickness and ill luck upon his neighbours, and came home a man before the dawn, and Hernando Ruiz de Alarcon heard the spells by which they called upon Tezcatlipoca for the change. If the sorcerer is wounded sorely enough, the jaguar will come forth out of him.
nahual.enrage_message: The Nahual's eyes go yellow, and he drops into a hunter's crouch.

enraged_form.line: Spots spread over the sorcerer's skin, and a jaguar drops to all fours!

likho.name: Likho
likho.lore: Russian peasants took great care never to waken Likho, the one-eyed hag of ill luck. Yet a blacksmith and a tailor went in search of her out of curiosity, in the tale that Afanasyev wrote down, and she devoured the tailor. The smith escaped only by burning out her single eye with a hot awl and creeping forth among her sheep beneath a sheepskin. When Likho leaps upon a man's neck, every plan that he makes thereafter goes wrong.

centaur.name: Centaur
centaur.lore: Men to the waist and horses below, the centaurs are named by Homer the beast-men of the mountains. At the wedding of the Lapith king Pirithous they drank the wine and would have carried off the bride, and so began the battle of which Ovid tells every blow, fought with tables, antlers and torches. In Dante's Hell they gallop with bent bows along the river of boiling blood, and one of that people is the archer of the zodiac. They shoot at the gallop, and whatever their arrows cannot hit they ride down beneath their hooves.

blue_men_of_the_minch.name: Blue Man of the Minch
blue_men_of_the_minch.lore: Between the Isle of Lewis and the Shiant Isles runs the Stream of the Blue Men, where men blue of skin and grey of face swim beside the boats and raise sudden gales. Their chief calls out two lines of verse to the captain, and if he answers in rhyme, quick and well, he may sail on, but if he stumbles he is sunk. In these drowned halls they ask the same of every traveller who would pass them by.

parley.subject: grammar
parley.call: The Blue Men rise to the waist and their chief calls out two lines of verse. Answer him well and they let you pass.
parley.right: The chief of the Blue Men laughs at your answer, and they sink back into the dark water, content to let you be.
parley.wrong: At your stumbling answer the Blue Men howl, and the squall comes down on you!
parley.unasked: The Blue Men watch you from the water, waiting for an answer.

vila.name: Vila
vila.lore: The vila of the Serbian epic songs is a fairy of the mountains and the clouds, robed in white and long of hair, who shoots with arrows and raises whirlwinds. Once the hero Milos sang upon the mountain of the vila Ravijojla, and his singing so angered her that she shot him, nor would she heal him until Prince Marko rode her down. Whoever steals a vila's hair or her girdle may command her service, but none has yet stolen anything from those who dwell down here.

myrmekes.name: Gold-Digging Ant
myrmekes.lore: Herodotus learned from the Persians that in the deserts of northern India there were ants, smaller than dogs but bigger than foxes, which cast up sand full of gold as they dug. The Indians came for the gold at midday, when the heat had driven the ants below, and they filled their sacks and rode away at once, for the ants follow a thief by scent and run faster than any beast. Scholars of our own day believe that the tale began with the marmots of the Himalaya, but those that dig in these depths are no marmots.

gold_gatherer.line: The Gold-Digging Ant stops to gather up the gold.

ponaturi.name: Ponaturi
ponaturi.lore: Beneath the sea lies the country of the Ponaturi, a hostile people of whom the Maori tell, who came ashore by night to sleep in their great house, Manawa-tane. They killed the father of Tawhaki and kept his mother to watch the door, and so Tawhaki and his mother stopped every chink of that house, that the Ponaturi might sleep on into the morning. Then mother and son threw wide the door, and the sunlight slew the sleepers where they lay.

taniwha.name: Taniwha
taniwha.lore: Many of the taniwha of the Maori are guardians of a river or a tribe, yet some there were that ate people. Such was Tutaeporoporo of the Whanganui River, who swallowed travellers and whole canoes, until the warrior Ao-kehu hid in a hollow log and let himself be swallowed in it, and cut his way out from within. Such also was Ngarara Huarau, which was lured from its cave and burned. Those that lie in these flooded deeps are guardians of nothing but themselves.

impundulu.name: Impundulu
impundulu.lore: The Zulu and the Xhosa hold that the impundulu, the lightning bird, strikes the earth as lightning. It is black and white and as tall as a man, a witch's servant that is handed down from mother to daughter, and it hungers for blood. Neither spears nor guns can harm it, nor can it be drowned or poisoned, yet fire will destroy it, and its fat, if it is dug from the place where the lightning struck, makes a powerful medicine.

mapinguari.name: Mapinguari
mapinguari.lore: Tall and shaggy is the mapinguari of which the rubber-tappers and the peoples of the Amazon speak, a beast with one eye, with feet turned backward and with a mouth in its belly. Before it rolls a stench like rot and dung that leaves hunters dizzy and sick, and its hide will turn arrows and knives everywhere except at the navel. The biologist David Oren has wondered whether the tales preserve a memory of the giant ground sloths that lived in that land at the end of the Ice Age.

aura.line: The reek of the Mapinguari turns your stomach.

mapinguari.weak_spot_line: Your blow finds the soft place at the Mapinguari's navel!

preta.name: Preta
preta.lore: A belly like a drum and a throat as thin as a needle are the lot of the preta, the hungry ghost of which Buddhists and Hindus tell. It is a spirit of greed that nothing it eats can fill, and in its mouth all food turns to fire. The monk Maudgalyayana, in the Ullambana story, found his own mother among these spirits. From of old a preta has been eased by offerings of food freely given, and so every year at the Ghost Festival a meal is set out for them.

appeased_by.line: The Preta falls on your offering, and for a while its hunger is quiet.

upas_tree.name: Upas Tree
upas_tree.lore: The London Magazine printed in 1783 a Dutch surgeon's tale of the upas tree of Java, whose poison killed every living thing for fifteen miles about, so that condemned criminals were sent to fetch its sap and few came back. The tale was a tall one, but the tree is real, and its milky latex is the ipoh poison with which island hunters tipped their blowgun darts. The upas trees of the deep need no tall tale to make them deadly.

aura.line: The air round the Upas Tree burns in your throat.

nuckelavee.name: Nuckelavee
nuckelavee.lore: Orkney islanders would not speak the name of the nuckelavee, which came out of the sea like a horse and rider grown into one body, and had no skin, so that the black blood could be seen running in its veins. Its breath withered the crops and brought upon the cattle the plague called mortasheen. An old man named Tammas told Walter Traill Dennison how it pursued him along the shore one night, and how he saved himself by leaping a burn of fresh water, where on that night it would not follow him.

star_jelly.name: Star Jelly
star_jelly.lore: After a night of falling stars the shepherds of Wales would find upon the grass a pale and trembling jelly that melted away within days, and they called it pwdre ser, the rot of the stars. Medieval physicians spread it upon sores, and naturalists today lay the blame on frog spawn or a swollen alga of the soil. The jelly that drops from the roofs in these depths has no such homely birth, and it shrinks away from any light.

psoglav.name: Psoglav
psoglav.lore: Villagers of Bosnia, Montenegro and Serbia told of the psoglavci, the dog-heads, who are men with the legs of horses and the heads of dogs, with teeth of iron and a single eye in the middle of the forehead. They live in caves in a land without sun, where precious stones give light in the darkness. With their one eye they see but poorly, yet their noses miss nothing, and they dig the dead out of their graves to eat them.

waq_waq_tree.name: Waq-Waq Tree
waq_waq_tree.lore: On the island of Waq-waq at the edge of the world, as the wonder-books of Arabs and Persians relate, there grows a tree whose fruit has the shape of people, and when it is ripe it falls, crying 'waq, waq!'. In later paintings its branches end in the heads of men and beasts, all calling at once. Such a tree, standing in the dark, cries out at anything that moves, and then everything near at hand comes to the sound of its crying.

alarm.line: Every head on the Waq-Waq Tree cries out at once: 'Waq! Waq!'
alarm.line_unseen: Somewhere ahead, a chorus of voices cries 'Waq! Waq!'

yuki_onna.name: Yuki-Onna
yuki_onna.lore: Two woodcutters took shelter in a hut from a blizzard, in the tale that Lafcadio Hearn wrote down, and there a woman in white breathed upon the old man until he froze. The snow woman spared the young one, whose name was Minokichi, and had his promise never to tell of it. Years afterward he told the story to his wife, and his wife was the snow woman herself, yet for their children's sake she did not kill him, but melted away into the mist and was gone.

yacumama.name: Yacumama

attacks.name: Drawing Breath
attacks.pull_line: The Yacumama breathes in, and the air drags you toward its coils!

yacumama.lore: Mother of the waters is the meaning of yacumama, and by that name the peoples of the Peruvian Amazon speak of an anaconda fifty yards long that lies in the deep pools where a river rises. The Nuttall Encyclopaedia of 1907 says that it draws in any creature within a hundred yards, as if the river itself were breathing in. Therefore the fishermen blew upon a conch before they waded, that the yacumama might show itself if it lay there.

tsuchigumo.name: Tsuchigumo
tsuchigumo.lore: While the warrior Minamoto no Raiko lay sick of a fever that no medicine could break, as the Heike tells, there came by night to his bedside a strange monk, taller than any man, who sought to bind him with rope. Raiko slashed at him with his sword, and the next day his men followed a trail of blood to a mound behind the Kitano Shrine and found a great earth spider lying there. In the picture scroll of the Tsuchigumo another was cut open, and one thousand nine hundred and ninety skulls rolled out of its belly.

bhuta_vahana_yanta.name: Relic Guardian
bhuta_vahana_yanta.lore: King Ajatashatru laid the relics of the Buddha in a deep chamber, as the Pali Lokapannatti tells, and set over them machines driven by spirits, the bhuta vahana yanta, that were built from plans brought out of the land of the Romans. None could pass those guardians until, long afterward, the emperor Ashoka learned their secret and stilled them. The machines of these depths still keep their watch, and there is never an hour when their swords cease from turning.

reem.name: Re'em
reem.lore: The re'em of the Hebrew Bible is a wild ox of terrible strength, which the translators of King James called the unicorn, and Job was asked whether it would ever serve him or harrow his valleys. The rabbis held it too great for Noah's ark and puzzled over the manner of its saving. A midrash tells how David in his youth climbed a sleeping re'em, thinking it a hill, and was borne up toward the sky upon its horns when it woke, but the re'em of the deep halls are awake already.

eitr.name: Eitr
eitr.lore: Poisonous rivers, the Elivagar, flowed in the beginning from the wellspring in Niflheim, as Snorri tells, and their venom, which is named eitr, hardened like slag from a furnace and spread as rime through the void. Where that rime met the heat of Muspell the first giant, Ymir, was born, but some part of the eitr never hardened. It crawls yet in the deepest cold, and whatever it touches is frozen and sickened at the same moment.

bakunawa.name: Bakunawa
bakunawa.lore: Seven moons were hung in the sky by the god Bathala, so the Visayan peoples of the Philippines say, until the sea serpent Bakunawa rose up and swallowed six. An eclipse comes whenever it rises for Bulan, the last moon, and then the people run out of doors and beat upon pots and gongs and drums until the noise drives it to spit the moon out again. The bakunawa coiled in these deeps will swallow any light that it sees.
